- [ ] **Step 8: README**

In `README.md` (a new subsection right before `### Dynamic storage-integrity table set`, base `:109`, after the subsections Plans S3-C1–S3-C4 put there), replace:

```markdown
### Dynamic storage-integrity table set
```

with:

````markdown
### Storage-integrity owner rebuild and settle (stage 3 P4)

When an SI owner's source ClickHouse is lost (pod, PVC and PV) but its host keeps its own volume, the owner is rebuilt under the same identity and signer key (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16 P4): the host's SNode journal survives, and `rebuild-safe` restores `hg_safe` on the re-created ClickHouse to the arbiter's acknowledged inventory before the SNode starts. The production chart runs it as the host pod's init container `si-rebuild-safe` (`storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe`), with the host's own config:

```bash
/sentio-node --config-path <config> storage-integrity rebuild-safe --backup <name> [--dry-run]
```

It runs through arbiter-core's `snode/rebuild` in four phases and refuses before the first unless the arbiter lists this indexer as quarantined and none of its issued promotions is unacknowledged (settle them first, below): `fence` (for every table the indexer owns, its SNode node id's replica under the table's Keeper path must be absent or inactive and is then dropped with `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA ... FROM ZKPATH`; the scoped root `/sentio/<shard>/unsafe_inc` must have no child), `tables` (every owned table is created; the new `hg_unsafe` replica clones from the network verifiers), `restore` (each `hg_safe` partition is restored through the restore gate to the arbiter's `SafeParts`, every part from the own `hg_unsafe` replica when it still holds it by `hash_of_all_files`, else from the named backup in `storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url` under `owner-<id>/`, each part's `hash_of_all_files` equal to the arbiter's, the partition closing over its base root) and `journal` (the restored inventories are recorded in the SNode journal, marked rebuilt, at the arbiter's publish sequence, so the owner audit takes them as its reference until the next promotion). A second run changes nothing. `--dry-run` plans every partition and its sources and writes nothing; it fails, naming the part, when no source holds a part, and it is the only form that may run beside a live SNode.

The command needs an indexer config (`node.node_type: indexer` and `PRIVATE_KEY`) with `storage_integrity.enabled`, no genesis tables (`storage_integrity.snode.table_ids` empty: genesis schemas are host configuration that the arbiter's registry does not carry), `storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url` (and `owner_indexer_id`, when set, equal to this indexer's id) and `--backup`, the backup taken after the quarantine and the settle. It reads this indexer's id from `IndexerRegistry.getIndexerBySigner` (read-only; it never registers an indexer, and a new key would be a new indexer) and checks it against the arbiter's `si_indexers` entry: its `snode_node_id` must be `storage_integrity.snode.node_id` and its signer the key's address. It logs in to ClickHouse as the SNode does (`storage_integrity.clickhouse_username`, the password from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`; the user needs `READ ON S3` for the restore) and takes the read-only restore key only from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. The registry read gives up after two minutes, each partition-state and promotion-outcome read after five. stdout carries one JSON object per line and nothing else, each with a `phase`: one `fence` line per owned table, one `restore` (or, for a dry run, `plan`) line per partition, and a final `done` line with the totals; it is written only when the run succeeds. Logs go to stderr and never carry a key or a password.

A quarantined track's issued promotions whose acknowledgements were lost are settled by the leader (`arbiter-admin indexer settle`, arbiter `ARBITER_TAG_P4`): it streams them, marked `settle`, only to an SNode whose subscription advertised settle support, which this release's embedded SNode does; the SNode answers each from its journal only and never applies it. `sentio_node_storage_integrity_settle_answers_total{outcome}` on the embedded HouseGate's metrics endpoint counts the answers: `journaled` (its stored acknowledgement sent again), `reconciled` (a published intent finished), `not_applied` (a journaled `Applied:false` acknowledgement, which consumes the promotion) and `unanswerable` (at or below the watermark with no stored acknowledgement; nothing sent), every outcome exported from zero.

### Dynamic storage-integrity table set
````

```bash
Stage 3 P4 of the multi-source storage-integrity network, the host side of the settle and of the same-identity owner rebuild (housegate spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` §14 "Exits from the release refusals", §16 P4; Plan S3-D Task 52, contract §35.6, clarifications K51–K54).

- Pins arbiter-core `@CORE_TAG_P4@` (the SNode advertises `SNodeHello.settle` and answers a settle-streamed promotion from its journal only; `snode/rebuild`: Keeper fence, tables, restore through the gate, rebuilt journal inventories) in go.mod, bazel_dep and git_override, and arbiter-proto `@PROTO_TAG_P4@` in go.mod; housegate stays `@HG_TAG_P3@`.
- `sentio-node storage-integrity rebuild-safe --backup <name> [--dry-run]`: the init container of a host whose source ClickHouse was re-created runs it before the SNode starts. It reads the indexer id read-only (`IndexerRegistry.getIndexerBySigner`, never `EnsureRegistered`: the signer key is kept, K51), checks the arbiter's `si_indexers` entry against `storage_integrity.snode`, reads the registry once and each owned table's `GetPartitionStates` and unacknowledged `GetPromotionOutcomes` (each read bounded), opens the named backup of `storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url` with the restore key from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, runs `rebuild.Rebuild` as the SNode's ClickHouse user and prints `Report.JSONLines()`; the library refuses a live track and unacknowledged promotions. An indexer with genesis tables is refused.
- `sentio_node_storage_integrity_settle_answers_total{outcome}` (`journaled`, `reconciled`, `not_applied`, `unanswerable`, always exported) from `(*snode.Role).SettleStats` on the embedded HouseGate registry.
- CI: a new `integration-clickhouse` step runs `TestRebuildSafeDryRunReportsCoverageWithoutWriting` (the real dry run against the CI ClickHouse with Keeper); the acceptance step's filter and count are unchanged.

Nothing changes until it is used: `rebuild-safe` runs only when invoked, the settle series reads zero until a leader on arbiter `ARBITER_TAG_P4` settles a track, and no signer key, consensus format or config default changes.
```

Contract §36.1–§36.5, clarifications K52 and K55–K57 and decision D39 (spec §14 "Network hardening (P4, before k is raised)", §9.3, §16 P4): before devnet2 can harden its SI network and rebuild indexer-c's source ClickHouse, production must be able to render every P4 change as a reviewed value and check it in tests. This task adds, to `charts/storage-integrity`, `clickhouse.interserver` (the three `interserver_http_credentials/*` settings, the password only through the operator's `valueFrom` from one shared Secret), `clickhouse.nodePins` (one pod template `clickhouse-<cluster>` per pinned cluster) and `clickhouse.access.snodeRestoreGrant` (`GRANT READ ON S3` as `si_snode`'s last grant); to `charts/sentio-node`, `storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe` (the init container `si-rebuild-safe` that runs Task 52's `sentio-node storage-integrity rebuild-safe` before every other container, with the SNode's login, the indexer key and the host's read-only restore key, and `storage_integrity.backup` from Plan S3-C1's `siBackup` values in its config); the three SI ClickHouse ingress policies and the shared Keeper's `clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress`, both in observe mode; the probe matrix `si_network_probe.tsv`; the interserver staging pair (generated from indexer-b's CHI); the user's `make-interserver-secret.sh`; the devnet2 network overlay's P4 values, all off (the one interserver Secret named with `enabled: false`, no node pin, `snodeRestoreGrant: false`), so each later live step flips one value; the rollout mirrors (interserver step 0 everywhere, only indexer-c pinned, every policy observing, no restore grant, no rebuild) with the live placement read read-only in Step 3; and the render tests that judge every later live commit of Tasks 55 and 56, including decision D39's placement rule over `DEVNET2_SI_ELIGIBLE_NODES`, with the earlier plans' comparisons taught to ignore exactly P4's per-installation moves. No deployed object changes on merge: every new chart value is unset or renders today's objects, the overlay's new values are all off and render nothing, no CHI manifest is edited (Tasks 55 and 56 add their settings in their own commits), the policy files and the staging example are applied only by hand (Task 55), and Step 24 proves that every release renders byte-identically. Decisions fixed by this task (recorded in Appendix B):

- **D53-1. The init container also takes `PRIVATE_KEY`.** Contract §36.2 lists the init container's environment as the SNode password and the restore key, but `rebuild-safe` resolves its indexer id with `IndexerRegistry.getIndexerBySigner` (contract §35.6), and sentio-node's `config.LoadConfig` loads the signer from `PRIVATE_KEY` for an indexer config and fails without it (`sentio-node:config/config.go:652-658` at `origin/main`). `si-rebuild-safe` therefore takes `PRIVATE_KEY` from `privateKeySecret` (key `private-key`), the same Secret reference the `sentio-node` container has; the key is never read, copied or printed by anyone (K51), only handed to the container as the pod already hands it to the node.
- **D53-2. `storage_integrity.backup` comes from Plan S3-C1's `siBackup` values.** `rebuild-safe` refuses a config without `storage_integrity.backup` (contract §35.6), and a host's `standalone.yaml` carries none (Plan S3-C1 renders it only into the backup job's ConfigMap). While `rebuildSafe` is on, `standalone.yaml` gains `storage_integrity.backup` as its last key, with `bucket_url` and `owner_indexer_id` from the release's own `siBackup.bucketURL` and `siBackup.ownerIndexerID` (and `max_chain_links` from `siBackup.maxChainLinks` when set, so the block has Plan S3-C1's shape), which Task 52 checks against its own id; a guard refuses `rebuildSafe` without them. The block exists only while the drill has `rebuildSafe` on, so the SNode never reads it otherwise; contract §36.2's values gain no bucket of their own.
- **D53-3. A host with genesis tables is refused by the chart.** Task 52 refuses an indexer whose `storage_integrity.snode.table_ids` is set (genesis schemas live on the lost ClickHouse); the chart refuses `rebuildSafe` with a non-empty `storageIntegrity.snode.tableIDs` too, so indexer-a's release can never render an init container that would fail its pod.
- **D53-4. The host rule selects components, not the whole release.** Contract §36.3's flow is "9000 and 8123 from pods of the installation's host release (… host pod, si-member, backup job, the rebuild init container)"; every pod of a `charts/sentio-node` release carries `app.kubernetes.io/instance: <release>`, the DinD pod (tenant driver and processor code) and Redis included. The rule therefore selects `app.kubernetes.io/instance: <release>` and `app.kubernetes.io/component In [node, si-backup, si-member]` (`SI_HOST_CLIENT_COMPONENTS`), and the probe matrix refuses `dind` (S3-B K17: no DinD session ever reached an SI ClickHouse). The network's release rule selects `app.kubernetes.io/component In [bootstrap, verifier]` for the same reason (its voters and DA never dial ClickHouse). `test_si_network_policies_admit_exactly_the_reviewed_flows` renders every host release and requires the host pod, the si-member and the backup job's pod template, and nothing else, to match.
- **D53-5. The kubelet's probes are an explicit rule.** The Altinity operator gives each ClickHouse container `httpGet /ping` probes on 8123, which come from the node itself; whether Cilium admits the local host without a rule depends on its `allow-localhost` setting, which nothing in production pins. Each SI policy therefore admits `fromEntities: [host]` on 8123 only; no pod can probe it, so the runbook checks instead that every pod stays Ready after enforce.
- **D53-6. Three flows have no probe row.** The contract's alias set has no operator or vmagent pod, so the operator's 8123, vmagent's 9363 and the kubelet's 8123 are `SI_NETWORK_UNPROBED_FLOWS`, each with the evidence the hardening runbook takes instead (the census, the scrape targets, pod readiness); every other allowed flow has an open row and every policy has refused rows.
- **D53-7. The grant probe rows take Plan S3-C1's `s3()` form.** Measured on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3` (26.3.51.7) in a container without network, as a user with `si_snode`'s grants and its two engine grants: the contract's `SELECT * FROM s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/p4', 'CSV', 'a String') LIMIT 0` answers code 36 (`Bucket name length is out of bounds in virtual hosted style S3 URI: 'p4'`) before the access check, with the grant and without it, so it cannot tell the grant; Plan S3-C1's `SELECT * FROM s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/probe.json', 'k', 's', 'RawBLOB') SETTINGS s3_retry_attempts = 0` answers 497 without `READ ON S3` and 499 (after the access check) with it, and the matching `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(…) SETTINGS async_insert = 0, s3_retry_attempts = 0 VALUES ('{}')` answers 497 either way (`WRITE ON S3`), so the restore grant is read-only. Plan S3-C1's `probe_atoms` already reads both forms, so the corpus carries them as `si_snode ok` and `si_snode denied`. A direct check that returns rows instead of an error (the owner-rebuild runbook's §4.1, Task 54) can use `SELECT * FROM s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/si-p4-probe/p4.csv', 'CSV', 'a String') LIMIT 0`: measured the same way, it returns no rows with the grant and 497 without it.
- **D53-8. The staging pair is born locked and names the one interserver Secret.** Task 54's runbook applies the committed example with only the three `interserver_http_credentials/*` keys added from `SI_INTERSERVER_SECRET` (its §4 runs before §3.1) and logs in as `default` with Plan S3-B's staging logins. Plan S3-B's lockdown runbook deleted that Secret (its §11), so the user makes it again in Step 2 with `make-clickhouse-logins.sh staging` into a new hashes file, and Step 22 generates the example from indexer-b's CHI and those hashes (`p4_staging_document`): indexer-b as Plans S3-B and S3-C1 left it (Plan S3-C3's server bundle, engine grants and `si_member` removed with `without_p2_chi`: its 100 GiB `keep_free_space_bytes` would refuse every insert on 1Gi volumes, and its named collections name live installations), posture C with the network's user set, no reader environment (no staging pod names a live installation or holds a live password), 1Gi volumes, the staging Keeper root, no interserver setting and no pin. The test compares the file with the generator's output, so P4's own moves on indexer-b and Plan S3-C3's P2 stages leave it valid and any other change to indexer-b makes it stale.
- **D53-9. The placement is read once, here, and judged by D39 as the rollout moves.** Step 3 reads the six SI ClickHouses' nodes (pod and local-path volume, which must agree) and the eligible nodes read-only, and Step 18 fills them in (`DEVNET2_CLICKHOUSE_NODES`, `DEVNET2_SI_ELIGIBLE_NODES`, never edited afterwards). `test_si_clickhouses_run_on_distinct_nodes` always requires at least four eligible nodes, every effective node eligible, the three sources pairwise distinct and an eligible node that holds no source; a verifier ClickHouse is judged (never on a source's node, on its own node when devnet2 has at least six eligible nodes) once it is pinned, and every verifier once the network CHI is at interserver step 1, because a conflict the read finds is resolved live by hardening runbook §5.0 after this PR merges. `test_devnet2_node_pins_follow_the_rollout` lets a pin differ from the read node only for a verifier the read placement put in conflict, never for a source, and requires every cluster of an installation at step 1 pinned.
- **D53-10. Earlier comparisons drop exactly P4's per-installation moves.** P4 moves one installation at a time (an interserver step, a pin, the restore grant), so every earlier comparison of a CHI with the network chart or with indexer-b drops exactly these three things on both sides (`p4_neutral`, `p4_neutral_chi`) and the new rollout tests check each installation's own values: Plan S3-B's two source-profile tests and its lockdown staging test, Plan S3-C1's `test_p1_staging_chi_mirrors_indexer_b` and Plan S3-C3's `test_p2_staging_chi_mirrors_indexer_b_with_the_bundle`. Plan S3-C3's helpers learn the two P4 shapes they meet: `clickhouse_container` reads the default pod template (a pinned installation has more than one), and `without_p2_users`, `p2_chi`, `_p2_strip_manifest_lines`, `p2_manifest_text` and `test_engine_grants_follow_the_census_constants` keep `si_snode`'s restore grant its last grant, as Plan S3-C4 keeps `si_gateway`'s replica grant (`_snode_restore_lines` reads only `si_snode`'s block, since `si_member` holds `GRANT READ ON S3` too). The control plane's Secret set gains the interserver Secret from the network's step 1 on, and `host_logout()` drops `rebuildSafe` too, so Plan S3-B's login tests hold while the drill has it on; Plan S3-C1's `test_backup_job_never_changes_the_host_pod` drops `rebuildSafe` with `siBackup` (the job alone must never touch the host pod, while `rebuildSafe` puts `siBackup`'s bucket into the host config by design), and Plans S3-C3 and S3-C4's `test_si_member_password_and_status_token_come_only_from_their_own_secrets` leaves the `si-rebuild-safe` init container out of the host pod it searches (it takes the same read-only restore key as the si-member, by design; the retained upstream adaptations address both; the complete Task56 live-editor replay remains its separate gate).
- **D53-11. Operator inputs are tokens filled by a local tool.** The constants that depend on the live read and the ledger are written with `__…__` tokens (`__SN_COMMIT_P4__`, `__SN_DIGEST_P4__`, the five `__NODE_…__` and `"__DEVNET2_SI_ELIGIBLE_NODES__"`) and `fill-p4.py` replaces them from `placement.json` and the environment; it refuses a malformed value and any token left, and the tests refuse an unfilled node name.
- **D53-12. The workflow's paths gain what the tests read outside its globs.** The policy file and the probe matrix are under `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/**` and `charts/storage-integrity/**` already; both triggers gain `docs/examples/storage-integrity-p4-interserver-staging-chi.yaml`, `k8s-sea/clickhouse/network-policy.yaml` and `k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse-extra-keeper.yaml` (read by `test_keeper_ingress_policy_keeps_the_raft_peers`).
- **D53-13. The network overlay carries P4's values, all off.** `storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml` gains `clickhouse.access.snodeRestoreGrant: false`, `clickhouse.interserver: {enabled: false, allowEmpty: true, secret: {name: storage-integrity-si-v2-interserver}}` (the comment above it names hardening §5.3 and §6.3) and `clickhouse.nodePins: {}`, which render nothing, so each live commit of Tasks 55 and 56 flips one value or fills the map; `test_devnet2_interserver_follows_the_rollout` requires exactly that shape at every step (the shape Task 55's `p4-edit.py overlay-interserver` checks before it edits), and `test_snode_restore_grant_follows_the_rollout` requires the explicit `snodeRestoreGrant` line.
- **D53-14. The P4 host image is every kind of reviewed host image.** The hosts move to `DEVNET2_STAGE3_P4_SOURCE_IMAGE` with `writerAuthorization`, `ownerAudit` and Plan S3-C4's `replicaReads` on, and Plan S3-C4 requires every replica-read host image to be a reviewed stage-3 host, member and writer-authorization image as well (`REPLICA_READ_HOST_IMAGES <= STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES & MEMBER_IMAGES & set(WRITER_AUTHORIZATION_IMAGES)`), so the image joins all four sets in this PR, before any pin moves, and is the one image of `REBUILD_SAFE_IMAGES`; `siMember.image` stays whatever Plan S3-C3's rollout set.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Plan S3-D Task 53 Step 3: judge the read-only placement read and write placement.json (local tool, never committed).

usage: preflight-p4.py PREFLIGHT_DIR WORKTREE

PREFLIGHT_DIR holds the kubectl reads of Step 3; WORKTREE is the production
worktree (its test_render.py gives Plan S3-B's DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES and
INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE). Prints the placement and exits 1 on any stop condition.
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

out, worktree = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
sys.path.insert(0, str(worktree / "charts/storage-integrity/tests"))
import test_render as t  # noqa: E402

CLICKHOUSES = {
    "storage-integrity-si-v2/source": ("storage-integrity-si-v2", "source", "storage-integrity-si-v2-source-0-0-0"),
    "storage-integrity-si-v2/verifier-1": ("storage-integrity-si-v2", "verifier-1", "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-1-0-0-0"),
    "storage-integrity-si-v2/verifier-2": ("storage-integrity-si-v2", "verifier-2", "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-2-0-0-0"),
    "storage-integrity-si-v2/verifier-3": ("storage-integrity-si-v2", "verifier-3", "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-3-0-0-0"),
    "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b/source": ("storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b", "source", "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source-0-0-0"),
    "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c/source": ("storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c", "source", "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source-0-0-0"),
}
stops = []


def load(name):
    return json.loads((out / name).read_text())["items"]


def running(pod):
    return pod["status"].get("phase") == "Running" and not pod["metadata"].get("deletionTimestamp")


pods = {pod["metadata"]["name"]: pod for pod in load("pods-devnet2.json")}
eligible = sorted(line.strip() for line in (out / "eligible-nodes.txt").read_text().splitlines() if line.strip())
pv_nodes = {}
for pv in load("pvs.json"):
    claim = pv["spec"].get("claimRef") or {}
    if claim.get("namespace") != t.LEGACY_NAMESPACE:
        continue
    terms = (((pv["spec"].get("nodeAffinity") or {}).get("required") or {}).get("nodeSelectorTerms")) or []
    nodes = sorted({value for term in terms for expression in term.get("matchExpressions", [])
                    if expression.get("key") == "kubernetes.io/hostname" for value in expression.get("values", [])})
    pv_nodes[claim["name"]] = nodes

placement = {}
print(f"eligible nodes (sentio.xyz/general=true): {len(eligible)}: {' '.join(eligible)}")
for key, (chi, cluster, name) in CLICKHOUSES.items():
    pod = pods.get(name)
    if pod is None or not running(pod):
        stops.append(f"{name} is not a Running pod")
        continue
    labels = pod["metadata"].get("labels") or {}
    if (labels.get("clickhouse.altinity.com/chi"), labels.get("clickhouse.altinity.com/cluster")) != (chi, cluster):
        stops.append(f"{name} carries chi/cluster labels {labels.get('clickhouse.altinity.com/chi')}/{labels.get('clickhouse.altinity.com/cluster')}")
    if pod["spec"].get("hostNetwork"):
        stops.append(f"{name} uses hostNetwork: a CiliumNetworkPolicy cannot select it")
    node = pod["spec"].get("nodeName") or ""
    volumes = pv_nodes.get(f"data-volume-claim-{name}")
    if volumes != [node]:
        stops.append(f"{name} runs on {node!r} but its data volume is pinned to {volumes}")
    placement[key] = {"pod": name, "node": node, "volume_nodes": volumes or []}
    print(f"{key:44} {name:52} node {node:12} volume {','.join(volumes or ['?'])}")

if len(placement) == len(CLICKHOUSES):
    nodes = {tuple(key.split("/")): entry["node"] for key, entry in placement.items()}
    for key, node in nodes.items():
        if node not in eligible:
            stops.append(f"{'/'.join(key)} runs on {node}, which is not labelled sentio.xyz/general=true")
    if nodes[("storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c", "source")] != t.INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE:
        stops.append(f"indexer-c's ClickHouse runs on {nodes[('storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c', 'source')]}, not INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE {t.INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE}")
    others = {node for key, node in nodes.items() if key[0] != "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c"}
    if not others <= t.DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES:
        stops.append(f"{sorted(others - t.DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES)} are not among Plan S3-B's DEVNET2_SOURCE_NODES: the placement moved since indexer-c's preflight")
    sources = [node for key, node in nodes.items() if key[1] == "source"]
    if len(set(sources)) != 3:
        stops.append(f"two source ClickHouses share a node ({sources}): stop and amend the plan (D39)")
    if len(eligible) < 4:
        stops.append("devnet2 has fewer than four eligible nodes: no placement keeps every verifier off every source (D39); stop")
    verifiers = {key: node for key, node in nodes.items() if key[1] != "source"}
    for key, node in sorted(verifiers.items()):
        why = []
        if node in sources:
            why.append("on a source's node")
        if len(eligible) >= 6 and list(verifiers.values()).count(node) > 1:
            why.append("beside another verifier while devnet2 has at least six eligible nodes")
        print(f"verifier {key[1]} on {node}: " + ("D39 conflict, " + " and ".join(why) + " (hardening runbook §5.0 moves it)" if why else "no D39 conflict"))
    free = [node for node in eligible if node not in set(nodes.values())]
    print(f"eligible nodes holding no SI ClickHouse: {' '.join(free) or 'none'}")

operators = [pod for pod in load("operator-pods.json") if running(pod)]
if len(operators) != 1:
    stops.append(f"expected one Running devnet2-operator pod with app.kubernetes.io/name=altinity-clickhouse-operator, found {len(operators)}")
vmagents = [pod for pod in load("vmagent-pods.json") if running(pod)]
if not vmagents or any(pod["spec"].get("hostNetwork") for pod in vmagents):
    stops.append("no Running vmagent pod in namespace monitoring, or one on hostNetwork (the 9363 rule selects the namespace's pods)")
keepers = [pod for pod in load("keeper-pods.json") if running(pod)]
if len(keepers) != 3 or any(pod["spec"].get("hostNetwork") for pod in keepers):
    stops.append(f"expected three Running clickhouse-keeper-extra pods off hostNetwork, found {len(keepers)}")
extra = [pod for pod in load("extra-pods.json") if running(pod)]
if not extra:
    stops.append("no Running clickhouse-extra pod (alias extra-ch)")
for alias, selector in (("dind", ("sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a", "dind")), ("observer", ("sentio-node-devnet2-observer", "node"))):
    found = [pod for pod in pods.values() if running(pod) and (
        (pod["metadata"].get("labels") or {}).get("app.kubernetes.io/instance"),
        (pod["metadata"].get("labels") or {}).get("app.kubernetes.io/component")) == selector]
    if not found:
        stops.append(f"no Running pod for probe alias {alias} ({selector})")
if not [line for line in (out / "toolbox-pods.txt").read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]:
    stops.append("no toolbox pod in namespace default (alias toolbox)")
print(f"operator {len(operators)}, vmagent {len(vmagents)}, keeper {len(keepers)}, clickhouse-extra {len(extra)} Running pods")

(out / "placement.json").write_text(json.dumps({
    "read_at": (out / "read-at.txt").read_text().strip(),
    "eligible_nodes": eligible,
    "clickhouse": placement,
}, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
for stop in stops:
    print(f"STOP {stop}")
sys.exit(1 if stops else 0)
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fill Plan S3-D Task 53's operator inputs into test_render.py (local tool, never committed).

usage: fill-p4.py PLACEMENT_JSON TEST_RENDER_PY

PLACEMENT_JSON is the read-only preflight of Task 53 Step 3. The environment
holds SN_COMMIT_P4 and SN_DIGEST_P4 as s3-ledger.py get printed them. Every
token below that the file holds is replaced; afterwards none may remain.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

placement_path, target_path = (Path(arg) for arg in sys.argv[1:3])
placement = json.loads(placement_path.read_text())
sn_commit, sn_digest = os.environ.get("SN_COMMIT_P4", ""), os.environ.get("SN_DIGEST_P4", "")
if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", sn_commit) or not re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", sn_digest):
    sys.exit("fill-p4: SN_COMMIT_P4 must be 40 hex and SN_DIGEST_P4 sha256:<64 hex> (from s3-ledger.py get)")
nodes = {key: entry["node"] for key, entry in placement["clickhouse"].items()}
eligible = sorted(placement["eligible_nodes"])
node_name = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?")
for node in [*nodes.values(), *eligible]:
    if not node_name.fullmatch(node):
        sys.exit(f"fill-p4: {node!r} is not a node name")
tokens = {
    "__SN_COMMIT_P4__": sn_commit,
    "__SN_DIGEST_P4__": sn_digest,
    "__NODE_NETWORK_SOURCE__": nodes["storage-integrity-si-v2/source"],
    "__NODE_NETWORK_VERIFIER_1__": nodes["storage-integrity-si-v2/verifier-1"],
    "__NODE_NETWORK_VERIFIER_2__": nodes["storage-integrity-si-v2/verifier-2"],
    "__NODE_NETWORK_VERIFIER_3__": nodes["storage-integrity-si-v2/verifier-3"],
    "__NODE_INDEXER_B_SOURCE__": nodes["storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b/source"],
    '"__DEVNET2_SI_ELIGIBLE_NODES__"': ", ".join(json.dumps(node) for node in eligible),
}
text = target_path.read_text()
filled = []
for token, value in tokens.items():
    if token in text:
        text = text.replace(token, value)
        filled.append(token.strip('"'))
left = sorted(set(re.findall(r"__(?:SN_COMMIT_P4|SN_DIGEST_P4|NODE_[A-Z0-9_]+|DEVNET2_SI_ELIGIBLE_NODES)__", text)))
if left:
    sys.exit(f"fill-p4: tokens left unfilled: {left}")
target_path.write_text(text)
print("fill-p4: filled " + (", ".join(filled) if filled else "nothing (no token present)"))
```

```python
# Stage 3 P4 network hardening (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14; Plan S3-D
# K55-K57; docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md). Every SI
# ClickHouse installation of devnet2-si-v2 presents and asks for one
# interserver credential, kept only in this Secret (key password), which the
# user's scripts/storage-integrity/make-interserver-secret.sh creates.
SI_INTERSERVER_SECRET = "storage-integrity-si-v2-interserver"
SI_INTERSERVER_USER = "si_interserver"
# si_snode's restore grant (Plan S3-D K52; clickhouse.access.snodeRestoreGrant
# and the CHI manifests' grant line): si_snode's last grant, after its engine
# grants (Plan S3-C3), once the owner-rebuild runbook (§4.1) turns it on for an
# installation.
SI_SNODE_RESTORE_GRANT = "GRANT READ ON S3"
```

```python
def interserver_settings(secret, allow_empty, user=SI_INTERSERVER_USER):
    """The three CHI settings of interserver credentials (Plan S3-D K56): the
    password only as a valueFrom reference, which the operator renders as
    from_env with the Secret in the pod environment."""
    return {
        "interserver_http_credentials/user": user,
        "interserver_http_credentials/password": {"valueFrom": {"secretKeyRef": {"name": secret, "key": "password"}}},
        "interserver_http_credentials/allow_empty": "true" if allow_empty else "false",
    }


def interserver_step_settings(step, secret=SI_INTERSERVER_SECRET):
    """An installation's interserver settings at one rollout step: 0 none, 1
    credentials with allow_empty true, 2 credentials with allow_empty false."""
    if step not in (0, 1, 2):
        raise ValueError(f"unknown interserver step {step!r}")
    return {} if step == 0 else interserver_settings(secret, step == 1)


def interserver_values(step, secret=SI_INTERSERVER_SECRET):
    """storage-integrity values of one interserver step (step 0 leaves it off)."""
    return {"clickhouse": {"interserver": {
        "enabled": step != 0, "user": SI_INTERSERVER_USER, "allowEmpty": step != 2,
        "secret": {"name": secret if step else "", "key": "password"},
    }}}


def without_interserver(settings):
    """CHI settings without the interserver credential keys."""
    return {key: value for key, value in settings.items() if not key.startswith("interserver_http_credentials/")}


def with_snode_restore_grant(users, enabled):
    """A users block with SI_SNODE_RESTORE_GRANT appended as si_snode's last grant when enabled."""
    users = copy.deepcopy(users)
    if enabled:
        users["si_snode/grants/query"] = list(users["si_snode/grants/query"]) + [SI_SNODE_RESTORE_GRANT]
    return users


def without_snode_restore_grant(users):
    """A users block without si_snode's restore grant (Plan S3-D K52)."""
    users = copy.deepcopy(users)
    if "si_snode/grants/query" in users:
        users["si_snode/grants/query"] = [grant for grant in users["si_snode/grants/query"] if grant != SI_SNODE_RESTORE_GRANT]
    return users


def p4_neutral(spec):
    """A CHI spec without what the P4 hardening rollout changes on a live
    installation one commit at a time (Plan S3-D K55, K56): the interserver
    settings, the per-cluster pod template names, the pinned pod templates and
    each remaining pod template's kubernetes.io/hostname node selector.
    Comparisons of a staging or fixed CHI with a live one go through it."""
    spec = copy.deepcopy(spec)
    configuration = spec["configuration"]
    configuration["settings"] = without_interserver(configuration["settings"])
    for cluster in configuration.get("clusters", []):
        cluster.pop("templates", None)
    pods = spec["templates"]["podTemplates"]
    default = spec["defaults"]["templates"]["podTemplate"]
    spec["templates"]["podTemplates"] = [pod for pod in pods if pod["name"] == default]
    for pod in spec["templates"]["podTemplates"]:
        selector = pod["spec"].get("nodeSelector")
        if selector is not None:
            selector.pop("kubernetes.io/hostname", None)
            if not selector:
                del pod["spec"]["nodeSelector"]
    return spec


def p4_neutral_chi(chi):
    """A CHI through p4_neutral, and its si_snode grants without the restore
    grant: the by-role comparisons of installations at different P4 steps."""
    chi = copy.deepcopy(chi)
    chi["spec"] = p4_neutral(chi["spec"])
    chi["spec"]["configuration"]["users"] = without_snode_restore_grant(chi["spec"]["configuration"]["users"])
    return chi
```

```python
class NetworkHardeningChartTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Stage 3 P4 network hardening in charts/storage-integrity (housegate spec
    2026-10-14 §14; Plan S3-D K52, K55, K56): interserver credentials from one
    shared Secret, per-cluster node pins and si_snode's restore grant."""

    @classmethod

        cls.pinned_base = documents(render({"nodeSelector": {"sentio.xyz/general": "true"}}))

    def assert_rejected(self, overrides, error, *, legacy=False):
        result = render_legacy(overrides) if legacy else render(overrides)
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
        self.assertIn(error, result.stderr)

        spec = self.installation(self.docs)
        configuration = spec["configuration"]
        self.assertEqual(without_interserver(configuration["settings"]), configuration["settings"])
        self.assertTrue(all("templates" not in cluster for cluster in configuration["clusters"]))
        self.assertEqual([pod["name"] for pod in spec["templates"]["podTemplates"]], ["clickhouse"])
        self.assertNotIn("interserver_http_credentials", self.result.stdout)
        self.assertNotIn(SI_SNODE_RESTORE_GRANT, render(clickhouse_access("C")).stdout)

            "enabled": False, "user": SI_INTERSERVER_USER, "allowEmpty": True, "secret": {"name": "", "key": "password"},
        })
        self.assertEqual(defaults["nodePins"], {})
        self.assertIs(defaults["access"]["snodeRestoreGrant"], False)
        # Every new value set to its default renders exactly what leaving it unset does.
        explicit = {"clickhouse": {"interserver": defaults["interserver"], "nodePins": {}}}
        self.assertEqual(render(explicit).stdout, self.result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(render(interserver_values(0)).stdout, self.result.stdout)
        for posture in ("B", "C"):
            with self.subTest(posture=posture):
                values = clickhouse_access(posture)
                values["clickhouse"]["access"]["snodeRestoreGrant"] = False
                self.assertEqual(render(values).stdout, render(clickhouse_access(posture)).stdout)

                # Settings restart the installation's pods; nothing else of it or of the release changes.

                self.assertEqual(secret_references(docs[("ClickHouseInstallation", "storage-integrity")]), {SI_INTERSERVER_SECRET})
        # The user is the chart's choice unless set; the Secret key too.

        self.assertEqual(settings["interserver_http_credentials/password"],
                         {"valueFrom": {"secretKeyRef": {"name": SI_INTERSERVER_SECRET, "key": "next"}}})
        self.assertEqual(settings["interserver_http_credentials/allow_empty"], "true")

    def test_snode_restore_grant_appends_read_on_s3(self):

        plain = self.installation(documents(render(member)))["configuration"]["users"]
        granted = self.installation(documents(render(merge_values(
            member, {"clickhouse": {"access": {"snodeRestoreGrant": True}}}))))["configuration"]["users"]
        self.assertTrue(plain["si_snode/grants/query"][-1].startswith("GRANT TABLE ENGINE ON "))
        self.assertEqual(granted, with_snode_restore_grant(plain, True))
        self.assertEqual(without_snode_restore_grant(granted), plain)
        self.assert_rejected({"clickhouse": {"access": {"snodeRestoreGrant": True}}},
                             "clickhouse.access.snodeRestoreGrant requires clickhouse.access.users")
        self.assert_rejected({"clickhouse": {"access": {"snodeRestoreGrant": "true"}}}, "snodeRestoreGrant")
```

`charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv` (one comment line before the header row, and the two rows right before the first `default` cleanup row, `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS hg_unsafe.si_grant_probe`):

**Phase-sensitive corpus and rollback boundary.** The added `si_snode ok` row is an access-boundary probe: the inherited generic oracle calls a non497 outcome `ok`; the historically measured result for this exact RawBLOB shape is499 after admission, not a successful S3 read. It cannot prove object-store availability, restore success or correct credentials, and arbitrary non497 errors are not independent proof that the intended access check ran. Task54's direct check is the two-segment CSV `LIMIT 0` form and must actually exit0. No ClickHouse measurement was repeated in this review. The TSV's 'every earlier run skips them' sentence is an operator phase rule, not implemented filtering: inherited lockdown/P1/P2 helpers still read every si_snode row. After this PR merges, do not claim an unmodified earlier helper automatically skips these rows or that it passes before the restore grant. Stop such a rerun until a separately reviewed explicit filter/wrapper selects the intended phase; Task54 owns documenting that boundary. The current Task53–56 mandatory path does not invoke those full-corpus readers: Task54's audited120 Bash blocks and11-runbook helper chain have no reachable generic corpus helper; Task55's conservative all-token-root graph and Task56's equivalent transitive audit likewise have no reachable corpus helper. `si_p4_roll` performs its own direct engine refusal, `si_p4_window_check` reaches only `si_p2_stage_check` metadata queries, and the rollback helper does not execute the corpus. Thus no mandatory P4 step waits for a future filter; the limitation is an additional earlier-runbook rerun outside this task's mandatory path. The same restriction applies after a restore-grant rollback: the new positive row should then be denied, so an unfiltered legacy rerun is not an acceptance oracle. Do not drop the rows, invent a skip result, enable a grant just to fit a test or use a historical pre-P4 run as post-P4 proof. Rebuild must be off before its required restore grant is removed.


```diff
diff --git a/charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv b/charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv
--- a/charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv
+++ b/charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv
@@ -11,2 +11,3 @@
 # Measured on clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3 (26.3.51.7) with the bundle: every refusal of a table engine names TABLE ENGINE ON <engine> and comes before ClickHouse touches Keeper; CREATE DATABASE ... ENGINE = Replicated is checked as TABLE ENGINE ON Replicated; a temporary table needs TABLE ENGINE ON Memory, remote(), s3() and BACKUP do not; CREATE TABLE ... AS needs SHOW COLUMNS on the source and its engine; ClickHouse grants CREATE VIEW with CREATE TABLE, so si_member's plain view and materialized view over hg_rstage are accepted (Plan S3-C2 contract §23.2), while a dictionary, dictGet, a definer, SQL SECURITY NONE and SYSTEM are refused.
+# Stage 3 P4 (Plan S3-D K52): the two s3() rows of si_snode above the cleanup need clickhouse.access.snodeRestoreGrant (a CHI manifest's GRANT READ ON S3 line): docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-owner-rebuild.md §4.1 runs them on each installation once its restore grant is on, and every earlier run skips them. They take the form of Plan S3-C1's rows; measured on clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3 (26.3.51.7): without the grant the read answers 497, with it 499 (after the access check), and the write 497 either way (WRITE ON S3). A one-segment URL such as http://127.0.0.1:1/p4 answers 36 (bucket name too short) before the access check, for every user.
 role	expect	statement
@@ -257,2 +258,4 @@
 si_member	override	SELECT count() FROM remote(si_owner_staging, password = 'p2-probe', database = 'hg_safe', table = 'si_grant_probe')
+si_snode	ok	SELECT * FROM s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/probe.json', 'k', 's', 'RawBLOB') SETTINGS s3_retry_attempts = 0
+si_snode	denied	INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/probe.json', 'k', 's', 'RawBLOB') SETTINGS async_insert = 0, s3_retry_attempts = 0 VALUES ('{}')
```

```python
    REBUILD_SAFE_TEST_BACKUP = "20261020T041700Z-full"

    @staticmethod
    def rebuild_safe(name, backup=REBUILD_SAFE_TEST_BACKUP, **changes):
        """storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe of a host release as the owner-rebuild runbook turns it on (§5.7)."""
        rebuild = {"enabled": True, "backup": backup, "restoreKeySecret": {"name": DEVNET2_SI_RESTORE_SECRETS[name]}}
        rebuild.update(changes)
        return {"storageIntegrity": {"snode": {"rebuildSafe": rebuild}}}

    @staticmethod
    def without_rebuild_safe():
        """A host release without rebuildSafe, whatever its overlay sets (the key has no chart default, so null removes it)."""
        return {"storageIntegrity": {"snode": {"rebuildSafe": None}}}

    def rebuildable_hosts(self):
        """The SI host releases rebuild-safe can rebuild: those without genesis
        tables (storageIntegrity.snode.tableIDs empty, Plan S3-D Task 52)."""
        return {
            name: release for name, release in self.host_releases().items()
            if not release_chart_values(FRESH_HELMFILE, self.releases[(LEGACY_NAMESPACE, name)], name)[0]["storageIntegrity"]["snode"].get("tableIDs")
        }

    def si_backup_of(self, name):
        """The siBackup values (Plan S3-C1) a host release merges, which name the object store a rebuild reads."""
        helmfile_release = self.releases[(LEGACY_NAMESPACE, name)]
        values, _ = release_chart_values(FRESH_HELMFILE, helmfile_release, name)
        return values.get("siBackup") or {}

    @staticmethod
    def host_pod(docs, name):
        """The host StatefulSet's pod template of one sentio-node release."""
        return docs[("StatefulSet", name)]["spec"]["template"]

    def test_unset_rebuild_safe_renders_unchanged(self):
        # rebuildSafe is only a comment in charts/sentio-node/values.yaml: no
        # release that leaves it unset renders the init container, a restore
        # key in its host pod or storage_integrity.backup, and its
        # checksum/config is unchanged.
        self.assertNotIn("rebuildSafe", yaml.safe_load((SENTIO_NODE_CHART / "values.yaml").read_text())["storageIntegrity"]["snode"])
        checksum = re.compile(r"^(\s+checksum/config: )[0-9a-f]{64}$", re.M)
        for name, release in self.host_releases().items():
            with self.subTest(release=name):
                plain = self.render_with(release, self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name), self.without_rebuild_safe())
                docs = documents(plain)
                spec = self.host_pod(docs, name)["spec"]
                self.assertNotIn("si-rebuild-safe", [container["name"] for container in spec.get("initContainers", [])])
                self.assertNotIn("STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_", json.dumps(spec))
                self.assertNotIn("backup", host_config(docs)["storage_integrity"])
                # enabled: false renders the same objects but still moves the
                # checksum (the key is part of storageIntegrity): the runbook
                # removes the block after the rebuild instead.
                off = self.render_with(release, self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name), self.rebuild_safe(name, enabled=False))
                self.assertEqual(off.returncode, 0, off.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(checksum.sub(r"\1-", off.stdout), checksum.sub(r"\1-", plain.stdout))
                self.assertNotEqual(checksum.search(off.stdout).group(0), checksum.search(plain.stdout).group(0))

    def test_rebuild_safe_runs_before_the_node_container_with_the_snode_login(self):
        self.assertEqual(sorted(self.rebuildable_hosts()), ["sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b", "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c"])
        for name, release in self.rebuildable_hosts().items():
            with self.subTest(release=name):
                login = documents(self.render_with(release, self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name), self.without_rebuild_safe()))
                docs = documents(self.render_with(release, self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name), self.rebuild_safe(name)))
                pod = self.host_pod(docs, name)
                node = next(container for container in pod["spec"]["containers"] if container["name"] == "sentio-node")
                rebuild = pod["spec"]["initContainers"][0]
                self.assertEqual(rebuild["name"], "si-rebuild-safe")
                self.assertEqual((rebuild["image"], rebuild["imagePullPolicy"]), (node["image"], node["imagePullPolicy"]))
                self.assertEqual(rebuild["command"], ["/sentio-node"])
                self.assertEqual(rebuild["args"], [
                    "storage-integrity", "rebuild-safe", "--config-path", "/config/standalone.yaml",
                    "--backup", self.REBUILD_SAFE_TEST_BACKUP,
                ])
                # The node's own key (the indexer id, read only) and SNode login,
                # and the host's read-only restore key: Secret references only.
                node_env = {item["name"]: item for item in node["env"]}
                restore = DEVNET2_SI_RESTORE_SECRETS[name]
                self.assertEqual(rebuild["env"], [
                    node_env["PRIVATE_KEY"],
                    node_env["STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD"],
                    {"name": "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "valueFrom": {"secretKeyRef": {"name": restore, "key": "access-id"}}},
                    {"name": "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", "valueFrom": {"secretKeyRef": {"name": restore, "key": "secret"}}},
                ])
                self.assertEqual(node_env["STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD"]["valueFrom"]["secretKeyRef"],
                                 {"name": f"{name}-clickhouse", "key": "snode-password"})
                # The node container's config and data, read-write data: it writes the SNode journal.
                self.assertEqual(rebuild["volumeMounts"], [
                    {"name": "config", "mountPath": "/config", "readOnly": True},
                    {"name": "data", "mountPath": "/data"},
                ])
                self.assertNotIn("resources", rebuild)
                # The rest of the pod is the login render's, checksum/config aside.
                expected = copy.deepcopy(self.host_pod(login, name))
                got = copy.deepcopy(pod)
                for template in (expected, got):
                    template["metadata"]["annotations"].pop("checksum/config")
                got["spec"]["initContainers"] = got["spec"]["initContainers"][1:]
                if not got["spec"]["initContainers"]:
                    del got["spec"]["initContainers"]
                self.assertEqual(got, expected)
                # standalone.yaml gains storage_integrity.backup only, as its last
                # key (Plan S3-C1's shape); the SNode keeps its si_snode login.
                old, new = host_config(login), host_config(docs)
                self.assertEqual(list(new["storage_integrity"])[-1], "backup")
                si_backup = self.si_backup_of(name)
                backup = {"bucket_url": si_backup["bucketURL"], "owner_indexer_id": si_backup["ownerIndexerID"],
                          "max_chain_links": si_backup["maxChainLinks"]}
                self.assertEqual(new["storage_integrity"].pop("backup"), backup)
                self.assertEqual(new, old)
                self.assertEqual(new["storage_integrity"]["clickhouse_username"], "si_snode")
                self.assertEqual({key for key in login if docs[key] != login[key]},
                                 {("ConfigMap", f"{name}-node-config"), ("StatefulSet", name)})

    def test_rebuild_safe_takes_the_restore_key_only_from_a_secret(self):
        for name, release in self.rebuildable_hosts().items():
            with self.subTest(release=name):
                result = self.render_with(release, self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name), self.rebuild_safe(name))
                docs = documents(result)
                restore = DEVNET2_SI_RESTORE_SECRETS[name]
                spec = self.host_pod(docs, name)["spec"]
                rebuild, others = spec["initContainers"][0], spec["initContainers"][1:] + spec["containers"]
                for item in rebuild["env"]:
                    self.assertEqual(set(item), {"name", "valueFrom"}, item["name"])
                    self.assertEqual(set(item["valueFrom"]), {"secretKeyRef"}, item["name"])
                # The key Secret reaches the init container alone in the host
                # pod: no other container and no volume of it names it, and no
                # other object does but the si-member, whose restore source
                # (Plan S3-C3 siMember.restoreSecret) is the same read-only key.
                self.assertEqual([item["name"] for item in rebuild["env"] if item["valueFrom"]["secretKeyRef"]["name"] == restore],
                                 ["STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"])
                for container in others:
                    self.assertNotIn(restore, json.dumps(container), container["name"])
                self.assertNotIn(restore, json.dumps(spec["volumes"]))
                for key, resource in docs.items():
                    if key not in (("StatefulSet", name), ("StatefulSet", f"{name}-si-member")):
                        self.assertNotIn(restore, json.dumps(resource), key)
                self.assertNotIn("ckh-manager", [mount["name"] for mount in rebuild["volumeMounts"]])
                # No rendered config carries a key or a key name.
                for key, resource in docs.items():
                    for text in (resource.get("data") or {}).values():
                        for word in ("access_key", "secret_access", "access-id", "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_"):
                            self.assertNotIn(word, text, key)

    def test_rebuild_safe_guards_fail_closed(self):
        name = "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c"
        login = (self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name))
        # Rebuild is an offline journal writer: typos and false-ish malformed
        # maps cannot silently skip it or render a runtime-invalid config.
        for malformed in (False, 0, [], ""):
            result = self.render_with(self.indexer_c_release, *login, {"storageIntegrity": {"snode": {"rebuildSafe": malformed}}})
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, repr(malformed))
            self.assertIn("storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe must be a map", result.stderr)
        for changes, error in (
            ({"backup": ["20261020T041700Z-full"]}, "rebuildSafe.backup must be"),
            ({"backup": "../foreign"}, "rebuildSafe.backup must be"),
            ({"enable": True}, "rebuildSafe has unknown key"),
            ({"restoreKeySecret": {"name": "restore", "accessIdKey": []}}, "rebuildSafe.restoreKeySecret"),
            ({"restoreKeySecret": {"name": "restore", "secretKey": False}}, "rebuildSafe.restoreKeySecret"),
            ({"restoreKeySecret": {"name": "restore", "secreKey": "typo"}}, "rebuildSafe.restoreKeySecret"),
        ):
            result = self.render_with(self.indexer_c_release, *login, self.rebuild_safe(name, **changes))
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, changes)
            self.assertIn(error, result.stderr)
        for owner in (-1, True, 1.5, "18446744073709551616", "01"):
            result = self.render_with(self.indexer_c_release, *login, self.rebuild_safe(name), {"siBackup": {"enabled": False, "ownerIndexerID": owner}})
            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, repr(owner))
            self.assertIn("rebuildSafe requires siBackup.ownerIndexerID", result.stderr)
        result = self.render_with(self.indexer_c_release, *login, self.rebuild_safe(name), {"siBackup": {"enabled": False, "ownerIndexerID": "18446744073709551615"}})
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(host_config(documents(result))["storage_integrity"]["backup"]["owner_indexer_id"], 18446744073709551615)
        name = "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c"
        self.require_indexer_c()
        release = self.indexer_c_release
        login = (self.host_logout(), self.host_login(name))
        for overrides, message in (
            ((*login, self.rebuild_safe(name, backup="")), "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe.backup is required"),
            ((self.host_logout(), self.rebuild_safe(name)),
             "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe requires storageIntegrity.clickhouseUsername: it restores as the SNode's ClickHouse user"),
            ((*login, self.rebuild_safe(name, restoreKeySecret={"name": ""})),
             "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe.restoreKeySecret.name is required"),
            ((*login, self.rebuild_safe(name, restoreKeySecret=None)),
             "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe.restoreKeySecret.name is required"),
            # siBackup's own guards would refuse first while its job is enabled.
            ((*login, self.rebuild_safe(name), {"siBackup": {"enabled": False, "bucketURL": ""}}),
             "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe requires siBackup.bucketURL and siBackup.ownerIndexerID: "
             "storage_integrity.backup names the object store and the owner prefix it restores from"),
            ((*login, self.rebuild_safe(name), {"siBackup": {"enabled": False, "ownerIndexerID": None}}),
             "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe requires siBackup.bucketURL and siBackup.ownerIndexerID"),
            ((*login, self.rebuild_safe(name, enabled="true")), "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe.enabled must be a boolean"),
            ((*login, {"storageIntegrity": {"snode": {"rebuildSafe": "on"}}}), "storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe must be a map"),
        ):
            with self.subTest(message=message, overrides=overrides[-1]):
                result = self.render_with(release, *overrides)
                self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
                self.assertIn(message, result.stderr)
        result = render_sentio_node(self.rebuild_safe(name))
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
        self.assertIn("storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe requires storageIntegrity.enabled", result.stderr)
        # indexer-a owns the genesis table: rebuild-safe refuses it, and so does the chart.
        indexer_a = "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a"
        result = self.render_with(self.source_release, self.host_logout(), self.host_login(indexer_a), self.rebuild_safe(indexer_a))
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
        self.assertIn("storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe requires an empty storageIntegrity.snode.tableIDs: "
                      "rebuild-safe rebuilds only an indexer without genesis tables", result.stderr)

    def test_rebuild_safe_needs_a_reviewed_image(self):
        # An image without the command fails the init container and with it the
        # pod: a values file may turn rebuildSafe on only with a reviewed image,
        # which is also a stage-3 host, replica-read host and writer-authorization image.
        self.assertRegex(DEVNET2_STAGE3_P4_SOURCE_IMAGE, r"^ghcr\.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-[0-9a-f]{40}@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$")
        self.assertIn(DEVNET2_STAGE3_P4_SOURCE_IMAGE, WRITER_AUTHORIZATION_IMAGES)
        self.assertIn(DEVNET2_STAGE3_P4_SOURCE_IMAGE, STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES)
        self.assertIn(DEVNET2_STAGE3_P4_SOURCE_IMAGE, REPLICA_READ_HOST_IMAGES)
        self.assertEqual(REBUILD_SAFE_IMAGES, frozenset({DEVNET2_STAGE3_P4_SOURCE_IMAGE}))
        checked, referenced = [], set()
        for helmfile in sentio_node_helmfiles():
            for release in yaml.safe_load(helmfile.read_text())["releases"]:
                if (helmfile.parent / release["chart"]).resolve() != SENTIO_NODE_CHART:
                    continue
                label = f"{helmfile.relative_to(ROOT)}:{release['name']}"
                values, files = release_chart_values(helmfile, release, label)
                referenced.update(files)
                checked.append(label)
                rebuild = values["storageIntegrity"]["snode"].get("rebuildSafe")
                if not (isinstance(rebuild, dict) and rebuild.get("enabled")):
                    continue
                image = values["node"]["image"]
                self.assertIn(f'{image["repository"]}:{image["tag"]}', REBUILD_SAFE_IMAGES,
                              f"{label}: storageIntegrity.snode.rebuildSafe needs a reviewed image")
        for name in DEVNET2_SI_RELEASES:
            self.assertIn(f"{FRESH_HELMFILE.relative_to(ROOT)}:{name}", checked)
        # No file outside those releases may set the key.
        tracked = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "ls-files", "k8s-*"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
        ).stdout.split()
        for name in tracked:
            path = ROOT / name
            if path.suffix in (".yaml", ".yml") and path not in referenced and path.is_file():
                self.assertNotIn("rebuildSafe", path.read_text(errors="ignore"), f"{name} is not part of any sentio-node release")
```

```python
def policy_documents(path):
    """Every document of a kubectl-applied policy file by metadata.name."""
    found = {}
    for document in yaml.safe_load_all(path.read_text()):
        if not document:
            continue
        name = document["metadata"]["name"]
        if name in found:
            raise AssertionError(f"{path.name}: {name} twice")
        found[name] = document
    return found


def si_network_probe():
    """The probe matrix: (aliases, rows). An alias line is
    "# alias<TAB>name<TAB>namespace<TAB>k=v,..." (the labels of the alias's pod
    that the policies select on); a row is (from, to, port, expect)."""
    aliases, rows, header = {}, [], None
    for line in SI_NETWORK_PROBE_FILE.read_text().splitlines():
        if line.startswith("# alias\t"):
            fields = line.split("\t")
            if len(fields) != 4:
                raise AssertionError(f"alias line needs four tab-separated fields: {line!r}")
            _, name, namespace, selector = fields
            if name in aliases:
                raise AssertionError(f"alias {name} defined twice")
            aliases[name] = (namespace, dict(item.split("=", 1) for item in selector.split(",")))
        elif not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        elif header is None:
            header = line
            if header != "from\tto\tport\texpect":
                raise AssertionError(f"probe matrix header is {header!r}")
        else:
            fields = line.split("\t")
            if len(fields) != 4 or not fields[2].isdigit():
                raise AssertionError(f"probe row needs from, to, port and expect: {line!r}")
            rows.append((fields[0], fields[1], int(fields[2]), fields[3]))
    return aliases, rows


def selector_matches(selector, namespace, labels, policy_namespace):
    """Whether a Cilium endpoint selector selects a pod with these labels in
    namespace: its k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace label names the namespace,
    else the policy's own."""
    match = dict(selector.get("matchLabels") or {})
    if namespace != match.pop("k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace", policy_namespace):
        return False
    if any(labels.get(key) != value for key, value in match.items()):
        return False
    for expression in selector.get("matchExpressions") or []:
        value = labels.get(expression["key"])
        operator = expression["operator"]
        if operator not in ("In", "NotIn", "Exists", "DoesNotExist"):
            raise AssertionError(f"unknown selector operator {operator}")
        if ((operator == "In" and value not in expression["values"])
                or (operator == "NotIn" and value in expression["values"])
                or (operator == "Exists" and value is None)
                or (operator == "DoesNotExist" and value is not None)):
            return False
    return True


def rule_ports(rule):
    return [int(entry["port"]) for ports in rule["toPorts"] for entry in ports["ports"]]


def rule_admits(rule, namespace, labels, port, policy_namespace):
    """Whether one ingress rule admits a pod (namespace, labels) on port; fromEntities rules admit no pod."""
    return port in rule_ports(rule) and any(
        selector_matches(peer, namespace, labels, policy_namespace) for peer in rule.get("fromEndpoints", [])
    )


def probed_policies():
    """Every policy the probe matrix covers: name -> its CiliumNetworkPolicy."""
    policies = dict(policy_documents(SI_NETWORK_POLICY_FILE))
    policies[KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY] = policy_documents(KEEPER_POLICY_FILE)[KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY]
    return policies


def workload_pods(docs):
    """(kind, name, pod template) of every workload a release renders, a CronJob's job template included."""
    for (kind, name), resource in docs.items():
        if kind in ("StatefulSet", "Deployment", "Job", "DaemonSet"):
            yield kind, name, resource["spec"]["template"]
        elif kind == "CronJob":
            yield kind, name, resource["spec"]["jobTemplate"]["spec"]["template"]
```

```python
    def test_si_network_policies_are_ingress_only(self):
        policies = policy_documents(SI_NETWORK_POLICY_FILE)
        self.assertEqual(set(policies), set(SI_NETWORK_POLICIES))
        keeper = policy_documents(KEEPER_POLICY_FILE)[KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY]
        for name, policy in {**policies, KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY: keeper}.items():
            with self.subTest(policy=name):
                self.assertEqual((policy["apiVersion"], policy["kind"]), ("cilium.io/v2", "CiliumNetworkPolicy"))
                spec = policy["spec"]
                # Ingress rules only: never an egress rule, a deny rule or a
                # default deny on egress, so no SI pod's own dial (backups,
                # restores, pulls, Keeper) can break (K57).
                self.assertEqual(set(spec), {"endpointSelector", "enableDefaultDeny", "ingress"})
                self.assertEqual(set(spec["enableDefaultDeny"]), {"ingress", "egress"})
                self.assertIs(spec["enableDefaultDeny"]["egress"], False)
                self.assertIsInstance(spec["enableDefaultDeny"]["ingress"], bool)
                for rule in spec["ingress"]:
                    self.assertLessEqual(set(rule), {"fromEndpoints", "fromEntities", "toPorts"}, rule)
                    self.assertEqual(len({"fromEndpoints", "fromEntities"} & set(rule)), 1, rule)
                    # Pod selectors, or the node itself for the kubelet: never
                    # world, cluster, CIDRs or service IPs (cilium-ops §D).
                    if "fromEntities" in rule:
                        self.assertEqual(rule["fromEntities"], ["host"])
                    for entry in rule["toPorts"]:
                        self.assertEqual(set(entry), {"ports"})
                        for port in entry["ports"]:
                            self.assertEqual(set(port), {"port", "protocol"})
                            self.assertEqual(port["protocol"], "TCP")
                            self.assertRegex(port["port"], r"^[1-9][0-9]*$")

        self.assertEqual(set(SI_NETWORK_POLICIES.values()), set(DEVNET2_SI_HOST_CLICKHOUSE.values()))
        # The operator labels a CHI's pods with clickhouse.altinity.com/chi;

    def test_si_network_policies_admit_exactly_the_reviewed_flows(self):
        policies = policy_documents(SI_NETWORK_POLICY_FILE)
        for name in SI_NETWORK_POLICIES:
            with self.subTest(policy=name):
                self.assertEqual(policies[name]["spec"]["ingress"], list(SI_NETWORK_FLOWS[name]))
                for rule in SI_NETWORK_FLOWS[name]:
                    self.assertLessEqual(set(rule_ports(rule)), {8123, 9000, 9009, 9363}, rule)
        # Each host rule names its own release, and the pods it means carry
        # exactly the labels it selects: the host pod, the si-member and the
        # backup job of that release, never its DinD, Redis or IPFS pod.
        self.require_every_si_host()
        for policy, installation in SI_NETWORK_POLICIES.items():
            host = next(name for name, chi in DEVNET2_SI_HOST_CLICKHOUSE.items() if chi == installation)
            rule = SI_NETWORK_FLOWS[policy][0]
            self.assertEqual(rule["fromEndpoints"], [_si_host_peer(host)])

            components = set()
            for kind, workload, pod in workload_pods(docs):
                with self.subTest(release=host, workload=workload):
                    labels = pod["metadata"].get("labels") or {}
                    self.assertEqual(labels.get("app.kubernetes.io/instance"), host)
                    component = labels.get("app.kubernetes.io/component")
                    components.add(component)

                    self.assertEqual(admitted, component in SI_HOST_CLIENT_COMPONENTS, f"{kind} {workload}: {component}")
            self.assertIn("node", components)

        # The network release's verifiers and bootstrap-source hook are admitted; its voters and DA are not.
        rule = SI_NETWORK_FLOWS["storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-ingress"][1]
        admitted = {

            for kind, workload, pod in workload_pods(self.control)

        self.assertEqual(admitted, {
            f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-arbiter": False, f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-verifier": True,
            f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-da": False, f"{FRESH_RELEASE}-bootstrap-source": True,

    def test_every_allowed_flow_has_a_positive_probe_row(self):
        aliases, rows = si_network_probe()
        policies = probed_policies()
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), len(set(rows)), "a probe row twice")
        used = {alias for row in rows for alias in row[:2]}
        self.assertEqual(used - set(aliases), set(), "undefined aliases")
        # Probed from every pod: each alias opens at least one row.
        self.assertEqual(set(aliases) - {row[0] for row in rows}, set(), "an alias never probes")
        targets = {}
        for alias, (namespace, labels) in aliases.items():
            selected = [name for name, policy in policies.items() if selector_matches(
                policy["spec"]["endpointSelector"], namespace, labels, policy["metadata"]["namespace"])]
            self.assertLessEqual(len(selected), 1, alias)
            if selected:
                targets[alias] = selected[0]
        for row in rows:
            source, target, port, expect = row
            with self.subTest(row=row):
                self.assertIn(expect, ("open", "refused"))
                self.assertIn(target, targets, f"{target} is no policy's pod")
                policy = policies[targets[target]]
                namespace, labels = aliases[source]
                admitted = any(rule_admits(rule, namespace, labels, port, policy["metadata"]["namespace"])
                               for rule in policy["spec"]["ingress"])
                # The matrix states what each policy enforces.
                self.assertEqual(admitted, expect == "open")
        # Every allowed (policy, rule, port) has an open row from a pod the
        # rule admits to a pod of the policy, but the flows no probe pod stands in for.
        for name, policy in policies.items():
            for rule in policy["spec"]["ingress"]:
                if rule in SI_NETWORK_UNPROBED_FLOWS.values():
                    continue
                for port in rule_ports(rule):
                    with self.subTest(policy=name, rule=rule, port=port):
                        self.assertTrue(any(
                            expect == "open" and targets.get(target) == name and probe_port == port
                            and rule_admits(rule, aliases[source][0], aliases[source][1], port, policy["metadata"]["namespace"])
                            for source, target, probe_port, expect in rows
                        ), f"{name}: no open row for {rule} on {port}")

    def test_probe_matrix_has_negative_rows(self):
        aliases, rows = si_network_probe()
        refused = {(source, target, port) for source, target, port, expect in rows if expect == "refused"}
        si_targets = {"storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-ingress": "ch-network-source",
                      "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-clickhouse-ingress": "ch-b",
                      "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-clickhouse-ingress": "ch-c"}
        self.assertEqual(set(si_targets), set(SI_NETWORK_POLICIES))
        other_host = {"ch-network-source": "host-b", "ch-b": "host-c", "ch-c": "host-a"}
        for target in si_targets.values():
            with self.subTest(target=target):
                # Tenant driver code, the ordinary devnet2 node and a pod of
                # another namespace never reach an SI ClickHouse ...
                for source in ("dind", "observer", "toolbox"):
                    self.assertIn((source, target, 9000), refused)
                # ... nor does another installation's host, and only a
                # ClickHouse fetches parts.
                self.assertIn((other_host[target], target, 9000), refused)
                self.assertTrue({(source, target, 9009) for source in ("host-a", "host-b", "host-c", "toolbox")} & refused)
        for source in ("host-a", "dind", "toolbox"):
            self.assertTrue(any(row[0] == source and row[1].startswith("keeper-") and row[2] == 2181 for row in refused), source)
        # Raft stays among the replicas.
        self.assertTrue(any(row[1].startswith("keeper-") and row[2] == 9444 and not row[0].startswith("keeper-") for row in refused))

    def test_keeper_ingress_policy_admits_every_census_client(self):
        documents_ = policy_documents(KEEPER_POLICY_FILE)
        policy = documents_[KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY]
        self.assertEqual(policy["metadata"], {"name": KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY, "namespace": "clickhouse"})
        self.assertEqual(policy["spec"]["endpointSelector"],
                         {"matchLabels": {"clickhouse-keeper.altinity.com/chk": "clickhouse-keeper-extra"}})
        # Every census client, then the peers; nothing else.
        self.assertEqual(policy["spec"]["ingress"], [*KEEPER_INGRESS_CLIENTS.values(), KEEPER_INGRESS_PEERS])
        for name, rule in KEEPER_INGRESS_CLIENTS.items():
            with self.subTest(client=name):
                self.assertIn(2181, rule_ports(rule))
                self.assertIn("fromEndpoints", rule)
        # Every SI ClickHouse installation is a client.
        si = KEEPER_INGRESS_CLIENTS["devnet2-si-clickhouse"]["fromEndpoints"][0]
        for installation in SI_NETWORK_POLICIES.values():
            self.assertTrue(selector_matches(si, LEGACY_NAMESPACE, {"clickhouse.altinity.com/chi": installation}, "clickhouse"))
        # The ensemble's enforced egress policy stays exactly as it was.
        self.assertEqual(documents_["clickhouse-keeper-extra-egress"]["spec"], {
            "endpointSelector": {"matchLabels": {"clickhouse-keeper.altinity.com/chk": "clickhouse-keeper-extra"}},
            "enableDefaultDeny": {"egress": True, "ingress": False},
            "egress": [
                {"toEntities": ["host"], "toPorts": [{"ports": [{"port": "53", "protocol": "UDP"}, {"port": "53", "protocol": "TCP"}]}]},
                {"toEndpoints": [{"matchLabels": {
                    "k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace": "clickhouse", "clickhouse-keeper.altinity.com/chk": "clickhouse-keeper-extra",
                }}], "toPorts": _tcp(9444, 2181)},
            ],
        })
        # Only this policy selects the ensemble for ingress.
        ingress = [name for name, document in documents_.items() if "ingress" in document["spec"]]
        self.assertEqual(ingress, [KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY])

    def test_keeper_ingress_policy_keeps_the_raft_peers(self):
        policy = policy_documents(KEEPER_POLICY_FILE)[KEEPER_INGRESS_POLICY]
        peers = [rule for rule in policy["spec"]["ingress"] if rule == KEEPER_INGRESS_PEERS]
        self.assertEqual(len(peers), 1)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(rule_ports(KEEPER_INGRESS_PEERS)), [2181, 9444])
        # The peers are exactly the pods the policy protects.
        (peer,) = KEEPER_INGRESS_PEERS["fromEndpoints"]
        selector = dict(peer["matchLabels"])
        self.assertEqual(selector.pop("k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace"), policy["metadata"]["namespace"])
        self.assertEqual({"matchLabels": selector}, policy["spec"]["endpointSelector"])
        # The ensemble's configuration: three replicas, clients on 2181, raft on 9444.
        keeper = yaml.safe_load((ROOT / "k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse-extra-keeper.yaml").read_text())
        settings = keeper["spec"]["configuration"]["settings"]
        self.assertEqual((settings["keeper_server/tcp_port"], settings["keeper_server/raft_configuration/server/port"]), ("2181", "9444"))
        self.assertEqual(keeper["spec"]["configuration"]["clusters"][0]["layout"]["replicasCount"], 3)
        # Every pair of replicas is probed on raft.
        aliases, rows = si_network_probe()
        raft = {(source, target) for source, target, port, expect in rows if port == 9444 and expect == "open"}
        replicas = [alias for alias in aliases if alias.startswith("keeper-")]
        self.assertEqual(sorted(replicas), ["keeper-0", "keeper-1", "keeper-2"])
        self.assertEqual({frozenset(pair) for pair in raft}, {frozenset(pair) for pair in
                         (("keeper-0", "keeper-1"), ("keeper-1", "keeper-2"), ("keeper-2", "keeper-0"))})
```

```yaml
# Ingress-only CiliumNetworkPolicies of the devnet2-si-v2 SI ClickHouse
# installations (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14 "Network hardening"; Plan S3-D
# K57; docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md §7). Not
# Helm-managed and never synced: the runbook applies one policy at a time
# with kubectl --context sentio-sea apply, a --dry-run=server run first.
#
# Each policy selects only one installation's ClickHouse pods, by the
# operator's clickhouse.altinity.com/chi label, which no host, gateway,
# verifier or voter pod carries; it admits exactly the reviewed flows
# (charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py SI_NETWORK_FLOWS):
# - 9000 and 8123 from the installation's host release: the host pod (SNode,
#   HouseGate, the rebuild-safe init container), its si-member and its backup
#   job; never its DinD, Redis or IPFS pod. The network installation also
#   admits this release's verifiers and its bootstrap-source hook.
# - 9000 and 9009 from every SI ClickHouse pod: member pulls through named
#   collections and interserver fetches.
# - 8123 from the devnet2 ClickHouse operator, 9363 from namespace monitoring
#   (vmagent), 8123 from the node itself (the kubelet's /ping probes).
#
# enableDefaultDeny.ingress false is observe (the rules match, nothing is
# denied); true is enforce, one installation per window, indexer-b first, only
# after the 7-day census is covered and tests/si_network_probe.tsv passes from
# every pod (runbook §7.2, §7.3). The enforce commit adds every further census
# client here and to SI_NETWORK_FLOWS. Egress is not enumerated (GCS needs world
# or FQDN rules with a DNS proxy), so enableDefaultDeny.egress stays false.
---
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-ingress
  namespace: sentio-network-devnet2
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      clickhouse.altinity.com/chi: storage-integrity-si-v2
  enableDefaultDeny:
    ingress: false
    egress: false
  ingress:
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            app.kubernetes.io/instance: sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a
          matchExpressions:
            - {key: app.kubernetes.io/component, operator: In, values: [node, si-backup, si-member]}
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - {port: "9000", protocol: TCP}
            - {port: "8123", protocol: TCP}
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            app.kubernetes.io/instance: storage-integrity-si-v2
          matchExpressions:
            - {key: app.kubernetes.io/component, operator: In, values: [bootstrap, verifier]}
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - {port: "9000", protocol: TCP}
            - {port: "8123", protocol: TCP}
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: clickhouse.altinity.com/chi
              operator: In
              values: [storage-integrity-si-v2, storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b, storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c]
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - {port: "9000", protocol: TCP}
            - {port: "9009", protocol: TCP}
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            app.kubernetes.io/instance: devnet2-operator
            app.kubernetes.io/name: altinity-clickhouse-operator
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - {port: "8123", protocol: TCP}
    - fromEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: monitoring
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - {port: "9363", protocol: TCP}
    - fromEntities: [host]
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - {port: "8123", protocol: TCP}
---
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-clickhouse-ingress
  namespace: sentio-network-devnet2
spec:

      clickhouse.altinity.com/chi: storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b
  enableDefaultDeny:

    - fromEndpoints:
```
