````markdown
## 2. Census

Seven days, read-only (K57). Start it right after §1, keep every other change out of the three installations and the Keeper ensemble for the whole window, and run §2.1 and §2.2 at its end; §2.3 samples once a day. The census is judged against the observe documents of the merged PR: a client the documents do not admit yet is added in its installation's enforce commit (§7.3) or in the Keeper PR (§8.3), with a probe row; an unattributed client stops the runbook until a reviewed deterministic attribution change is applied and both initial and targeted checks are rerun. A human naming note alone does not change the parser and cannot clear the gate.

```bash
date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' | tee "$si_backup/census-start"
```

### 2.1 ClickHouse clients

At the end of the window, every query each SI ClickHouse logged over the 7 days, and the scrapers of their metrics ports:

```bash
[ -s "$si_backup/census-start" ] || { echo "start the census first (§2)"; exit 1; }
start="$(cat "$si_backup/census-start")"
for inst in network indexer-b indexer-c; do si_net_census "$inst" "$start" > "$si_backup/census-clickhouse-$inst.tsv"; done
si_net_scrapes > "$si_backup/census-scrape.tsv"
wc -l "$si_backup"/census-clickhouse-*.tsv "$si_backup/census-scrape.tsv"
```

Expected: rows for the three hosts' SNodes (`si_snode`) and gateways (`si_gateway`), the si-members (`si_member`, and their pulls arriving from the peer source ClickHouses with that ClickHouse's pod as `client`), the backup jobs (`si_backup`), the verifiers (`si_verifier` on their own ClickHouses), the bootstrap hook on the network source, `loopback` rows (this runbook's and the earlier runbooks' own admin reads), and the vmagent scrape of port 9363 on all six pods and of 7000 on the Keeper replicas if it is scraped.

### 2.2 Interserver fetches

The interserver fetchers are the replicas Keeper records under every SI table's path (`<path>/replicas/<replica>/host`): every replica of a table fetches from every other one on port 9009. Members hold no Keeper replica before P6.

```bash
si_net_replicas | tee "$si_backup/census-interserver-all.tsv" | awk -F'\t' '{print $2}' | LC_ALL=C sort | uniq -c
si_p4_py split-interserver "$si_backup/census-interserver-all.tsv" "$si_backup"
wc -l "$si_backup"/census-interserver-*.tsv
```

Expected: replica names `snode-1`, `snode-2`, `snode-3`, `verifier-1`, `verifier-2`, `verifier-3` only, each with its own replica Service as host and port 9009, every one `active` `yes` (an inactive replica of a node that left: stop and explain it before §5); the split writes `census-interserver-network.tsv`, `-indexer-b.tsv` and `-indexer-c.tsv`. A host that is no SI ClickHouse's replica Service stops the split.

### 2.3 Keeper clients

Once a day of the window (at least seven samples, `n` from 1), the sessions every Keeper replica holds:

```bash
n=$(( $(find "$si_backup" -maxdepth 1 -name 'census-keeper-*.txt' | wc -l) + 1 ))
si_keeper_cons > "$si_backup/census-keeper-$n.txt"
si_keeper_state | tee "$si_backup/keeper-state-$n.txt"
awk -F'\t' 'NR > 1 {print $4 "/" $5}' "$si_backup/census-keeper-$n.txt" | LC_ALL=C sort | uniq -c
```

Expected: sessions from the `clickhouse-extra` pods (namespace `clickhouse`) and the six SI ClickHouse pods, and whatever else the ensemble serves; an address no pod or node holds prints `-/-`. Short-lived clients (four-letter-word probes) do not show in `cons`; §8.3's watch catches them.

Then the census check, read-only, against the observe documents at HEAD:

```bash
find "$si_backup" -maxdepth 1 -name 'census-keeper-*.txt' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
si_p4_py census-check "$si_backup"/pods-census-*.json "$si_backup"/census-clickhouse-*.tsv "$si_backup"/census-interserver-network.tsv "$si_backup"/census-interserver-indexer-b.tsv "$si_backup"/census-interserver-indexer-c.tsv "$si_backup/census-scrape.tsv" "$si_backup"/census-keeper-*.txt 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/census-check.txt" | grep -v '^admitted ' || true
```

Expected: at least 7 samples; then only `loopback` lines and the summary `census: <n> admitted, <m> uncovered or unattributed`. Each `UNCOVERED` line names a client the policy must admit: it joins its installation's enforce commit (§7.3) or the Keeper PR (§8.3), with a positive probe row and its `SI_NETWORK_FLOWS` or `KEEPER_INGRESS_CLIENTS` entry. Each `unattributed` line stops the runbook until the user has named the client (by its address, `client`, user and time): a client nobody can name is not admitted. Keep `census-check.txt`; §7.3 and §8.3 re-run the check against their enforce documents.

### 2.4 Placement

A `drift` line means `DEVNET2_CLICKHOUSE_NODES` no longer matches a pod: explain it before §5. `verdict placement STOP` (two sources on one node, every eligible node holding a source, fewer than four eligible nodes, a pin that disagrees with its pod): stop; the plan is amended (K55).

## 3. Staging proof

Two throwaway CHIs, `storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-a` and `-b` (`docs/examples/storage-integrity-p4-interserver-staging-chi.yaml`: indexer-b's CHI renamed with 1Gi volumes, posture C with S3-B's staging logins), replicate one table under their own Keeper root and show on the deployed ClickHouse image what M16 showed in CI: a credentialed server with `allow_empty` accepts an uncredentialed fetcher, an uncredentialed server refuses a credentialed one, and step 2 closes the uncredentialed path. M16's deployed-image run (`<P4_MECHANICS>`) is required first. The committed example carries no interserver setting; each staging state adds only the three `interserver_http_credentials/*` keys, with the password from the one Secret every SI installation names, `storage-integrity-si-v2-interserver` (key `password`; `si_p4_py staging-secret` prints the reference, which an example that names its own would override). That Secret exists only once the user has run §4, so §4 runs before §3.1 although it is numbered after the proof: nothing reads the Secret until §5, and §3.1 refuses while it is missing. If the pair shows any other behaviour, stop: the plan is amended (K56).

### 3.1 Staging pair

The Keeper root first (ClickHouse refuses Keeper operations until a CHI's root exists; the block refuses a root that exists already), then the pair in the mixed state, `-a` with credentials and `allow_empty` `"true"`, `-b` without:

Confirm before running.

```bash
read -r sname skey <<< "$(si_p4_py staging-secret)"
case " $(si_secret_keys "$sname" 2>/dev/null) " in *" $skey "*) ;; *) echo "the staging pair's password, Secret $sname key $skey, is missing (the interserver Secret: run §4 first)"; exit 1 ;; esac
exists="$(si_p4_keeper_exists /storage-integrity/devnet2/p4-interserver-staging)" || exit 1
[ "$exists" = 0 ] || { echo "the staging root exists already: reconcile prior ownership before any write"; exit 1; }
si_keeper "touch '/storage-integrity/devnet2/p4-interserver-staging'"
si_p4_py staging empty none "$si_backup/staging-empty-none.yaml"
si_kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f "$si_backup/staging-empty-none.yaml" > /dev/null
si_kubectl apply -f "$si_backup/staging-empty-none.yaml"
for x in a b; do
  until si_kubectl get pod "storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-$x-source-0-0-0" > /dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 5; done
  si_kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-$x-source-0-0-0" --timeout=15m
  si_wait_chi "storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-$x"
done
for x in a b; do si_staging_pair "$x" "CREATE TABLE default.p4_interserver (x UInt64) ENGINE = ReplicatedMergeTree('/p4/interserver', '{replica}') ORDER BY x"; done
```

Then, read-only:

```bash
{
  for x in a b; do
    pod="storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-$x-source-0-0-0"
    printf '%s %s\n' "$pod" "$(si_kubectl exec "$pod" -c clickhouse -- awk "$si_interserver_awk" /var/lib/clickhouse/preprocessed_configs/config.xml)"
    si_staging_pair "$x" "SELECT replica_name, is_readonly, active_replicas, total_replicas FROM system.replicas WHERE database = 'default' AND table = 'p4_interserver' FORMAT TSV"
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/staging-pair.txt"
```

Expected: `-a` `user=si_interserver allow_empty=true password=set`, `-b` `credentials=absent`; on both, one replica row with `is_readonly` 0 and `2` active of `2` replicas.

### 3.2 Mixed-state fetches

A row inserted on `-a` must reach `-b` (an uncredentialed fetcher asks a credentialed `allow_empty` server), and a row inserted on `-b` must not reach `-a` within 60 s, with `-a`'s queue naming the refusal (a credentialed fetcher asks an uncredentialed server):

Confirm before running.

```bash
{
  si_staging_pair a "INSERT INTO default.p4_interserver VALUES (1)"
  si_staging_pair b "SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA default.p4_interserver" || true
  si_p4_staging_count b 1 || exit 1
  si_staging_pair b "INSERT INTO default.p4_interserver VALUES (2)"
  sleep 60
  si_p4_staging_count a 1 || exit 1
  si_p4_staging_auth a || exit 1
  si_staging_pair a "SELECT type, new_part_name, num_tries, last_exception FROM system.replication_queue WHERE table = 'p4_interserver' FORMAT Vertical"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/staging-mixed.txt"
```

Expected: `staging b count 1`, `staging a count 1` and a failed `GET_PART` with positive `num_tries`; its error must be either the measured `Client requires HTTP Basic authentication` refusal or a 401 with HTTP basic authentication. No other error establishes the mechanics. Any other outcome: stop (K56).

### 3.3 Step 2

`-b` gains credentials with `allow_empty` `"true"` (step 1 complete on the pair: `-a`'s queued fetch succeeds), then both go to `allow_empty` `"false"` (step 2: both directions replicate), then `-b` loses its credentials again while `-a` stays strict (an uncredentialed fetcher is now refused):

Confirm before running.

```bash
{
  for v in "empty empty" "strict strict" "strict none"; do
    read -r am bm <<< "$v"
    si_p4_py staging "$am" "$bm" "$si_backup/staging-$am-$bm.yaml"
    si_kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f "$si_backup/staging-$am-$bm.yaml" > /dev/null
    si_kubectl apply -f "$si_backup/staging-$am-$bm.yaml"
    sleep 30
    for x in a b; do si_kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-$x-source-0-0-0" --timeout=15m; si_wait_chi "storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-$x"; done
    for x in a b; do printf '%s %s %s\n' "$v" "$x" "$(si_kubectl exec "storage-integrity-si-v2-p4-staging-$x-source-0-0-0" -c clickhouse -- awk "$si_interserver_awk" /var/lib/clickhouse/preprocessed_configs/config.xml)"; done
    case "$v" in
      "empty empty") si_staging_pair a "SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA default.p4_interserver" || true ;;
      "strict strict") si_staging_pair a "INSERT INTO default.p4_interserver VALUES (3)"; si_staging_pair b "INSERT INTO default.p4_interserver VALUES (4)"; sleep 20 ;;
      "strict none") si_staging_pair a "INSERT INTO default.p4_interserver VALUES (5)"; sleep 60 ;;
    esac
    case "$v" in
      "empty empty") si_p4_staging_count a 2 || exit 1; si_p4_staging_count b 2 || exit 1 ;;
      "strict strict") si_p4_staging_count a 4 || exit 1; si_p4_staging_count b 4 || exit 1 ;;
      "strict none") si_p4_staging_count a 5 || exit 1; si_p4_staging_count b 4 || exit 1; si_p4_staging_auth b || exit 1 ;;
    esac
    si_staging_pair b "SELECT type, new_part_name, num_tries, last_exception FROM system.replication_queue WHERE table = 'p4_interserver' FORMAT Vertical"
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/staging-step2.txt"
```

Expected: `empty empty`: both `allow_empty=true password=set`, `a` and `b` hold `2` rows; `strict strict`: both `allow_empty=false password=set`, both hold `4` rows and `-b`'s queue is empty; `strict none`: `-a` `allow_empty=false`, `-b` `credentials=absent`, `a` holds `5` and `b` `4`, with `-b`'s queue entry for the new part failing on authentication (its `last_exception` names the refused basic authentication). Any other outcome: stop (K56).

## 4. Interserver secret (user action)

Run before §3.1 (§3 says why). The user creates the one interserver Secret in the user's own fish terminal, from the root of a production checkout at `origin/main`. The script generates the password with `openssl rand -hex 24`, writes it only into Secret `storage-integrity-si-v2-interserver` (key `password`) in `sentio-network-devnet2` of context `sentio-sea`, refuses to overwrite an existing Secret and never prints it:

```fish
bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-interserver-secret.sh
```

It prints `make-interserver-secret: created Secret storage-integrity-si-v2-interserver (key password) in sentio-network-devnet2`, or refuses (`… exists; it is never overwritten`) and changes nothing.

Then, read-only:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$(si_secret_keys storage-integrity-si-v2-interserver)" | tee "$si_backup/interserver-secret.txt"
```

Expected: `password ` (one key; the value is never read here). No SI installation reads it until §5.

## 5. Interserver step 1 and node pins

One restart window per installation in K56's order: indexer-b's CHI, indexer-c's CHI, then the network CHI (indexer-a's source and `verifier-1..3`, the only `hg_unsafe` fetchers before P6), so every fetch of the mixed state is an uncredentialed verifier asking a credentialed `allow_empty` source, which succeeds. Each window's commit also pins the installation's ClickHouses to the nodes their `local-path` volumes already hold (`placement.tsv`; indexer-c's source is pinned since the E PR), so the restart moves nothing. A refused fetch only delays evidence: a verifier without a candidate part refuses to attest. No hold is needed: no consensus update runs.

### 5.0 Moving a verifier ClickHouse, only when §2.4 finds a conflict

Only for a `MOVE` line of `placement-verdict.txt`, one verifier per window, before §5.1. The verifier's ClickHouse holds only the protocol tables its verifier creates when it registers (its `hg_unsafe` replicas clone again from the sources; nothing promotes into a verifier's `hg_safe`), so its volume is not kept: its PVCs go and their PVs stay `Retain`ed and `Released` for the user to delete, and the verifier pod restarts once on the new, empty ClickHouse. While it is away the two other verifiers keep every block's quorum. Each move costs three promotions (one acceptance write per owner, values and rows `429<n>`), so the budget is read again first, read-only:

```bash
si_budget_capture
si_budget 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/budget-move.txt"
grep -c '^verdict MOVE ' "$si_backup/placement-verdict.txt"
```

Expected: `a drill spends at most <n>` with `<n>` at least the promotions still to come (18 minus the writes made so far, plus 3 per `MOVE` line). Less: stop.

One commit `chore(devnet2): P4 node pin moves verifier-<n> off <node>` in `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml` and `charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py`: `clickhouse.nodePins.verifier-<n>: "<target>"` (the `MOVE` line's target) and `DEVNET2_NODE_PINS[("storage-integrity-si-v2", "verifier-<n>")] = "<target>"`; nothing else. Set `n` and `target` from the `MOVE` line:

Confirm before running.

```bash
n='<n>'; target='<target>'
case "$n$target" in *'<'*) echo "set n and target from the MOVE line first"; exit 1 ;; esac
grep -q "^verdict MOVE verifier-$n from .* to $target " "$si_backup/placement-verdict.txt" || { echo "placement-verdict.txt has no MOVE of verifier-$n to $target"; exit 1; }
ev="$si_backup/move-verifier-$n.txt"
[ ! -e "$ev" ] || { echo "$ev exists: this move ran; never re-run it"; exit 1; }
pod="storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-$n-0-0-0"
for h in a b c; do si_quiet_point "$h"; done # a verifier attests every track
si_head_is charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml
python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py
[ "$(si_render_diff storage-integrity-si-v2)" = "changed ClickHouseInstallation/storage-integrity-si-v2" ] || { echo "the commit renders more than the network CHI differently; stop"; exit 1; }
move_head="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || exit 1
{
  echo "start $(si_stamp) commit $move_head"
  si_kubectl get pvc -l "clickhouse.altinity.com/chi=storage-integrity-si-v2,clickhouse.altinity.com/cluster=verifier-$n" -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.volumeName}{"\n"}{end}'
} | tee "$ev"
si_p4_commit_gate || exit 1
git push origin HEAD:main
helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml sync --selector name=storage-integrity-si-v2
sed -n '2,$p' "$ev" | while read -r pvc pv; do
  si_kadmin patch pv "$pv" -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'
  si_kubectl delete pvc "$pvc" --wait=false
done
# The pinned pod cannot start on its old local-path volume. Deleting it releases the old claims; a pod the
# StatefulSet re-creates before they are gone holds them Terminating, so it is deleted again until no old
# claim is left and the StatefulSet has created fresh ones on the target node.
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  si_kubectl delete pod "$pod" --wait --ignore-not-found
  sleep 10
  # an old claim is left while its name still binds its old volume; a claim that cannot be read counts as left
  left="$(sed -n '2,$p' "$ev" | while read -r pvc pv; do v="$(si_kubectl get pvc "$pvc" --ignore-not-found -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumeName}')" || v="$pv"; [ "$v" != "$pv" ] || echo "$pvc"; done)"
  [ -z "$left" ] && break
done
[ -z "$left" ] || { echo "the old claims of verifier-$n are still there after 30 deletions of its pod: stop and ask"; exit 1; }
for _ in $(seq 1 90); do
  [ "$(si_kubectl get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}' 2>/dev/null)" = "$target" ] && break
  sleep 10
done
[ "$(si_kubectl get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}' 2>/dev/null)" = "$target" ] || { si_kubectl describe pod "$pod" | tail -n 20; echo "the verifier ClickHouse is not scheduled on $target after 15 minutes: stop and ask"; exit 1; }
si_kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$pod" --timeout=30m
si_wait_chi storage-integrity-si-v2
# The verifier creates its protocol tables when it registers, so its pod restarts once on the empty ClickHouse.
vpod="storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-$(( n - 1 ))"
si_kubectl delete pod "$vpod" --wait
until si_kubectl get pod "$vpod" > /dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done
si_kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$vpod" --timeout=15m
echo "end $(si_stamp)" | tee -a "$ev"
```

Then, read-only, until the moved replica has caught up:

```bash
n='<n>'
case "$n" in *'<'*) echo "set n first"; exit 1 ;; esac
{
  si_kubectl get pod "storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier-$n-0-0-0" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}{"\n"}'
  si_kubectl get pvc -l "clickhouse.altinity.com/chi=storage-integrity-si-v2,clickhouse.altinity.com/cluster=verifier-$n" -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.phase} {.spec.volumeName}{"\n"}{end}'
  si_verifier_ch "$n" "SELECT database, table, is_readonly, queue_size, absolute_delay FROM system.replicas WHERE database = 'hg_unsafe' ORDER BY table FORMAT TSV"
  for i in 0 1 2; do si_metrics "$i"; done
  si_tracks | jq -c '[.indexers[] | {id: .indexer_id, quarantined}]'
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/move-verifier-$n-check.txt"
```

Expected: the target node; new PVCs `Bound` to new volumes; every `hg_unsafe` table of the network present with `is_readonly` 0, `queue_size` 0 and `absolute_delay` 0 (the restarted verifier created its protocol tables again at its registration, its `hg_unsafe` replicas under its own name, dropping the stale one first, and they cloned from the sources); three active verifiers on every voter; no track quarantined. Then one acceptance write per owner proves every track's blocks reach quorum with the moved verifier, in the user's terminal (the block sets `key_file`):

n='<n>'

  si_p4_accept "$key_file" b "429$n" "move$n"
  si_p4_accept "$key_file" c "429$n" "move$n"

```

## 7. SI ClickHouse policies

The production source pins Cilium 1.18.8 in `k8s-sea/cilium/helmfile.yaml`. Its [versioned CRD](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/v1.18.8/pkg/k8s/apis/cilium.io/client/crds/v2/ciliumnetworkpolicies.yaml) and [API types](https://github.com/cilium/cilium/blob/v1.18.8/pkg/k8s/apis/cilium.io/v2/cnp_types.go) define `status.conditions` with `type: Valid`. The apply helper checks the exact policy spec and API-server identity alongside one `Valid=True`; this condition does not prove data-plane enforcement. The matrix, pod readiness, Hubble observations and owner acceptance below remain required. If the deployed Cilium version differs from this pin, stop and reconcile its versioned API and behavior before applying a policy.

One `CiliumNetworkPolicy` per installation, ingress-only, selecting only that installation's ClickHouse pods (`clickhouse.altinity.com/chi`), never a gateway or host pod (a policy that selects a gateway pod is an instant site-wide 502). Observe first: the rules match and nothing is denied. Enforce follows only a covered census and a passing probe matrix from every pod, one installation per window, indexer-b first.

### 7.1 Observe

One apply per installation, from the merged file's document (observe), each confirmed on its own; the first:

si_cnp_apply "$p" observe | tee "$si_backup/cnp-$p-observe-applied"
```

Then the same block with `p=storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-clickhouse-ingress`, and then with `p=storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-ingress`, each after its own confirmation. Then, read-only:

  si_cnp_modes
  for chi in storage-integrity-si-v2 storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c; do si_chi_state "$chi"; done
  si_global
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/cnp-observe-state.txt"
```

Expected: the three SI policies `observe valid=True` and the Keeper policy `absent`; every pod's uid and restart count as in §6 (a policy restarts nothing); safe progress unchanged.

## 8. Keeper ingress allowlist

`clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress` selects the three replicas of the shared production ensemble (`clickhouse-keeper.altinity.com/chk: clickhouse-keeper-extra`) and admits 2181 from the `clickhouse-extra` pods, from the six SI ClickHouses, 2181 and 9444 from the Keeper peers, and every census client (`KEEPER_INGRESS_CLIENTS`); the existing egress policy `clickhouse-keeper-extra-egress` is unchanged. It narrows which pods reach the ensemble; any SI ClickHouse can still write its paths (spec §18).

### 8.3 Enforce

The Keeper policy is cross-namespace shared production infrastructure, so its enforce flip is its own small PR, created and merged only after the user's confirmation, and applied with an abort criterion. First, read-only, the Keeper census against the PR's document, in the PR's branch:

```bash

si_p4_py census-check --policy clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress "$si_backup"/pods-census-*.json "$si_backup"/census-keeper-*.txt "$si_backup/census-scrape.tsv" 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/keeper-census-enforce.txt" || exit 1
```

Expected (on the PR's branch, its commit at HEAD): `clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress enforce` and every Keeper census line `admitted`. The PR: a branch of its own from a freshly fetched `origin/main` (any name but `main`; a live agent uses its task's branch name), one commit `chore(clickhouse): enforce the clickhouse-keeper-extra ingress allowlist (storage-integrity P4)` in `k8s-sea/clickhouse/network-policy.yaml` (that one document's `enableDefaultDeny.ingress: true` and every `UNCOVERED` Keeper client), `charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py` (`KEEPER_INGRESS_MODE = "enforce"`, `KEEPER_INGRESS_CLIENTS`) and, for added clients, `charts/storage-integrity/tests/si_network_probe.tsv`:

Confirm before running.

```bash
b="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" || exit 1
case "$b" in HEAD|main) echo "check out the Keeper PR's own branch first (not main, not a detached HEAD)"; exit 1 ;; esac
git fetch -q origin main || exit 1
parent="$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)" || exit 1
main="$(git rev-parse origin/main)" || exit 1
[ "$parent" = "$main" ] || { echo "the PR branch is not one commit on origin/main"; exit 1; }
state="$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" || exit 1
[ -z "$state" ] || { echo "the checkout has uncommitted changes"; exit 1; }
files="$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD)" || exit 1
[ -n "$files" ] || { echo "the Keeper PR changes no file"; exit 1; }
while IFS= read -r file; do
  case "$file" in k8s-sea/clickhouse/network-policy.yaml|charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py|charts/storage-integrity/tests/si_network_probe.tsv) ;; *) echo "the PR commit changes another file"; exit 1 ;; esac
done <<< "$files"
[ "$(si_p4_py mode clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress)" = "clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress enforce" ] || { echo "the PR commit does not enforce clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress"; exit 1; }
python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py
si_p4_commit_gate || exit 1
head="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$head" > "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-head" || exit 1
git push -u origin HEAD || exit 1
body="$(mktemp)"
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Markdown backticks, not expansions
printf '%s\n' '## Summary' '- Enforce `clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress` (k8s-sea/clickhouse/network-policy.yaml): ingress to the shared Keeper ensemble only from the `clickhouse-extra` pods, the six SI ClickHouses of devnet2-si-v2, the Keeper peers (2181, 9444) and the census clients of the storage-integrity P4 hardening runbook §2.3.' '- In observe mode since the P4 PR; the census and the probe matrix from every pod found every client admitted (docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md §8).' '- Applied after the merge with `kubectl apply` of this one document; abort: any `clickhouse-extra` Keeper session error or a new `ZSESSIONEXPIRED` in any client log within 30 minutes reverts it to observe.' '' '## Test plan' '- [x] `python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py`' '- [x] census check and probe matrix (runbook §8.2)' '' '🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)' > "$body"
gh pr create --repo sentioxyz/production --base main --title "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" --body-file "$body" | tee "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-pr"
```

Then, after review, the merge, its own confirmation:

Confirm before running.

```bash
pr="$(sed -n 's|.*/pull/\([0-9][0-9]*\).*|\1|p' "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-pr" | head -n 1)"
[ -n "$pr" ] || { echo "no PR number in keeper-enforce-pr"; exit 1; }
head="$(cat "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-head")" || exit 1
s3d_read_54_2552_0="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || exit 1
[ "${s3d_read_54_2552_0}" = "$head" ] || exit 1
si_p4_commit_gate || exit 1
si_p4_pr_gate sentioxyz/production "$pr" "$head" || exit 1
gh pr merge "$pr" --repo sentioxyz/production --squash --match-head-commit "$head" || exit 1
gh pr view "$pr" --repo sentioxyz/production --json state,mergeCommit --jq '.state + " " + .mergeCommit.oid' | tee -a "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-pr"
git fetch -q origin main && git switch --detach origin/main
```

Then the apply, which watches for 30 minutes and reverts by itself on the abort criterion: any `clickhouse-extra` Keeper session error or a new `ZSESSIONEXPIRED` in any client's log (the `clickhouse-extra` pods and the six SI ClickHouses), a Hubble `POLICY_DENIED` flow towards a Keeper replica, or a replica that loses its leader or a follower:

Confirm before running.

```bash
grep -q '^MERGED ' "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-pr" || { echo "the Keeper PR is not merged"; exit 1; }
s3d_read_54_2566_0="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || exit 1
s3d_read_54_2566_1="$(git rev-parse origin/main)" || exit 1
[ "${s3d_read_54_2566_0}" = "${s3d_read_54_2566_1}" ] || { echo "the checkout is not at origin/main"; exit 1; }
t0="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
echo "apply $t0" | tee "$si_backup/keeper-watch.txt"
abort=""
si_cnp_apply clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress enforce | tee -a "$si_backup/keeper-watch.txt" || abort="the apply was not confirmed valid"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  [ -z "$abort" ] || break
  sleep 60
  e="$(si_keeper_client_errors "$t0")" || e="the client logs could not be read"
  d="$(si_cnp_drops "$t0" | awk -F'\t' 'NR > 1 && $3 ~ /^clickhouse\/clickhouse-keeper-extra-/')" || d="Hubble could not be read"
  s="$(si_keeper_state)" || s=""
  printf '%s minute %s: errors [%s] drops [%s] %s\n' "$(si_stamp)" "$i" "$e" "$d" "$(printf '%s' "$s" | tr '\n' ' ')" | tee -a "$si_backup/keeper-watch.txt"
  printf '%s\n' "$s" > "$si_backup/keeper-state-watch.txt" || exit 1
  if [ -n "$e" ] || [ -n "$d" ] || ! si_p4_py keeper-health "$si_backup/keeper-state-watch.txt"; then abort="minute $i"; fi
done
if [ -n "$abort" ]; then
  echo "ABORT ($abort): reverting clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress to observe" | tee -a "$si_backup/keeper-watch.txt"
  si_p4_py doc clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress enforce "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-doc.yaml"
  python3 -I -c 'import sys, yaml
d = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))
d["spec"]["enableDefaultDeny"]["ingress"] = False
yaml.safe_dump(d, open(sys.argv[2], "w"), sort_keys=False)' "$si_backup/keeper-enforce-doc.yaml" "$si_backup/keeper-revert-doc.yaml"
  si_p4_observe_apply clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress "$si_backup/keeper-revert-doc.yaml" | tee -a "$si_backup/keeper-watch.txt" || { echo "ABORT rollback is unverified; reconcile before any further action" >&2; exit 1; }
  echo "reverted live; the revert PR follows §12.4"
  exit 1
fi
echo "keeper enforce held for 30 minutes" | tee -a "$si_backup/keeper-watch.txt"
```

Expected: `clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress enforce valid=True`, thirty minute lines with empty `errors` and `drops` and one `leader` with two synced followers, then `keeper enforce held for 30 minutes`. A watch that cannot read the logs, Hubble or the ensemble aborts as well: an enforce nobody can watch is reverted (`si_keeper_client_errors` fails, naming the read on stderr, when a client pod list cannot be read or is empty or a client's log cannot be read, and `si_cnp_drops` when a pod list or a Cilium agent cannot be read, so the minute line shows `errors [the client logs could not be read]` or `drops [Hubble could not be read]` and the block reverts). After an `ABORT`, the policy is in observe mode again live and `main` still says enforce: open the revert PR of §12.4 at once. Then the probes, and one write per owner (every source and every verifier needs Keeper for it), in the user's terminal:

  si_p4_accept "$key_file" c 4207 keeper

Expected: a budget line; `INTERSERVER_STEP1_END=…`, `INTERSERVER_STEP2_END=…`, `DEVNET2_FAILURE_DOMAINS=…`, any D39 sharing, the exit probe count and `HARDENING_END=<date>`. Plan S3-D Task 55 records `INTERSERVER_STEP1_END`, `INTERSERVER_STEP2_END`, `DEVNET2_FAILURE_DOMAINS` and `HARDENING_END` from this file (run record `hardening run`). `devuser1.s3_p4` stays: the owner-rebuild runbook writes to it and drops it.

## 12. Rollback

Each step reverts on its own, in reverse order, each revert one confirmed commit (`si_head_is`) and one window.

### 12.1 Interserver

Step 2 to step 1: revert the step-2 commits in reverse order (network, indexer-c, indexer-b), each through `si_p4_roll` with a new evidence name (`interserver-revert2-<installation>-commit`) after `git revert --no-edit "$(cat "$si_backup/interserver-step2-<installation>-commit")"` on a freshly fetched `origin/main`; each restart lets uncredentialed fetchers in again. Step 1 to none: revert the step-1 commits the same way, network first (the fetchers lose their credentials before the sources do, so no credentialed fetcher ever asks an uncredentialed server), then indexer-c, then indexer-b; each revert also removes that commit's node pins, which moves nothing (the `local-path` volumes keep the pods in place). The Secret stays until no installation names it; the user deletes it then.

Confirm before running.

```bash
inst='<installation>'; step='<1|2>'
case "$inst$step" in *'<'*) echo "set inst and step first"; exit 1 ;; esac
git fetch -q origin main && git switch --detach origin/main
git revert --no-edit "$(head -n 1 "$si_backup/interserver-step$step-$inst-commit")"
si_p4_roll "$inst" "interserver-revert$step-$inst-commit"
```

Then, read-only, the window check with that evidence name (same `inst` and `step`):

```bash
inst='<installation>'; step='<1|2>'
case "$inst$step" in *'<'*) echo "set inst and step first"; exit 1 ;; esac
si_p4_window_check "$inst" "interserver-revert$step-$inst-commit" "fetch-errors-$inst-revert$step.tsv" 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/window-$inst-revert$step.txt"
```

Expected: as §5.1 with the reverted credentials (`allow_empty=true` after a step-2 revert, `credentials=absent` after a step-1 revert); then the window's acceptance writes as in its section (§5.1, §5.2 or §5.3), with the value `428<k>` for the `<k>`th revert window (`k` from 1) instead of that section's value.

### 12.2 Node pins

A pin goes with its step-1 commit's revert (§12.1). A verifier moved by §5.0 is not moved back: its old volume is `Retain`ed and `Released`, and the user deletes it once the moved verifier has been healthy for a day. Never move a source ClickHouse: its `hg_safe` is the only copy of its owner's safe tables (the owner-rebuild runbook is the only way to re-create one).

### 12.3 Policies

Enforce to observe, at once and before anything else when an enforce breaks a flow: apply the observe document from the commit before the enforce commit, then revert the enforce commit on `main`:

Confirm before running.

```bash
p='<policy>'
case "$p" in *'<'*) echo "set p first"; exit 1 ;; esac
c="$(head -n 1 "$si_backup/cnp-$p-enforce-commit")"
git fetch -q origin main && git switch --detach origin/main
git show "$c~1:k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-network-policy.yaml" > "$si_backup/revert-policy-file.yaml"
python3 -I -c 'import sys, yaml
docs = [d for d in yaml.safe_load_all(open(sys.argv[1])) if d and d.get("metadata", {}).get("name") == sys.argv[2]]
assert len(docs) == 1 and docs[0]["spec"]["enableDefaultDeny"]["ingress"] is False, "no observe document"
yaml.safe_dump(docs[0], open(sys.argv[3], "w"), sort_keys=False)' "$si_backup/revert-policy-file.yaml" "$p" "$si_backup/revert-$p.yaml"
si_p4_observe_apply "$p" "$si_backup/revert-$p.yaml" || exit 1
git revert --no-edit "$c"
python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py
si_p4_commit_gate || exit 1
git push origin HEAD:main
```

Observe to absent: `si_kadmin -n sentio-network-devnet2 delete ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io <policy>` in a confirmed block of its own; nothing else changes.

### 12.4 Keeper allowlist

Enforce to observe: the abort path of §8.3 applies the observe document live; then a revert PR of the enforce PR's squash commit (`git revert`, PR, merge, each confirmed), since `main` must not say enforce while the live policy observes. Observe to absent: `si_kadmin -n clickhouse delete ciliumnetworkpolicies.cilium.io clickhouse-keeper-extra-ingress` in a confirmed block of its own, and a PR that removes the document. The egress policy `clickhouse-keeper-extra-egress` is never touched.

## 13. Operating rules

Hardening and its rollback use the direct engine-fence, staging, network and reader checks in these blocks. They never call the inherited all-role grant-corpus runners. Task53 adds phase-sensitive SNode S3 rows which those earlier runners do not automatically filter; an optional rerun of an earlier whole corpus is not a P4 gate and must not be used before the owner-rebuild restore grant is present or after that grant is withdrawn. No grant or artificial skip is introduced to fit an old runner.

These extend §11 of the stage-1, stage-2, P0, lockdown and indexer-c runbooks and the P2 runbook's §14, which stay in force.

- Every new client of an SI ClickHouse or of `clickhouse-keeper-extra` (a new si-member, job, tool or production CHI) is admitted by its policy before it first connects: a rule, its `SI_NETWORK_FLOWS` or `KEEPER_INGRESS_CLIENTS` entry and a positive probe row, in the same commit (the Keeper one through a PR). A refused flow shows as a stuck pull, a failing job or a Keeper session error, and as a Hubble `POLICY_DENIED` drop (`si_cnp_drops`).
- Apply a policy only as its one document (`si_cnp_apply`), never the whole file, and never a policy that selects a gateway or host pod.
- A new SI installation gets its own policy in observe mode first, then this runbook's §7 for it.
- The interserver Secret is read by every SI ClickHouse at its start; never edit it in place. Its rotation is a follow-up (a successor credential through `interserver_http_credentials/users`). A new SI ClickHouse is born with `allow_empty: false` and the Secret.
- Every SI ClickHouse restart keeps following the P2 runbook's restart window; the pins never change in a restart window of another change.
- Placement (D39): the three sources on pairwise distinct nodes and no verifier ClickHouse on a source's node; two verifiers share a node only while devnet2 has fewer than six eligible nodes, and move apart (§5.0) once it has six. `DEVNET2_FAILURE_DOMAINS` changes only with a source's node, which never moves outside the owner-rebuild runbook.
- Egress is not enumerated (K57): GCS needs world or FQDN rules with a DNS proxy. A dedicated SI Keeper ensemble with per-path ACLs is a follow-up (spec §14, §18).
````

Then run Step 2's check again: it now reads both files and must pass (Step 7 shows its output).

````markdown
# Storage integrity devnet2: stage 3 P4, settle and owner rebuild

This runbook rolls out the P4 settle (an operator can settle a quarantined track's issued promotions whose acknowledgement was lost: the leader streams only those, marked `settle`, to a settle-capable SNode, which answers each from its journal and never applies new state) and then drills the same-identity rebuild of indexer-c's source ClickHouse: indexer-c is quarantined and settled, a backup is taken and a dry run proves every safe part covered, the ClickHouse is lost (pod, PVC and PV), its old volume isolated and its Keeper replica fenced, a new ClickHouse is created under the same identity and signer key, `rebuild-safe` restores `hg_safe` to the arbiter's acknowledged inventory through the gate, the owner audit is clean, and a signed INSERT reaches safe on indexer-c's track again; the RTO is recorded. Design: housegate `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md`, §14 "Exits from the release refusals" and §16 row P4, as clarified by Plan S3-D (housegate `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3d-p4-settle-rebuild-hardening.md`, clarifications K51 to K54). It continues [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md) (done: `$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening/hardening-end.txt`).

| Stage | Change | Way back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | PR (P4, merged with the hardening runbook): this runbook and the chart values it turns on | Revert the PR |
| 1 | Offline replay of the voters' logs under `<ARBITER_TAG>` and `<ARBITER_TAG_P4>` (§2.1) | None needed |
| 2 | Verifiers to `<ARBITER_TAG_P4>` (§2.2) | Revert the pin (§7) |
| 3 | Hosts to sentio-node `<SN_COMMIT_P4>`: indexer-b, indexer-c, indexer-a (§2.3) | Revert each (§7) |
| 4 | Voters to `<ARBITER_TAG_P4>`, followers first, leader last (§2.4) | Replace them back (§7) |
| 5 | `GRANT READ ON S3` for `si_snode` on every SI ClickHouse (§4.1) | Revert each (§7) |
| 6 | Drill: quarantine indexer-c, settle, backup and dry run (§5.1 to §5.3) | Release (§5.10) |
| 7 | Loss: indexer-c's host at zero, its ClickHouse deleted, its old volume isolated (§5.4, §5.5) | None: the fence is one-way (§7) |
| 8 | A new ClickHouse and `rebuild-safe` (§5.6, §5.7) | Fix forward (§7) |
| 9 | Audit, rebuild values off, release, acceptance (§5.8 to §5.11) | None needed |
| 10 | End: drop `devuser1.s3_p4`, record (§6) | None needed |

Every command block is bash. Run them from the root of a production checkout at `origin/main`, in order, in one dedicated `bash` session started with `set -eo pipefail` (from fish, run `bash` first); a live agent runs each block from a block file after sourcing the §0 helpers along their chain. Every value a later block needs is written under `$si_backup`, so a block also runs in a new session once §0 is defined. Never run two stages in one window. From §2 until §6, freeze every other change to `storage-integrity-si-v2`, the three SI installations and the three host releases: no other sync or apply, no pod deletion and no consensus update outside this runbook. From §2.4 until §2.4's checks have passed, also no Raft membership change.

Every block that pushes to production `main`, syncs a release, applies, patches, labels, scales or deletes a resource, creates a Job, writes into a pod, runs DDL or writes data, or submits a quarantine, a settle or a release needs explicit user confirmation in chat before it runs; each such block is preceded by the line `Confirm before running.`. §5.4 to §5.7 are additionally one-way: the fence drops indexer-c's old Keeper replica for good and the old volume is never rebound. Never re-run a confirmed block only to see its output: a re-run repeats its writes. The read-only checks sit in blocks of their own, are safe to re-run, and `tee` their output into `$si_backup`; read that file instead. The PersistentVolume patches and labels use `si_kadmin` (the admin context `sentio-sea-admin`: PersistentVolumes are cluster-scoped and the operators' `editor` role cannot change them); every other command uses `sentio-sea`.

The user's own actions are the writes of the `devuser1` owner: a confirmed block that sets `key_file` runs in the user's own terminal (the owner key never leaves it), in a bash session started with `set -eo pipefail` and §0 defined, from the root of the same checkout and with the same `$HOME`, so it writes into the same `$si_backup`; it replaces `/path/to/devuser1-owner.key` with the key file's path there, and the read-only blocks around it run in the operator's session. Indexer-c keeps its signer key (K51): it lives in Secret `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-private-key`, survives the lost volume, and is never read, copied or rotated here. The restore key of indexer-c's host (Secret `storage-integrity-si-v2-restore-c`, keys `access-id` and `secret`) goes from its Secret into the host container's stdin for the dry run and into the init container through `secretKeyRef`; ClickHouse logins go through the lockdown runbook's helpers; nothing is printed, echoed or put on argv.

Writes in this runbook: the single-service commits of §2, §4.1, §5.7 and §5.9 and their syncs or applies; the quarantine, settles and release of indexer-c; the backup Job of §5.3; the drill's deletions (indexer-c's ClickHouse, its PVCs) and the PV patches and labels; the new ClickHouse and its `devnet2` database; `rebuild-safe`'s fence, tables, restore and journal (§5.7); indexer-a's acceptance INSERTs into `devnet101.swap_new2` through indexer-a's sidecar, values `4004` and `4005`; and the `devuser1` owner's writes through its own local agent: row `id` `4002` into the hardening runbook's `devuser1.s3_p4` (indexer-b), which §6 drops, and rows `4003` and `4001` (`4001` the drill's acceptance and the RTO's end) into indexer-c's acceptance table `<db>.s3e_e2e` (the indexer-c runbook's §8; `<db>` is the name in `$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c/acceptance-db`), each with `v` = `p4-<section>-<id>`. These values are disjoint from every earlier runbook's (the stage-3 P0 runbook's `3001` to `3004`, the indexer-c runbook's `3101`, `3102` and its `s3e_e2e` rows `1` to `3`, the lockdown runbook's `4101` to `4104`, the P1 runbook's `5101` to `5104`, the P2 runbook's `5201` to `5299`, the P3 runbook's `5301` and its `s3e_e2e` row `4`) and from the hardening runbook's `4201` to `4299`. The runbook makes 5 promotions and one table-set transition (the `DROP TABLE` of §6).

## 0. Session helpers

Define the helpers of §0 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p2-members.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p2-members.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p3-replica-reads.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p3-replica-reads.md) and [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md), unchanged and in that order (the first bash block of each §0), then these. They replace `si_backup`, so the hardening evidence stays untouched; the hardening runbook's `si_pin`, `si_indexer_c_id`, `si_kadmin`, `si_p4_accept`, `si_net_replicas`, `si_keeper_pod`, `si_cnp_modes` and `si_interserver_state` read this runbook's `si_backup` and pins from here on. The earlier helpers it calls beyond the hardening runbook's are `si_capability`, `si_replace_voter`, `si_features_tracks`, `si_voter_series`, `si_revert_stage3` and `si_login`. `si_settle_status` and `si_unacked` run `arbiter-admin indexer settle-status` in the leader's arbiter container; `si_unacked` prints the leader's preview of the promotions a settle would list (the quarantined track's issued promotions without an acknowledgement, which clarification C8 withholds), `[]` for an unquarantined track. `si_rebuild_report` keeps only the report lines of `rebuild-safe` (a JSON object with a `phase` of `fence`, `tables`, `restore`, `journal`, `plan` or `done` and no `msg`, `level`, `ts` or `time` key), so its log lines on stderr, which the container log interleaves, are dropped.

```bash
si_backup="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p4-rebuild"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the blocks of §2.1
R4="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p4-rehearsal"
si_p4_image() { printf 'ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-%s@%s\n' "$(si_pin SN_COMMIT_P4)" "$(si_pin SN_DIGEST_P4)"; } # the P4 host image (§1.1)
si_settle_status() { # $1 indexer id: the leader's GetTrackSettle (arbiter-admin indexer settle-status) as one JSON line; uint64 values are strings
  local l
  l="$(si_leader)" || { echo "no leader answers" >&2; return 1; }
  si_arbiter "$l" /usr/local/bin/arbiter-admin indexer settle-status --address "$(si_voter "$l")" --indexer "$1" | jq -c .
}
si_unacked() { # $1 indexer id: its issued, unacknowledged promotions the leader withholds while it is quarantined, as a JSON array of numbers
  si_settle_status "$1" | jq -c '(.unacked_promotion_seqs // []) | map(tonumber)'
}
si_settle_series() { # $1 voter ordinal: the settle series of that voter's /metrics (none before ARBITER_TAG_P4)
  si_voter_series "$1" 'arbiter_track_settle_active|arbiter_track_settles_total|arbiter_track_settle_sends_total'
}
si_settle_answers() { # $1 a|b|c: the settle answers that host's SNode counted, by outcome (:9091; none before the P4 image)
  local m
  case "$1" in a|b|c) ;; *) echo "usage: si_settle_answers a|b|c" >&2; return 2 ;; esac
  m="$(si_kubectl exec "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1-0" -c sentio-node -- wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9091/metrics)" || { echo "cannot read indexer-$1's :9091 metrics" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$m" | grep -E '^sentio_node_storage_integrity_settle_answers_total\{' || true
}
si_rto_mark() { # $1 step: appends "<step>\t<UTC time>\t<seconds since the epoch>" to rto-marks.tsv; a step is marked once
  local f="$si_backup/rto-marks.tsv" now stamp
  if [ -f "$f" ] && cut -f1 "$f" | grep -qx "$1"; then echo "the RTO mark $1 is recorded already" >&2; return 1; fi
  case "$1" in loss|lost|recreated|rebuilt|released|accepted) ;; *) echo "unknown RTO mark" >&2; return 2 ;; esac
  now="$(date -u +%s)" || return 1
  stamp="$(python3 -I -B -c 'from datetime import datetime, timezone; import sys; print(datetime.fromtimestamp(int(sys.argv[1]), timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))' "$now")" || return 1
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$stamp" "$now" | tee -a "$f"
}
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the in-pod script is single-quoted on purpose: it expands inside the Keeper pod
si_keeper_replicas() { # $1 Keeper table node (<database>__<table>): its replicas under the network root's unscoped unsafe path; TSV table, replica, interserver host, active
  local p
  p="$(si_keeper_pod 0)" || return 1
  kubectl --context sentio-sea -n clickhouse exec "$p" -- sh -c '
    r="/storage-integrity/devnet2/devnet2-si-v2/sentio/0/unsafe/$1"
    q() { clickhouse-keeper-client -h localhost -p 2181 -q "$1"; }
    exists() {
      answer="$(q "exists '\''$1'\''")" || return 1
      case "$answer" in 0|1) printf "%s\n" "$answer" ;; *) echo "Keeper exists returned neither literal 0 nor 1" >&2; return 1 ;; esac
    }
    children() {
      [ "$(exists "$1")" = 1 ] || { echo "required Keeper census node is missing or unreadable" >&2; return 1; }
      answer="$(q "ls '\''$1'\''")" || return 1
      for child in $answer; do
        case "$child" in ""|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) echo "malformed Keeper child name" >&2; return 1 ;; esac
      done
      printf "%s\n" "$answer"
    }
    replicas="$(children "$r/replicas")" || exit 1
    [ -n "$replicas" ] || { echo "unsafe table has no replicas" >&2; exit 1; }
    for n in $replicas; do
      [ "$(exists "$r/replicas/$n/host")" = 1 ] || exit 1
      h="$(q "get '\''$r/replicas/$n/host'\''")" || exit 1
      host="$(printf "%s\n" "$h" | sed -n "s/^host: //p")"
      case "$host" in ""|*[!A-Za-z0-9_.-]*) echo "malformed replica host" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
      active="$(exists "$r/replicas/$n/is_active")" || exit 1
      a=no; [ "$active" = 0 ] || a=yes
      printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n" "$1" "$n" "$host" "$a"
    done' sh "$1"
}
si_pv_of() { # $1 CHI: the PersistentVolumes whose claim belongs to that installation's pods, bound or released; TSV claim, volume, reclaim policy, phase, node, fenced label
  kubectl --context sentio-sea get pv -o json | jq -r --arg chi "$1" '.items[] | select(.spec.claimRef.namespace == "sentio-network-devnet2" and (.spec.claimRef.name | test("-" + $chi + "-source-0-0-0$"))) | [.spec.claimRef.name, .metadata.name, .spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy, .status.phase, (.spec.nodeAffinity.required.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0].values[0] // "-"), (.metadata.labels["storage-integrity.sentio.xyz/fenced"] // "-")] | @tsv'
}
si_rebuild_report() { # the report of indexer-c's si-rebuild-safe init container (Report.JSONLines: JSON objects with a phase and no log fields), read from its log
  local f
  f="$(mktemp)"
  si_kubectl logs sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-0 -c si-rebuild-safe > "$f" || { rm -f "$f"; return 1; }
  si_rebuild_py report "$f" || { rm -f "$f"; return 1; }
  rm -f "$f"
}
si_safe_parts_c() { # every active part of indexer-c's hg_safe as "<table>\t<partition_id>\t<hash_of_all_files>\t<rows>", sorted (the names are not compared: a rebuild gives new ones)
  si_ch_admin c "SELECT table, partition_id, hash_of_all_files, toString(rows) FROM system.parts WHERE database = 'hg_safe' AND active ORDER BY table, partition_id, hash_of_all_files FORMAT TSV"
}
si_c_snode_tables() { # the Keeper table nodes on which snode-3 holds a replica (from si_net_replicas)
  si_net_replicas | awk -F'\t' '$2 == "snode-3" {print $1}' | LC_ALL=C sort -u
}
si_rebuild_py() { # the report, part, partition-state, RTO, schedule and backup-index checks
  python3 -I -B - "$@" <<'PY'
import json
import sys
import re
import math
import hashlib
import os
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

PHASES = ("fence", "tables", "restore", "journal", "plan", "done")
LOG_KEYS = ("msg", "level", "ts", "time")


def die(msg):
    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def report_lines(path):
    out = []
    for line in open(path):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line.startswith("{"):
            continue
        try:
            obj = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError:
            die("malformed JSON in rebuild output; stop instead of omitting evidence")
        if isinstance(obj, dict) and not any(k in obj for k in LOG_KEYS):
            if obj.get("phase") not in PHASES:
                die("unrecognized non-log JSON object in rebuild output")
            out.append(obj)
    return out


def cmd_report(args):
    for obj in report_lines(args[0]):
        print(json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":")))


def integer(v, field):
    if type(v) is not int or v < 0 or v > 18446744073709551615:
        die(f"{field}: expected a nonnegative uint64 integer")
    return v


def nonempty(v, field):
    if not isinstance(v, str) or not v or any(c in v for c in "\t\n\r"):
        die(f"{field}: expected a nonempty single-line string")
    return v


def cmd_check_report(args):
    path, mode = args[0], args[1]
    if mode not in ("dry", "run"):
        die("mode is dry or run")
    keeper = args[2] if len(args) > 2 and args[2] != "-" else None
    lines = report_lines(path)
    if not lines or lines[-1]["phase"] != "done" or sum(l["phase"] == "done" for l in lines) != 1:
        die(f"{path}: expected exactly one final done line")
    done = lines[-1]
    if type(done.get("dry_run")) is not bool or done["dry_run"] != (mode == "dry"):
        die("report dry_run does not match the requested execution mode")
    if type(done.get("already_rebuilt")) is not bool or (mode == "dry" and done["already_rebuilt"]):
        die("invalid already_rebuilt flag")
    phase = "plan" if mode == "dry" else "restore"
    allowed = {phase, "done"} | ({"fence"} if mode == "run" else set())
    if any(l["phase"] not in allowed for l in lines):
        die("report contains a phase incompatible with the requested execution mode")
    parts = [l for l in lines if l["phase"] == phase]
    seen, tables = set(), set()
    totals = dict.fromkeys(("parts", "from_own_unsafe", "from_object_store", "missing"), 0)
    for row in parts:
        key = (nonempty(row.get("table_id"), "table_id"), nonempty(row.get("partition_id"), "partition_id"))
        if key in seen:
            die(f"duplicate partition report {key}")
        seen.add(key)
        tables.add(key[0])
        integer(row.get("publish_seq"), "publish_seq")
        nonempty(row.get("root"), "root")
        missing = row.get("missing")
        if not isinstance(missing, list) or any(not isinstance(v, str) or not v for v in missing) or len(missing) != len(set(missing)):
            die("invalid missing-parts list")
        for k in ("parts", "from_own_unsafe", "from_object_store"):
            totals[k] += integer(row.get(k), k)
        covered = row["from_own_unsafe"] + row["from_object_store"] + len(missing)
        if covered > row["parts"] or (mode == "dry" and covered != row["parts"]):
            die("partition source counts contradict the dry/full-plan or run/needed-fetch contract")
        totals["missing"] += len(missing)
    if totals["missing"]:
        die("report contains uncovered parts")
    for k, expected in dict(totals, tables=len(tables), partitions=len(parts)).items():
        if integer(done.get(k), "done." + k) != expected:
            die(f"done.{k} disagrees with partition rows")
    if not parts:
        die("the report has no owned partitions; stop and investigate the drill target")
    if len(args) > 3:
        baseline = {key: (value[0], value[1], len(value[2])) for key, value in partstates(args[3]).items() if value[2]}
        actual = {(row["table_id"], row["partition_id"]): (row["publish_seq"], row["root"], row["parts"]) for row in parts}
        if not baseline or actual != baseline:
            die("report partition identities, publish sequences, roots or part counts differ from the frozen nonempty SafeParts baseline")
    fence = [l for l in lines if l["phase"] == "fence"]
    fenced_tables = set()
    for row in fence:
        table = nonempty(row.get("table_id"), "fence.table_id")
        nonempty(row.get("path"), "fence.path")
        if table in fenced_tables or type(row.get("present")) is not bool or type(row.get("dropped")) is not bool:
            die("duplicate or malformed fence result")
        if row["dropped"] and not row["present"]:
            die("an absent replica cannot have been dropped")
        fenced_tables.add(table)
    if done["already_rebuilt"] and (fence or totals["from_own_unsafe"] or totals["from_object_store"]):
        die("an already-rebuilt report must not claim a fence or newly fetched parts")
    if keeper and not done["already_rebuilt"]:
        rows = [r.split("\t") for r in open(keeper).read().splitlines()[1:] if r.strip()]
        if any(len(r) != 4 for r in rows):
            die("malformed pre-rebuild Keeper replica census")
        tables = sorted({r[0] for r in rows if r[1] == "snode-3"})
        dropped = sorted(row["path"].rstrip("/").rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for row in fence if row["dropped"])
        if tables != dropped:
            die(f"fence dropped {dropped}, but Keeper listed snode-3 on {tables}")
    if mode == "dry":
        print(f"dry run: {len(parts)} partitions planned, every part covered")
    elif done["already_rebuilt"]:
        print("rebuild: already rebuilt, nothing written; this report does not re-prove a historical fence")
    else:
        print(f"rebuild: {len(fence)} fence lines, {sum(row['dropped'] for row in fence)} stale replicas dropped, {len(parts)} partitions restored, {totals['from_own_unsafe']} parts from the own hg_unsafe replica, {totals['from_object_store']} from the object store")


def checked_init(value):
    if not isinstance(value, dict) or type(value.get("exit_code")) is not int or value["exit_code"] != 0:
        die("init proof must show the actual rebuild init container exited zero")
    for field in ("pod_uid", "container_id", "started_at", "finished_at"):
        nonempty(value.get(field), "init." + field)
    try:
        start = datetime.fromisoformat(value["started_at"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        end = datetime.fromisoformat(value["finished_at"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if start.tzinfo is None or end.tzinfo is None or end < start:
            raise ValueError("unordered or naive init timestamps")
    except ValueError:
        die("invalid init proof timestamps")
    return value


def cmd_fence_receipt(args):
    if len(args) != 7:
        die("fence-receipt report keeper-before baseline backup-name init-proof owner-id output-dir")
    report, keeper, baseline, backup_file, init_file, owner, output = args
    if re.fullmatch(r"0|[1-9][0-9]*", owner) is None:
        die("receipt owner must be a canonical uint64")
    owner = integer(int(owner), "receipt owner")
    backup = Path(backup_file).read_text().strip()
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*", backup) is None:
        die("invalid receipt backup name")
    init = checked_init(json.loads(Path(init_file).read_text()))
    cmd_check_report([report, "run", keeper, baseline])
    current = report_lines(report)[-1]
    directory = Path(output)
    if not directory.is_dir():
        die("receipt directory must already exist")
    archive, receipt = directory / "rebuild-first-fence.jsonl", directory / "rebuild-first-fence.receipt.json"
    digest = lambda path: hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    bindings = {"format": "si-p4-first-fence-v1", "owner_indexer_id": owner, "backup": backup,
                "keeper_before_sha256": digest(keeper), "baseline_sha256": digest(baseline)}
    if archive.exists() != receipt.exists() or archive.is_symlink() or receipt.is_symlink():
        die("partial or nonregular prior fence custody; reconcile without replacing it")
    if archive.exists():
        old = json.loads(receipt.read_text())
        if not isinstance(old, dict) or type(old.get("owner_indexer_id")) is not int or any(old.get(k) != value for k, value in bindings.items()) or old.get("report_sha256") != digest(archive):
            die("prior fence receipt bindings or source hash differ")
        checked_init(old.get("init"))
        if report_lines(archive)[-1].get("already_rebuilt") is not False:
            die("a prior already-rebuilt result cannot establish the first fence")
        cmd_check_report([str(archive), "run", keeper, baseline])
        if not current["already_rebuilt"] and digest(report) != digest(archive):
            die("a different normal rebuild report cannot overwrite first-fence custody")
    else:
        if current["already_rebuilt"]:
            die("already-rebuilt lacks independent prior successful first-fence custody; reconcile before recording")
        bindings.update(report_sha256=digest(report), init=init)
        # Never overwrite an earlier attempt. A crash leaving a partial pair is an explicit stop above.
        for path, content in ((archive, Path(report).read_bytes()), (receipt, (json.dumps(bindings, indent=2) + "\n").encode())):
            fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                handle.write(content)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    print("first-fence receipt verified; owner, backup, init exit, report, Keeper and baseline custody retained")


def cmd_restore_grants(args):
    def snapshot(path):
        rows = []
        for line in open(path):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            row = json.loads(line)
            fields = ("user_name", "access_type", "access_object", "database", "table", "column", "is_partial_revoke", "grant_option")
            if not isinstance(row, dict) or any(k not in row for k in fields):
                die("incomplete eight-field admin grant row")
            if not isinstance(row["user_name"], str) or not row["user_name"].startswith("si_") or not isinstance(row["access_type"], str):
                die("unexpected grant role/type")
            for k in ("access_object", "database", "table", "column"):
                if row[k] is not None and not isinstance(row[k], str):
                    die("invalid nullable grant scope")
            for k in ("is_partial_revoke", "grant_option"):
                if type(row[k]) is not int or row[k] not in (0, 1):
                    die("invalid grant flags")
            rows.append(tuple(row[k] if k != "access_object" else row[k] or "" for k in fields))
        if not rows or len(rows) != len(set(rows)) or not {"si_snode", "si_backup"} <= {r[0] for r in rows}:
            die("empty/duplicate/incomplete baseline grant snapshot")
        return set(rows)
    before, after = map(snapshot, args)
    added = ("si_snode", "READ", "S3", None, None, None, 0, 0)
    if added in before or after != before | {added}:
        die("restore-grant change is not exactly one si_snode READ ON S3 row; every other stored row must remain")
    print("si_snode READ ON S3 added; every other eight-field admin grant row unchanged")


def multiset(path):
    rows = [l.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for l in open(path) if l.strip()]
    out = {}
    for r in rows:
        if len(r) != 4 or any(not value for value in r[:3]) or re.fullmatch(r"0|[1-9][0-9]*", r[3]) is None:
            die(f"{path}: malformed four-field part row")
        integer(int(r[3]), "part.rows")
        key = tuple(r)
        out[key] = out.get(key, 0) + 1
    if not out:
        die(f"{path}: empty safe-parts snapshot")
    return out


def cmd_parts_diff(args):
    before, after = multiset(args[0]), multiset(args[1])
    if before == after:
        print(f"hg_safe equal by (table, partition, hash_of_all_files, rows): {sum(before.values())} parts")
        return
    for k in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
        if before.get(k, 0) != after.get(k, 0):
            print(f"differs {k}: before {before.get(k, 0)}, after {after.get(k, 0)}")
    sys.exit(1)


def partstates(path):
    out = {}
    for line in open(path):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        r = json.loads(line)
        key = (nonempty(r.get("table_id"), "table_id"), nonempty(r.get("partition_id"), "partition_id"))
        if key in out:
            die(f"{path}: duplicate partition state {key}")
        seqs = [integer(r.get(k), k) for k in ("publish_seq", "last_acked_promotion_seq", "unacked_promotion_seq")]
        parts = r.get("safe_parts")
        if parts is None:
            parts = []
        if not isinstance(parts, list) or any(not isinstance(v, str) or not v for v in parts) or len(parts) != len(set(parts)):
            die("invalid safe_parts")
        out[key] = (seqs[0], nonempty(r.get("base_partition_root"), "base_partition_root"), sorted(parts), seqs[1], seqs[2])
    if not out:
        die(f"{path}: empty partition-state snapshot")
    return out


def cmd_partstates_diff(args):
    before, after = partstates(args[0]), partstates(args[1])
    if before == after:
        print(f"partition states equal: {len(before)} partitions, none unacknowledged" if all(v[4] == 0 for v in after.values()) else f"partition states equal: {len(before)} partitions")
        return
    for k in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
        if before.get(k) != after.get(k):
            print(f"differs {k}: before {before.get(k)}, after {after.get(k)}")
    sys.exit(1)


def cmd_rto(args):
    marks = {}
    previous = -1
    for line in open(args[0]):
        cols = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        if len(cols) != 3 or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", cols[0]) or cols[0] in marks or not re.fullmatch(r"0|[1-9][0-9]*", cols[2]):
            die("malformed or duplicate RTO mark")
        epoch = int(cols[2])
        try:
            stamp = datetime.strptime(cols[1], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        except ValueError:
            die("RTO mark needs an exact UTC timestamp")
        if int(stamp.timestamp()) != epoch or epoch < previous:
            die("RTO mark timestamp/epoch mismatch or clock moved backwards")
        marks[cols[0]] = epoch
        previous = epoch
    if "loss" not in marks or "accepted" not in marks or next(iter(marks)) != "loss" or next(reversed(marks)) != "accepted":
        die("RTO marks must start at loss and finish at accepted")
    for k, v in marks.items():
        print(f"{k}\t+{v - marks['loss']} s")
    print(f"P4_REBUILD_RTO={marks['accepted'] - marks['loss']}")


def cmd_next_run(args):
    fields = args[0].split()
    if len(fields) != 5 or fields[2:] != ["*", "*", "*"] or not fields[0].isdigit() or not fields[1].isdigit():
        die(f"schedule {args[0]!r} is not the daily 'M H * * *' form this runbook reads")
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    if not 0 <= int(fields[0]) < 60 or not 0 <= int(fields[1]) < 24:
        die("daily backup hour/minute is out of range")
    if len(args) > 1 and (not math.isfinite(float(args[1])) or float(args[1]) <= 0):
        die("backup budget must be finite and positive")
    run = now.replace(hour=int(fields[1]), minute=int(fields[0]), second=0, microsecond=0)
    if run <= now:
        run += timedelta(days=1)
    print(f"next scheduled backup {run.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')}, in {(run - now).total_seconds() / 3600:.1f} h")
    if len(args) > 1 and (run - now).total_seconds() < float(args[1]) * 3600:
        die(f"the next scheduled backup is less than {args[1]} h away")


def cmd_backup(args):
    path = args[0]
    if not re.fullmatch(r"0|[1-9][0-9]*", args[1]):
        die("owner must be a canonical uint64")
    owner = integer(int(args[1]), "owner")
    idx = None
    for line in open(path):
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("{"):
            obj = json.loads(line)
            if obj.get("format") == "si-backup-index-v1":
                if idx is not None:
                    die("multiple backup index records")
                idx = obj
    if idx is None:
        die(f"{path} holds no si-backup-index-v1 line")
    if integer(idx.get("owner_indexer_id"), "owner_indexer_id") != owner:
        die(f"the backup is of indexer {idx.get('owner_indexer_id')}, not {owner}")
    if not isinstance(idx.get("tables"), list) or not idx["tables"]:
        die("the backup lists no table")
    if not isinstance(idx.get("name"), str) or re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*", idx["name"]) is None:
        die("invalid backup name")
    if idx.get("kind") not in ("full", "incr") or integer(idx.get("chain_length"), "chain_length") < 1:
        die("invalid backup kind/chain length")
    nonempty(idx.get("snapshot_id"), "snapshot_id")
    entry = idx.get("entry")
    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        die("backup lacks the frozen entry")
    safe = integer(entry.get("safe_block_seq"), "entry.safe_block_seq")
    integer(entry.get("applied_promotion_seq"), "entry.applied_promotion_seq")
    if len(args) != 4 or not re.fullmatch(r"0|[1-9][0-9]*", args[3]) or safe != integer(int(args[3]), "quarantined published seq"):
        die("backup entry does not match the measured quarantined published frontier")
    table_ids, physical = set(), set()
    for table in idx["tables"]:
        if not isinstance(table, dict):
            die("invalid backup table")
        tid = nonempty(table.get("table_id"), "backup.table_id")
        pname = nonempty(table.get("physical_table"), "backup.physical_table")
        if tid in table_ids or pname in physical:
            die("duplicate backup table identity")
        table_ids.add(tid)
        physical.add(pname)
        integer(table.get("incarnation_seq"), "backup.incarnation_seq")
        parts = table.get("parts")
        if not isinstance(parts, list):
            die("invalid backup parts")
        seen = set()
        for part in parts:
            if not isinstance(part, dict):
                die("invalid backup part")
            key = (nonempty(part.get("partition_id"), "backup.partition_id"), nonempty(part.get("name"), "backup.part.name"))
            if key in seen:
                die("duplicate backup part")
            seen.add(key)
            nonempty(part.get("phys_hash"), "backup.phys_hash")
            integer(part.get("rows"), "backup.rows")
    print(f"backup {idx['name']} kind {idx['kind']} chain {idx['chain_length']} snapshot {idx['snapshot_id']} entry safe_block_seq {entry.get('safe_block_seq')} applied_promotion_seq {entry.get('applied_promotion_seq')} tables {len(idx['tables'])} parts {sum(len(t.get('parts') or []) for t in idx['tables'])}")
    print(idx["name"], file=open(args[2], "w"))


COMMANDS = {"fence-receipt": cmd_fence_receipt, "restore-grants": cmd_restore_grants, "report": cmd_report, "check-report": cmd_check_report, "parts-diff": cmd_parts_diff, "partstates-diff": cmd_partstates_diff, "rto": cmd_rto, "next-run": cmd_next_run, "backup": cmd_backup}
if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] not in COMMANDS:
    die("usage: si_rebuild_py " + "|".join(COMMANDS) + " ...")
COMMANDS[sys.argv[1]](sys.argv[2:])
PY
}
```

## 1. Preparation

### 1.1 Pins and identities

Create the evidence directory once, fresh, and record the pins (PR-time values from Plan S3-D's ledger copy):

```bash
[ ! -e "$si_backup" ] || { echo "$si_backup exists: move it aside; this runbook's evidence starts in a fresh directory"; exit 1; }
ARBITER_TAG_P4='<ARBITER_TAG_P4>'; ARBITER_DIGEST_P4='<ARBITER_DIGEST_P4>'; CORE_TAG_P4='<CORE_TAG_P4>'; PROTO_TAG_P4='<PROTO_TAG_P4>'; SN_COMMIT_P4='<SN_COMMIT_P4>'; SN_DIGEST_P4='<SN_DIGEST_P4>'; HG_TAG_P3='<HG_TAG_P3>'
ARBITER_TAG='<ARBITER_TAG>'; ARBITER_DIGEST='<ARBITER_DIGEST>'; SN_COMMIT_P3='<SN_COMMIT_P3>'; SN_DIGEST_P3='<SN_DIGEST_P3>'
INDEXER_C_ID='<INDEXER_C_ID>'; INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE='<INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE>'; INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE='<INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE>'; UNSAFE_INC_ROOT='<UNSAFE_INC_ROOT>'; P1_END='<P1_END>'

for p in "arbiter:$ARBITER_TAG_P4 $ARBITER_DIGEST_P4" "arbiter:$ARBITER_TAG $ARBITER_DIGEST" "sentio-node:sha-$SN_COMMIT_P4 $SN_DIGEST_P4" "sentio-node:sha-$SN_COMMIT_P3 $SN_DIGEST_P3"; do
  read -r ref digest <<< "$p"

done
for f in "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening/hardening-end.txt" "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c/acceptance-db" "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p0/tools/partstates" "$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-s3a-rehearsal/statedigest/main.go" "$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-s3a-rehearsal/v20check/main.go" "$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-s3a-rehearsal/snapdump/main.go"; do
  [ -s "$f" ] || { echo "$f is missing: the earlier runbooks are not done on this machine; stop"; exit 1; }
done
grep -q '^HARDENING_END=' "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening/hardening-end.txt" || { echo "the hardening runbook has not ended; stop"; exit 1; }
python3 -I -B - "$SN_COMMIT_P4" "$SN_DIGEST_P4" "$ARBITER_DIGEST_P4" <<'EOF'

sys.path.insert(0, "charts/storage-integrity/tests")

assert t.DEVNET2_REBUILD_SAFE == {r: None for r in t.DEVNET2_REBUILD_SAFE} and not any(t.DEVNET2_SNODE_RESTORE_GRANT.values()), "a rebuild or a restore grant is on already"

EOF

printf '%s\n' "ARBITER_TAG_P4=$ARBITER_TAG_P4" "ARBITER_DIGEST_P4=$ARBITER_DIGEST_P4" "CORE_TAG_P4=$CORE_TAG_P4" "PROTO_TAG_P4=$PROTO_TAG_P4" "SN_COMMIT_P4=$SN_COMMIT_P4" "SN_DIGEST_P4=$SN_DIGEST_P4" "HG_TAG_P3=$HG_TAG_P3" "ARBITER_TAG=$ARBITER_TAG" "ARBITER_DIGEST=$ARBITER_DIGEST" "SN_COMMIT_P3=$SN_COMMIT_P3" "SN_DIGEST_P3=$SN_DIGEST_P3" "INDEXER_C_ID=$INDEXER_C_ID" "INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE=$INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE" "INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE=$INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE" "UNSAFE_INC_ROOT=$UNSAFE_INC_ROOT" "P1_END=$P1_END" "ARBITER_REPO=$arbiter_repo" > "$si_backup/pins"

| indexer-c | SI indexer `<INDEXER_C_ID>`, SNode `snode-3`, release `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c` (host pod `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-0` on `<INDEXER_C_HOST_NODE>`, its si-member `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-member-0`), signer key Secret `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-private-key` (never read) |

| Its backups | CronJob `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-backup` (Plan S3-C1), prefix `owner-<INDEXER_C_ID>/` of the replica bucket, P1 since `<P1_END>`; the read-only restore key `storage-integrity-si-v2-restore-c` |
| SNode journal | `/data/storage-integrity-devnet2-si-v2/snode` on the host's own PVC, which the drill keeps (K52) |

### 1.2 Preconditions

- The hardening runbook is done; every track is unquarantined; every host's owner audit is clean in repair mode.
- Indexer-c's ClickHouse holds no table outside the protocol databases (`hg_safe`, `hg_unsafe`, `hg_promote`) and the member databases (`hg_replica`, `hg_rstage`, `hg_member_unsafe`): the drill loses everything on it, and `rebuild-safe` and the si-member restore only those. Its other databases (the indexer-c runbook's `devnet2`, `Atomic`) are empty; `databases-c.tsv` records them, and §5.6 creates them again.

```bash
db_c="$(cat "$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c/acceptance-db")"
{
  si_show | jq -c '{epoch, promotion_seq, max_writers: .current.max_writers, si_indexers: [.current.si_indexers[] | {indexer_id, snode_node_id}], verifiers: [.current.verifiers[].node_id]}'
  si_tracks | jq -c '[.indexers[] | {id: .indexer_id, published: .published.safe_block_seq, generation: .quarantine_generation, quarantined, rejected: .rejected_blocks}]'
  si_images
  for i in 0 1 2; do si_capability "$i"; done
  for x in a b c; do printf 'indexer-%s %s\n' "$x" "$(si_node_image "$x")"; si_audit "$x" | grep -E 'owner_audit_(mode|unclean_tables)'; done
  si_cnp_modes
  for inst in network indexer-b indexer-c; do si_interserver_state "$inst"; done
  si_ch_admin c "SELECT database, name, engine, total_rows FROM system.tables WHERE database NOT IN ('system', 'INFORMATION_SCHEMA', 'information_schema', 'hg_safe', 'hg_unsafe', 'hg_promote', 'hg_replica', 'hg_rstage', 'hg_member_unsafe') ORDER BY database, name FORMAT TSV"
  si_ch_admin c "SELECT name, engine FROM system.databases WHERE name NOT IN ('system', 'INFORMATION_SCHEMA', 'information_schema', 'default', 'hg_safe', 'hg_unsafe', 'hg_promote', 'hg_replica', 'hg_rstage', 'hg_member_unsafe') ORDER BY name FORMAT TSV" | tee "$si_backup/databases-c.tsv"
  si_status c "$db_c" s3e_e2e
  si_status b devuser1 s3_p4
  printf 'restore key: %s\n' "$(si_secret_keys storage-integrity-si-v2-restore-c)"
  si_kubectl get cronjob sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-backup -o jsonpath='{.spec.schedule} suspend={.spec.suspend} last={.status.lastScheduleTime} success={.status.lastSuccessfulTime}{"\n"}'
  si_kubectl get jobs -l app.kubernetes.io/component=si-backup -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} active={.status.active} succeeded={.status.succeeded}{"\n"}{end}'
  si_unsafe_inc
  for v in "patch persistentvolumes" "patch pods/ephemeralcontainers -n sentio-network-devnet2"; do
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    printf '%s: %s\n' "$v" "$(si_kadmin auth can-i $v)"
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/preconditions.txt"
```

Expected: `max_writers` `"3"`, the three entries, `verifier-1..3`; every track unquarantined with no rejected block; all six arbiter pods on `<ARBITER_DIGEST>`, all three hosts on `sha-<SN_COMMIT_P3>@<SN_DIGEST_P3>`, every audit repair and `unclean_tables 0`; the four policies `enforce valid=True`; six pods `allow_empty=false password=set`; no table row from indexer-c's ClickHouse (a table is data the drill would destroy: stop and ask the user); the database rows `devnet2	Atomic` and any other empty database with its engine, each `Atomic` or `Ordinary` (another engine: stop and ask the user); `<db>.s3e_e2e` and `devuser1.s3_p4` both `active`; the restore key's keys `access-id secret `; the backup CronJob not suspended with a recent success and no active Job; an empty `unsafe_inc` listing; `yes` twice.
````
