## 2. Settle rollout

Every component of the settle can return to its previous image (§7): the RPCs are leader-local and never proposed, the SNode's settle answer and the leader's settle stream are read only by each other, and no consensus format changes (Plan S3-D contract §33.1).

### 2.1 Offline replay check

Plan S3-A Task 11's throwaway tools (`statedigest`, `v20check`, `snapdump`; sources in `$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-s3a-rehearsal`) restore a copy of each voter's `raft` directory into one arbiter build: `old` is the voters' live release `<ARBITER_TAG>`, `new` is `<ARBITER_TAG_P4>`. Identical lines and an identical written container prove on devnet2's own log that the release changes no consensus byte. The binaries are built into `$R4`, never reused (local only):

```bash
[ ! -e "$R4" ] || { echo "$R4 exists: move it aside; a rehearsal directory is never reused"; exit 1; }
S3A="$HOME/si-devnet2-multisource-s3a-rehearsal"; arbiter_repo="$(si_pin ARBITER_REPO)"
mkdir -m 700 "$R4"
git -C "$arbiter_repo" fetch -q --tags origin
for build in "old $(si_pin ARBITER_TAG)" "new $(si_pin ARBITER_TAG_P4)"; do
  b="${build%% *}"; tag="${build#* }"; src="$R4/src/$b"
  mkdir -p "$src" "$R4/bin/$b"
  git -C "$arbiter_repo" archive "$tag" | tar -x -C "$src"
  for tool in statedigest v20check snapdump; do mkdir -p "$src/cmd/$tool" && cp "$S3A/$tool/main.go" "$src/cmd/$tool/main.go"; done
  (cd "$src" && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3+auto GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false go build -o "$R4/bin/$b/" ./cmd/statedigest ./cmd/v20check ./cmd/snapdump)
done
si_pin ARBITER_TAG > "$R4/old_tag.txt"
ls "$R4/bin/old" "$R4/bin/new"
```

Expected: both directories list `snapdump`, `statedigest` and `v20check`. Then the baseline, read-only: every voter runs one image, the published digest of `<ARBITER_TAG>`:

```bash
{
  old_tag="$(cat "$R4/old_tag.txt")"
  live="$(si_images | awk '$1 ~ /^storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-/ {sub(/.*@/, "", $3); print $3}' | sort -u)"
  echo "old_tag $old_tag; voters run $live"
  [ -n "$live" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$live" | wc -l)" -eq 1 ] || { echo "the voters do not run exactly one image; stop"; exit 1; }
  [ "$live" = "$(si_pin ARBITER_DIGEST)" ] || { echo "the voters run $live, not $(si_pin ARBITER_DIGEST); stop"; exit 1; }
  printf '%s %s %s\n' "$old_tag" "$live" "$R4/bin" > "$si_backup/replay-baseline"
  echo "old matches the voters' live release $old_tag"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/replay-baseline.txt"
```

Expected: `old matches the voters' live release <ARBITER_TAG>`. Then the replay of fresh copies of all three voters, local CPU only (the replay loads each voter's `arbiter.yaml` with `config.Load`, which needs `anchor.evm.private_key_hex`, so a throwaway random key is exported; the replay signs nothing):

```bash
{
  read -r base_tag base_digest bin < "$si_backup/replay-baseline" || { echo "run the baseline check first"; exit 1; }
  [ "$(si_images | awk '$1 ~ /^storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-/ {sub(/.*@/, "", $3); print $3}' | sort -u)" = "$base_digest" ] || { echo "the voters no longer run $base_digest ($base_tag): rerun the baseline"; exit 1; }
  ARBITER_ANCHOR_EVM_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"; export ARBITER_ANCHOR_EVM_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX
  si_show | tee "$si_backup/show-replay.json" | jq -c '{epoch, params_digest, promotion_seq}'
  for i in 0 1 2; do
    si_kubectl exec "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-$i" -c arbiter -- tar -C /data -czf - raft > "$si_backup/arbiter-$i-raft.tgz"
    si_kubectl exec "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-$i" -c arbiter -- cat /config/arbiter.yaml > "$si_backup/arbiter-$i.yaml"
    work="$(mktemp -d)"
    tar -C "$work" -xzf "$si_backup/arbiter-$i-raft.tgz"
    for v in old new; do
      out="$si_backup/digest-$i-$v"
      "$bin/$v/statedigest" -data-dir "$work/raft" -config "$si_backup/arbiter-$i.yaml" > "$out.txt" 2> "$out.err" || { echo "statedigest $v failed for arbiter-$i (a raft.db that fails to open is a torn copy; re-copy):"; cat "$out.err"; exit 1; }
      grep -E '^(snapshot_index|last_index|applied_commands|rejected_commands|written_version|genesis_configured|live_check|apply_error|apply_rejected|key|spent_ids|snapshot_sha256)' "$out.txt" > "$out.cmp"
      if grep -q '^apply_error ' "$out.txt"; then echo "arbiter-$i $v: apply_error"; exit 1; fi
      "$bin/$v/snapdump" -data-dir "$work/raft" -config "$si_backup/arbiter-$i.yaml" -out "$si_backup/written-$i-$v.container" || { echo "snapdump $v failed for arbiter-$i"; exit 1; }
    done
    if cmp -s "$si_backup/digest-$i-old.cmp" "$si_backup/digest-$i-new.cmp"; then echo "arbiter-$i: old and new replay identically"; else echo "arbiter-$i: DIFFERENT; stop"; diff "$si_backup/digest-$i-old.cmp" "$si_backup/digest-$i-new.cmp"; exit 1; fi
    cmp -s "$si_backup/written-$i-old.container" "$si_backup/written-$i-new.container" || { echo "arbiter-$i: the containers differ; stop"; exit 1; }
    echo "arbiter-$i: both builds write the same v20 container"
    "$bin/old/v20check" "$si_backup/written-$i-new.container"
    "$bin/new/v20check" "$si_backup/written-$i-old.container"
    grep -E '^(applied_commands|written_version|live_check)' "$si_backup/digest-$i-new.txt"
    rm -rf "$work"
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/replay.txt"
```

Expected, for each voter: `old and new replay identically`, `both builds write the same v20 container`, `restore_ok version 20` twice, `applied_commands` above zero, `written_version 20` and the `live_check` lines naming epoch and `promotion_seq` of `show-replay.json` (or a later sequence if a promotion landed between the read and the copy); no `apply_error`. Any difference: stop before §2.2.

## 3. Settle

The settle is the exit from release refusal (iii) of the stage-2 runbook (§11 there): a quarantined track's promotions that were issued and never acknowledged are not re-sent (clarification C8), so `release of indexer <n> refused: rejected statement <s> of block <b> is covered by unacknowledged promotion <p>` could never clear. `arbiter-admin indexer settle` signs, with the authority key every voter carries (`ARBITER_AUTHORITY_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX`), `{indexer_id, expected_generation, promotion_seqs}` (purpose `arbiter-settle-track-v1`), where the list is exactly the leader's preview; the leader then re-signs and streams only those promotions, marked `settle`, every orchestrator pass, only to the track's SNode and only while its subscription advertised `settle`. The SNode answers each from durable state only: its journaled acknowledgement (`journaled`), a published promotion intent finished (`reconciled`), otherwise a journaled `Applied:false` with detail `settle: promotion <seq> was not applied on this SNode` (`not_applied`, which consumes the promotion), or nothing for a sequence below its watermark with no stored acknowledgement (`unanswerable`); it never builds a shadow, runs `REPLACE` or writes `hg_safe`. The settle ends `settled` once every listed promotion is acknowledged, `released` on a release or a generation change, `expired` after `--settle-timeout` (at most `consensus_admin.max_track_settle`, 10m) and `leadership_lost` on a leader change; the CLI exits 0 only for `settled`. Nothing of it is written to the Raft log; the acknowledgements it brings are ordinary ones.

The successful Task51 CLI stdout is exactly six fields: `indexer_id`, `expected_generation`, `promotion_seqs`, `state`, `unacked_promotion_seqs` and `sends`. Every uint64 is a canonical decimal string (including list elements), and `state` is `TRACK_SETTLE_STATE_SETTLED`; compare the indexer and generation with the signed attempt. Raft term, expiry and SNode identity are checked inside its polling loop and are not invented stdout fields.

The reviewed Task51 CLI binds its wait to the original returned indexer, Raft term, expiry, promotion list and SNode identity; `SETTLED` must also match the signed quarantine generation. It refuses a different attempt rather than accepting that attempt's success. `--settle-timeout` must be at least 1ms and no more than the configured maximum. Expiry is refreshed before sends and terminal transitions; the process-local attempt token is not a new wire or consensus field. A timed-out, released, leadership-lost or mismatched wait is a failure and requires a fresh read instead of an automatic retry.

### 3.1 Read the track

Read-only, with `indexer` set to the track's indexer id:

```bash
indexer='<indexer id>'
case "$indexer" in *'<'*) echo "set indexer first"; exit 1 ;; esac
{
  si_track "$indexer"
  si_settle_status "$indexer"
  printf 'unacked: %s\n' "$(si_unacked "$indexer")"
  for i in 0 1 2; do si_settle_series "$i"; done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/settle-read-$indexer.txt"
```

Expected for a track that needs a settle: `quarantined` `true`, its `generation`, and a non-empty `unacked` list. An unquarantined track never needs one: its promotions are streamed anyway, and the CLI refuses with `indexer <n> is not quarantined: nothing to settle`; an empty list refuses with `indexer <n> has no issued, unacknowledged promotion: nothing to settle`.

### 3.2 Settle

With `indexer` and `n` (the settle's number in this runbook, from 1) set; the generation is read right before signing, and after an unknown outcome read §3.1 again instead of retrying:

Confirm before running.

```bash
indexer='<indexer id>'; n='<n>'
case "$indexer$n" in *'<'*) echo "set indexer and n first"; exit 1 ;; esac
[ ! -e "$si_backup/settle-$n.json" ] || { echo "settle $n ran already; never re-run this block"; exit 1; }
x=""; case "$indexer" in 0) x=a ;; 1) x=b ;; "$(si_indexer_c_id)") x=c ;; esac
[ -n "$x" ] || { echo "indexer $indexer is not an SI indexer of devnet2"; exit 1; }
g="$(si_track "$indexer" | jq -r .generation)"
si_settle_answers "$x" > "$si_backup/settle-$n-answers-before.txt"
leader="$(si_leader)"
si_arbiter "$leader" /usr/local/bin/arbiter-admin indexer settle --address "$(si_voter "$leader")" --indexer "$indexer" --expected-generation "$g" --settle-timeout 10m --timeout 15m > "$si_backup/settle-$n.json" 2> "$si_backup/settle-$n.err" || { cat "$si_backup/settle-$n.err" "$si_backup/settle-$n.json"; echo "the settle did not end settled; read §3.1"; exit 1; }
jq -c . "$si_backup/settle-$n.json"
```

Then, read-only:

```bash
indexer='<indexer id>'; n='<n>'
case "$indexer$n" in *'<'*) echo "set indexer and n first"; exit 1 ;; esac
x=""; case "$indexer" in 0) x=a ;; 1) x=b ;; "$(si_indexer_c_id)") x=c ;; esac
{
  jq -c '{state, promotion_seqs, unacked_promotion_seqs, sends}' "$si_backup/settle-$n.json"
  printf 'unacked now: %s\n' "$(si_unacked "$indexer")"
  si_settle_status "$indexer"
  cat "$si_backup/settle-$n-answers-before.txt"; si_settle_answers "$x"
  for i in 0 1 2; do si_settle_series "$i"; done
  si_track "$indexer"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/settle-$n-checks.txt"
```

Expected: `state` `TRACK_SETTLE_STATE_SETTLED`, `promotion_seqs` the §3.1 list, `unacked_promotion_seqs` empty and a nonnegative `sends` count; `unacked now: []`; the SNode answer counters observed across `journaled`, `reconciled` and `not_applied` (an `unanswerable` answer leaves its promotion unacknowledged: the settle then ends `expired` and the CLI fails); the leader's `arbiter_track_settles_total{state="settled"}` observed after the settle (absent before the first); counters may include retries, concurrent work or a late ordinary acknowledgement and are diagnostic, not proof that this exact attempt settled; the track still quarantined, its generation unchanged. A `not_applied` answer means the SNode never applied that promotion: the arbiter records `Applied:false`, the promotion is consumed, and its rows were never promoted.

### 3.3 Release after a settle

With refusal (iii) gone, the release acknowledges exactly the rejected blocks the track lists (none after a manual quarantine). Refusal (ii) (`… has promoted parts`) can follow a settle whose promotion had applied: it never clears (the subtractive revert is v22), and the indexer stays quarantined. With `indexer` set:

Confirm before running.

```bash
indexer='<indexer id>'
case "$indexer" in *'<'*) echo "set indexer first"; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$(si_track "$indexer" | jq -r .quarantined)" = true ] || { echo "indexer $indexer is not quarantined; stop"; exit 1; }
[ "$(si_unacked "$indexer")" = "[]" ] || { echo "indexer $indexer still has unacknowledged promotions: settle first (§3.2)"; exit 1; }
g="$(si_track "$indexer" | jq -r .generation)"
ack=()
for b in $(si_track "$indexer" | jq -r '.rejected[]?'); do ack+=(--acknowledge-rejected "$b"); done
leader="$(si_leader)"
si_arbiter "$leader" /usr/local/bin/arbiter-admin indexer release --address "$(si_voter "$leader")" --indexer "$indexer" --expected-generation "$g" "${ack[@]}" --timeout 20s 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/release-$indexer.json"
```

Expected: the committed answer (`"outcome": "committed"`) naming every rejected block it acknowledged. A refusal: `release-<indexer>.json` holds it; (ii) means the track stays quarantined, recorded, never forced.

## 4. Rebuild preparation

### 4.1 Restore grant

`rebuild-safe` restores scratch tables in `hg_promote` from the object store as `si_snode`, which needs `GRANT READ ON S3` (the host's existing login; no new user, K52). One commit per installation, indexer-b, then indexer-c, then the network, as every P4 change moves (the grant is the same on every SI ClickHouse, so a later rebuild of indexer-b finds it in place; indexer-a, whose genesis tables are host configuration, is not rebuilt this way: `rebuild-safe rebuilds only an indexer without genesis tables`); each is a users reload, no restart: for indexer-b and indexer-c `GRANT READ ON S3` appended to `si_snode`'s `grants/query` in the CHI manifest, for the network `clickhouse.access.snodeRestoreGrant: true` in the overlay, each with `DEVNET2_SNODE_RESTORE_GRANT["<the installation's CHI>"] = True`. With `inst` set to `indexer-b`, then `indexer-c`, then `network`, each in its own confirmed run:

Confirm before running.

```bash
inst=indexer-b
ev="$si_backup/restore-grant-$inst-commit"
[ ! -e "$ev" ] || { echo "$inst's grant commit was pushed already; never re-run this block"; exit 1; }
file="$(si_p4_manifest "$inst")"; chi="$(si_chi_of "$inst")"
si_head_is "$file" charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py
python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py
if [ "$inst" = network ]; then
  [ "$(si_render_diff storage-integrity-si-v2)" = "changed ClickHouseInstallation/storage-integrity-si-v2" ] || { echo "the release renders more than the CHI differently"; exit 1; }
else
  si_kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f "$file" > /dev/null
fi
si_chi_state "$chi" > "$ev.before" || exit 1
hosts="$(si_hosts_of "$inst")" || exit 1
for h in $hosts; do si_grants "$h" > "$ev.grants-$h.before.jsonl" || exit 1; done
git rev-parse HEAD > "$ev" || exit 1
si_p4_commit_gate || exit 1
git push origin HEAD:main
if [ "$inst" = network ]; then helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml sync --selector name=storage-integrity-si-v2; else si_kubectl apply -f "$file"; fi
si_wait_chi "$chi"
```

Then, read-only, with the same `inst`:

```bash
inst=indexer-b
ev="$si_backup/restore-grant-$inst-commit"
h="$(si_owner_of "$inst")"
{
  si_chi_state "$(si_chi_of "$inst")" > "$ev.after"
  if diff <(grep '^pod ' "$ev.before") <(grep '^pod ' "$ev.after"); then echo "no pod restarted"; else echo "a pod RESTARTED: stop and explain it"; exit 1; fi
  for _ in $(seq 1 30); do [ -n "$(si_ch_admin "$h" "SELECT 1 FROM system.grants WHERE user_name = 'si_snode' AND access_type = 'READ' AND access_object = 'S3'")" ] && break; sleep 10; done
  si_ch_admin "$h" "SELECT user_name, access_type, access_object FROM system.grants WHERE user_name = 'si_snode' AND access_type = 'READ' FORMAT TSV"
  hosts="$(si_hosts_of "$inst")" || exit 1
  for h in $hosts; do
    si_grants "$h" > "$ev.grants-$h.after.jsonl" || exit 1
    si_rebuild_py restore-grants "$ev.grants-$h.before.jsonl" "$ev.grants-$h.after.jsonl" || exit 1
    if out="$(si_ch_exec "$h" si_snode "SELECT * FROM s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/si-p4-probe/p4.csv', 'CSV', 'a String') LIMIT 0" 2>&1)"; then
      [ -z "$out" ] || { echo "the explicit-structure LIMIT0 probe returned unexpected output" >&2; exit 1; }
      echo "READ ON S3: the s3() read exited 0 (no rows) on $h"
    else
      echo "READ ON S3 direct probe failed on $h; no nonzero code establishes this gate" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/restore-grant-$inst.txt"
```

Expected: `no pod restarted`; exactly one new `si_snode READ S3` row on every ClickHouse host of the installation, with every other eight-field stored admin grant row unchanged (including the legitimate backup WRITE row, reader metadata and member grants); and `READ ON S3: the s3() read exited 0 (no rows) on <host>` (the explicit-structure, two-path-segment `LIMIT 0` success probe; the separate RawBLOB corpus row tests an access boundary and is not this success oracle). `Code: 497`: the grant has not reloaded yet or is missing, read `system.grants` again; any other code: stop and read the answer.

### 4.2 RTO marks

The RTO runs from the loss (§5.4's mark `loss`) to the first signed INSERT on indexer-c's track that reaches safe after the release (§5.11's mark `accepted`); `si_rto_mark` records each step once in `rto-marks.tsv`, and `P4_REBUILD_RTO` is the difference in seconds. The drill's window from §5.4 to §5.11 must end before indexer-c's next scheduled backup: a backup Job that ran against the lost or the half-rebuilt ClickHouse reads only, but its index would not describe the arbiter's state, so §5.4 refuses to start with less than 8 hours left. Read-only:

```bash
{
  s="$(si_kubectl get cronjob sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-backup -o jsonpath='{.spec.schedule}')"
  echo "schedule $s (UTC)"
  si_rebuild_py next-run "$s"
  [ -e "$si_backup/rto-marks.tsv" ] && cat "$si_backup/rto-marks.tsv" || echo "no RTO mark yet"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/rto-window.txt"
```

Expected: the schedule (`17 4 * * *` for indexer-c), the next run and the hours left, and `no RTO mark yet`.

## 5. Rebuild drill

### 5.1 Quarantine

Indexer-c is quarantined first: a live track's `hg_safe` is never rebuilt (`rebuild: indexer <n> is not quarantined; a live track's hg_safe is never rebuilt`). While it is quarantined its host refuses its tables (392), the members of indexer-a and indexer-b may serve them (P3), and indexer-a's and indexer-b's tracks carry on.

Confirm before running.

```bash
id="$(si_indexer_c_id)"
[ "$(si_track "$id" | jq -r .quarantined)" = false ] || { echo "indexer $id is already quarantined; stop"; exit 1; }
g="$(si_track "$id" | jq -r .generation)"
leader="$(si_leader)"
si_arbiter "$leader" /usr/local/bin/arbiter-admin indexer quarantine --address "$(si_voter "$leader")" \
  --indexer "$id" --expected-generation "$g" --reason "devnet2 stage-3 P4 owner-rebuild runbook §5.1: rebuild drill of indexer-c" --timeout 20s 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/quarantine.json"
```

Then, read-only:

```bash
id="$(si_indexer_c_id)"
{
  sleep 10
  si_track "$id"
  si_info c
  si_settle_status "$id"
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/verify-quarantine.txt"
```

Expected: the committed answer; the track `quarantined` `true` with its generation one higher; `si_info c` `"quarantined":true`; `settle-status` with `quarantined` `true`.

### 5.2 Settle

Read-only, the promotions the leader withholds:

```bash
si_unacked "$(si_indexer_c_id)" | tee "$si_backup/unacked-drill.json"
```

Expected: `[]` normally (nothing was in flight). A non-empty list: run §3.2 with `indexer` = `<INDEXER_C_ID>` and `n=1` and its check block now, then this block again until it prints `[]`; `rebuild-safe` refuses otherwise (`rebuild: indexer <n> has issued, unacknowledged promotions …; settle them first (arbiter-admin indexer settle)`).

### 5.3 Backup and dry run

With the track quarantined and settled, `hg_safe` equals the arbiter's `SafeParts`: the audit is clean and no promotion or cleanup runs any more. First the state before the loss, read-only:

```bash
id="$(si_indexer_c_id)"
{
  [ "$(cat "$si_backup/unacked-drill.json")" = "[]" ] || { echo "settle first (§5.2)"; exit 1; }
  si_audit c | grep -E 'unclean_tables|runs_total'
  si_partstates_run -indexer "$id" > "$si_backup/partstates-c-before.jsonl"
  wc -l < "$si_backup/partstates-c-before.jsonl"
  si_safe_parts_c > "$si_backup/safe-parts-c-before.tsv"
  wc -l < "$si_backup/safe-parts-c-before.tsv"
  si_c_snode_tables | tee "$si_backup/snode-3-tables.txt"
  si_kubectl get jobs -l app.kubernetes.io/component=si-backup -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} active={.status.active}{"\n"}{end}'
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/before-loss.txt"
```

Expected: `unclean_tables 0`; one partition-state line per promoted partition of indexer-c (with `unacked_promotion_seq` 0) and as many `hg_safe` parts; the Keeper table nodes on which `snode-3` holds a replica (every table indexer-c owns); no active backup Job. Then the backup, through Plan S3-C1's CronJob:

Confirm before running.

```bash
id="$(si_indexer_c_id)"
track="$(si_track "$id")" || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$track" | jq -e '.quarantined == true' > /dev/null || exit 1
published="$(printf '%s\n' "$track" | jq -r '.published.safe_block_seq')" || exit 1
case "$published" in ""|*[!0-9]*) echo "no measured quarantined published frontier" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
printf '%s\n' "$published" > "$si_backup/backup-published-seq" || exit 1
j=sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-backup-p4-rebuild
if si_kubectl get job "$j" > /dev/null 2>&1; then echo "job $j exists: this backup ran; never re-run this block"; exit 1; fi
si_kubectl create job --from=cronjob/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-backup "$j"
st=""
for _ in $(seq 1 360); do
  st="$(si_kubectl get job "$j" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}/{.status.failed}')" || st=""
  case "$st" in 1/*|*/1) break ;; esac
  sleep 10
done
si_kubectl logs "job/$j" > "$si_backup/backup-c-p4.json"
case "$st" in 1/*) ;; *) tail -n 20 "$si_backup/backup-c-p4.json"; echo "the backup job did not succeed (succeeded/failed: ${st:-unknown}); stop"; exit 1 ;; esac
si_rebuild_py backup "$si_backup/backup-c-p4.json" "$id" "$si_backup/backup-name.txt" "$published" || exit 1
cat "$si_backup/backup-name.txt"
```

Expected: one line naming the backup (`<YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ>-incr` or `-full`), its chain, snapshot, entry (`safe_block_seq` equal to indexer-c's published frontier in `verify-quarantine.txt`), tables and parts; then the name. Then the dry run inside the running host, a write into the pod's `/tmp` only: `rebuild-safe` reads the object store named by `storage_integrity.backup`, which the host's own config does not carry, so the block builds a config beside it with that block added (the bucket of indexer-c's backup ConfigMap), pipes the restore key from its Secret into the container's stdin, runs `--dry-run` and removes the file:

Confirm before running.

```bash
id="$(si_indexer_c_id)"; name="$(cat "$si_backup/backup-name.txt")"
[ ! -e "$si_backup/dry-run.jsonl" ] || { echo "the dry run ran already; never re-run this block"; exit 1; }
bucket="$(si_kubectl get configmap sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-backup -o 'jsonpath={.data.config\.yaml}' | python3 -I -c 'import sys, yaml; print(yaml.safe_load(sys.stdin)["storage_integrity"]["backup"]["bucket_url"])')"
[ -n "$bucket" ] && [ -n "$name" ] || { echo "no bucket or backup name"; exit 1; }
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the in-pod script is single-quoted on purpose: it expands inside the host container
{ si_kubectl get secret storage-integrity-si-v2-restore-c -o 'jsonpath={.data.access-id}' | base64 -d; echo; si_kubectl get secret storage-integrity-si-v2-restore-c -o 'jsonpath={.data.secret}' | base64 -d; echo; } |
  si_kubectl exec -i sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-0 -c sentio-node -- sh -c '
    IFS= read -r STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID; IFS= read -r STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    export STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    [ -n "$STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID" ] && [ -n "$STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" ] || { echo "the restore key arrived empty" >&2; exit 2; }
    for tool in awk grep; do command -v "$tool" > /dev/null || { echo "the host container has no $tool" >&2; exit 2; }; done
    [ "$(grep -c "^storage_integrity:$" /config/standalone.yaml)" = 1 ] || { echo "/config/standalone.yaml has no single top-level storage_integrity block" >&2; exit 2; }
    cfg=/tmp/si-rebuild-dry-run.yaml
    if grep -q "^  backup:$" /config/standalone.yaml; then cp /config/standalone.yaml "$cfg"; else
      awk -v id="$1" -v bucket="$2" '"'"'{print} /^storage_integrity:$/ && !done {print "  backup:"; print "    bucket_url: \"" bucket "\""; print "    owner_indexer_id: " id; done = 1}'"'"' /config/standalone.yaml > "$cfg"
    fi
    grep -q "^  backup:$" "$cfg" || { echo "no storage_integrity block in /config/standalone.yaml" >&2; rm -f "$cfg"; exit 2; }
    rc=0; /sentio-node storage-integrity rebuild-safe --config-path "$cfg" --backup "$3" --dry-run || rc=$?
    rm -f "$cfg"; exit "$rc"' sh "$id" "$bucket" "$name" > "$si_backup/dry-run.jsonl" 2> "$si_backup/dry-run.err" || { tail -n 20 "$si_backup/dry-run.err"; echo "the dry run failed: nothing is destroyed; stop"; exit 1; }
si_rebuild_py check-report "$si_backup/dry-run.jsonl" dry - "$si_backup/partstates-c-before.jsonl"
```

Expected: exit 0 and `dry run: <n> partitions planned, every part covered`, `<n>` the count of baseline partitions with nonempty `safe_parts` in `partstates-c-before.jsonl`; `dry-run.jsonl` ends with its `done` line. A failure (`rebuild: no source holds part …`, a refused key, a missing grant): stop; nothing is destroyed, release with §5.10.

### 5.4 Loss

From here the drill is one-way. The RTO starts. The block refuses unless the dry run passed and the next scheduled backup is at least 8 hours away; then it stops indexer-c's host and its si-member, keeps every volume of the old ClickHouse (`Retain`) and deletes the ClickHouse (its pods and StatefulSet; the operator keeps its PVCs):

Confirm before running.

```bash
si_rebuild_py check-report "$si_backup/dry-run.jsonl" dry - "$si_backup/partstates-c-before.jsonl" > /dev/null || { echo "no passing dry run (§5.3)"; exit 1; }
si_rebuild_py next-run "$(si_kubectl get cronjob sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-backup -o jsonpath='{.spec.schedule}')" 8
[ ! -e "$si_backup/pv-before.txt" ] || { echo "the loss ran already; never re-run this block"; exit 1; }
si_pv_of storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c | tee "$si_backup/pv-before.txt"
[ "$(grep -c . "$si_backup/pv-before.txt")" = 3 ] || { echo "indexer-c's ClickHouse does not hold three volumes; stop"; exit 1; }
si_rto_mark loss
si_kubectl scale statefulset sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c --replicas=0
si_kubectl scale statefulset sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-member --replicas=0
si_kubectl wait --for=delete pod/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-0 --timeout=10m
si_kubectl wait --for=delete pod/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-member-0 --timeout=10m
cut -f2 "$si_backup/pv-before.txt" | while read -r pv; do si_kadmin patch pv "$pv" -p '{"spec":{"persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy":"Retain"}}'; done
si_pv_of storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c | cut -f2,3 | tee "$si_backup/pv-retain.txt"
si_kubectl delete chi storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c --wait
si_kubectl wait --for=delete pod/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source-0-0-0 --timeout=10m
si_rto_mark lost
```

Expected: three volumes (data, log, member), each `Retain` after the patch; the host, its si-member and the ClickHouse gone; the marks `loss` and `lost`.

### 5.5 Isolate the old volume

The old volumes are labelled fenced and their claims deleted, so they stay `Released` with their data and are never rebound (their `claimRef` names the deleted claims):

Confirm before running.

```bash
[ ! -e "$si_backup/pv-fenced.txt" ] || { echo "the volumes were isolated already; never re-run this block"; exit 1; }
cut -f2 "$si_backup/pv-before.txt" | while read -r pv; do si_kadmin label pv "$pv" storage-integrity.sentio.xyz/fenced=true; done
si_kubectl delete pvc -l clickhouse.altinity.com/chi=storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c --wait
sleep 5
si_pv_of storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c | tee "$si_backup/pv-fenced.txt"
```

Expected: the three volumes `Retain`, `Released`, on `<INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE>`, fenced `true`. Then, read-only, until the old server's Keeper session has expired (`session_timeout_ms` 100000) and `snode-3` is inactive on every table:

```bash
{
  for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
    : > "$si_backup/keeper-before.txt.new"
    printf 'table\treplica\thost\tactive\n' >> "$si_backup/keeper-before.txt.new"
    while read -r t; do si_keeper_replicas "$t" >> "$si_backup/keeper-before.txt.new"; done < "$si_backup/snode-3-tables.txt"
    awk -F'\t' 'NR > 1 && $2 == "snode-3" && $4 == "yes"' "$si_backup/keeper-before.txt.new" | grep -q . || break
    sleep 10
  done
  mv "$si_backup/keeper-before.txt.new" "$si_backup/keeper-before.txt"
  awk -F'\t' 'NR > 1 {print $2, $4}' "$si_backup/keeper-before.txt" | LC_ALL=C sort | uniq -c
  si_unsafe_inc
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/keeper-fence-ready.txt"
```

Expected: `snode-3 no` on every table of `snode-3-tables.txt`, `verifier-1..3 yes` on each; an empty `unsafe_inc` listing (`rebuild-safe`'s fence refuses otherwise). `snode-3 yes` after 5 minutes: the old server is not dead (its pod or node still runs it); stop and find it before anything else (`fence: replica snode-3 of … is active`).

### 5.6 Re-create the ClickHouse

The CHI is applied again unchanged from `origin/main`: it is born with every hardening setting (interserver credentials with `allow_empty` false, the node pin, posture C, the P2 bundle, the restore grant), and its pod is selected by its enforced policy at once. The lockdown runbook's lock record `locked-indexer-c` stays, so `si_ch_admin c` sends the admin password, which the re-created `default` requires. Then, as admin, every database of `databases-c.tsv` with its engine (the indexer-c runbook's §4 created `devnet2` the first time); the protocol databases come with `rebuild-safe`'s tables and the member databases with the si-member:

Confirm before running.

```bash
if si_kubectl get chi storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c > /dev/null 2>&1; then echo "the installation exists: this block ran; never re-run it"; exit 1; fi
[ -s "$si_backup/pv-fenced.txt" ] || { echo "isolate the old volumes first (§5.5)"; exit 1; }
f=k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source.yaml
si_kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f "$f" > /dev/null
si_kubectl apply -f "$f"
until si_kubectl get pod storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source-0-0-0 > /dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 5; done
si_kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-source-0-0-0 --timeout=15m
si_wait_chi storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c
while IFS=$'\t' read -r name engine <&3 || [ -n "$name" ]; do
  [ -n "$name" ] || continue
  case "$engine" in Atomic|Ordinary) ;; *) echo "database $name has engine '$engine' in databases-c.tsv: stop"; exit 1 ;; esac
  case "$name" in *[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) echo "database name '$name' is not a plain identifier: stop"; exit 1 ;; esac
  si_ch_admin c "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS \`$name\` ENGINE = $engine"
done 3< "$si_backup/databases-c.tsv"
si_rto_mark recreated
```

  si_login c si_snode

  si_cnp_mode storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-c-clickhouse-ingress
  si_ch_admin c "SELECT name FROM system.zookeeper WHERE path = '/sentio/0/unsafe' ORDER BY name FORMAT TSV" | wc -l

### 5.7 Rebuild

One commit `chore(devnet2): rebuild-safe for indexer-c from backup <name> (P4 drill)` in `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/sentio-node-indexer-c-storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml` and `charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py`: under `storageIntegrity.snode`

The sync renders the init container `si-rebuild-safe` before every container of the host pod (the P4 image's `storage-integrity rebuild-safe --config-path <the node config> --backup <name>`, as `si_snode` with the restore key from its Secret and the host's own `PRIVATE_KEY` reference, which it needs to read its indexer id, and the host's `/data` and `/config`; the node config gains `storage_integrity.backup` from the release's `siBackup` values while `rebuildSafe` is on) and brings the host and its si-member back to one replica each. The init container is the journal's only writer while it runs: phase `fence` (for every table indexer-c owns: `snode-3`'s replica absent or inactive, then `SYSTEM DROP REPLICA 'snode-3' FROM ZKPATH`; the scoped root empty), `tables` (every owned incarnation created, each new `hg_unsafe` replica cloned from the verifiers until its queue is empty), `restore` (per partition, the gate's plan against the arbiter's `SafeParts`, each needed part from the own `hg_unsafe` replica, else the backup, its `hash_of_all_files` equal to the arbiter's, attached into `hg_safe`, closure over the base root), `journal` (the rebuilt inventories, marked `rebuilt`, at the arbiter's `PublishSeq`).

### 5.8 Audit

The restored `hg_safe` meets the owner audit by hash, not by name: each partition's local inventory is marked `rebuilt` at the arbiter's `PublishSeq` and is the reference exactly when its multiset of (row LtHash, `hash_of_all_files`) equals the arbiter's `SafeParts`. Read-only:

```bash
id="$(si_indexer_c_id)"
{
  si_audit c | tee "$si_backup/audit-c-rebuild.txt"
  si_partstates_run -indexer "$id" > "$si_backup/partstates-c-rebuild.jsonl"
  si_rebuild_py partstates-diff "$si_backup/partstates-c-before.jsonl" "$si_backup/partstates-c-rebuild.jsonl"
  si_safe_parts_c > "$si_backup/safe-parts-c-after.tsv"
  si_rebuild_py parts-diff "$si_backup/safe-parts-c-before.tsv" "$si_backup/safe-parts-c-after.tsv"
  while read -r t; do si_keeper_replicas "$t"; done < "$si_backup/snode-3-tables.txt" | awk -F'\t' '{print $2, $4}' | LC_ALL=C sort | uniq -c
  si_info c
  si_settle_answers c
  si_kubectl get pod sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c-si-member-0 -o jsonpath='{.status.phase} {.status.containerStatuses[0].ready}{"\n"}'
} 2>&1 | tee "$si_backup/audit-c-checks.txt"
```

Expected: `owner_audit_unclean_tables 0` with `runs_total{trigger="startup"}` at least 1 and `fsm_unavailable_total` unchanged; `partition states equal: <n> partitions, none unacknowledged` (the FSM did not move during the quarantine); `hg_safe equal by (table, partition, hash_of_all_files, rows): <m> parts` (the names differ: a rebuild cannot reproduce them, K52); `snode-3 yes` and `verifier-1..3 yes` on every table; `quarantined:true` still; the settle answers unchanged; the si-member `Running true` (its audit re-installs its copies into the new ClickHouse). An unclean table (`the rebuilt inventory of promotion <p> differs from the arbiter's by row hash or hash_of_all_files`): stop; the track stays quarantined.

The fenced volumes' directories on `<INDEXER_C_CHI_NODE>` stay until the user deletes them, after `P4_END`; no agent deletes them.

## 7. Rollback

- Verifiers and voters: revert `stage3-p4-verifiers-commit` (`si_revert_stage3 stage3-p4-verifiers-commit storage-integrity-si-v2 statefulset/storage-integrity-si-v2-verifier`, confirmed), then replace the voters as §2.4 (followers first). `<ARBITER_TAG>` reads the v20 snapshots `<ARBITER_TAG_P4>` writes (§2.1 proved both ways); a settle active at the change ends `leadership_lost`.
- Hosts: revert each host's commit in reverse order (indexer-a, indexer-c, indexer-b) with `si_revert_stage3 stage3-p4-indexer-<x>-commit sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-<x> statefulset/sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-<x>`, each confirmed. An older SNode advertises no `settle`, so the leader never sends it one (`SettleTrack` refuses: `the SNode … is not connected with settle support`). Never take indexer-c's host back after §5.7 until §5.11's promotion has replaced the rebuilt reference: an older owner audit compares names and would hold its tables.
- Restore grant: revert each `restore-grant-<installation>-commit` (a users reload), confirmed; it is needed only while a rebuild runs.
- Before §5.4 the drill reverts by §5.10 (release); the backup and the dry run wrote nothing a release has to undo.
- From §5.4 on there is no way back to the old ClickHouse: its Keeper replica is dropped by the fence and its volume is fenced. Fix forward: a failed `rebuild-safe` leaves the host in its init container and the track quarantined (its members serve its databases, P3); read the refusal: `ErrRebuildSourceMissing` (a part no source holds: a member-copy source is a follow-up), `ErrRebuildPhysHashMismatch` (a source returned other bytes), `ErrRebuildClosure` or `ErrRebuildForeignSafeParts` (the new `hg_safe` is not empty or not ours: drop it as admin and run again), `ErrRebuildJournalBehind` (the host's journal is behind the arbiter: a journal rebuilt from the arbiter is a follow-up), `ErrFenceReplicaActive` or `ErrFenceScopedReplica` (the old server is alive or a scoped replica exists: find it). A second run is idempotent: turn `rebuildSafe` off and on again with the same backup (two commits), or delete the host pod to restart the init container (confirmed).
- The fenced volumes are never rebound and never deleted by an agent.

## 8. Operating rules

The mandatory P4 blocks and their rollback helpers do not call the inherited all-role corpus runners `si_grant_probe`, `si_p1s_grant_probe` or `si_p2s_grant_probe`. Their definitions are retained unchanged only as part of the D20 helper chain. Task53 adds two phase-sensitive SNode S3 rows; the older runners do not automatically filter them. Do not rerun those earlier whole corpora as a P4 prerequisite or rollback acceptance before the restore grant is present or after it is withdrawn. The P4 restore-grant gate is the exact eight-field admin delta plus the direct exit-0 probe in §4.1; no permission is enabled to make an earlier corpus pass. RebuildSafe must be off before withdrawing its restore grant.

These extend §11 of the stage-1, stage-2, P0, lockdown and indexer-c runbooks, the P2 runbook's §14 and the hardening runbook's §13, which stay in force.

- Settle: only a quarantined track with issued, unacknowledged promotions needs one (§3), and only through `arbiter-admin indexer settle`, which signs the leader's preview; never hand-build the list. A settle before a release clears refusal (iii); refusal (ii) never clears and the indexer stays quarantined. A settle needs the track's SNode on `<SN_COMMIT_P4>` or later and the leader on `<ARBITER_TAG_P4>` or later; `expired` means an answer was missing (an `unanswerable` promotion or a disconnected SNode): read §3.1 and the SNode's log before a second settle.
- Rebuild: only of an indexer without genesis tables (indexer-b or indexer-c on devnet2), only of a quarantined, settled track; a backup taken after the quarantine and a passing dry run before anything is destroyed; the old volume isolated (`Retain`, `Released`, fenced) and the Keeper session expired before `rebuild-safe`; `rebuildSafe` on only for the rebuild and off before the release; the window from the loss to the acceptance ends before the owner's next scheduled backup. The host's PVC (the SNode journal) must survive: a lost host PVC cannot be rebuilt this way (follow-up).
- The fenced PV of a rebuild stays `Released`; only the user deletes its directory, after the run's record.
- Restarts: a host restart with `rebuildSafe` on runs `rebuild-safe` again (idempotent while quarantined, refused once released); every SI ClickHouse restart follows the P2 runbook's restart window.
- The signer key of a rebuilt indexer is kept (K51); a signer rotation that keeps the indexer id needs a registry change and is not part of P4.
````

The release counts the block as passed and schedules the cleanup of its candidate parts on that indexer's SNode.
-- Some release refusals never clear (arbiter `v0.12.0` README, "Rejected blocks"). A release that acknowledges a rejected block is refused while a Rejected statement of it has no bound result claim, has promoted parts, or is covered by a promotion that was issued and not acknowledged: `release of indexer <n> refused: rejected statement <s> of block <b> has no result claim`, `… has promoted parts`, `… is covered by unacknowledged promotion <p>`. A missing claim can still arrive, and a pending promotion can still be acknowledged, which clears the refusal; but promoted parts, and a promotion whose delivery or acknowledgement was lost before the verdict (a quarantined track's promotions are not re-sent), never clear. The indexer then stays quarantined: there is no way back inside the protocol, and rebuilding its safe tables out of band does not lift the refusal.
+- Some release refusals never clear (arbiter `v0.12.0` README, "Rejected blocks"). A release that acknowledges a rejected block is refused while a Rejected statement of it has no bound result claim, has promoted parts, or is covered by a promotion that was issued and not acknowledged: `release of indexer <n> refused: rejected statement <s> of block <b> has no result claim`, `… has promoted parts`, `… is covered by unacknowledged promotion <p>`. A missing claim can still arrive, and a pending promotion can still be acknowledged, which clears the refusal; but promoted parts, and a promotion whose delivery or acknowledgement was lost before the verdict (a quarantined track's promotions are not re-sent), never clear. The indexer then stays quarantined: there is no way back inside the protocol, and rebuilding its safe tables out of band does not lift the refusal. Since stage 3 P4 the lost acknowledgement clears: a settle (`arbiter-admin indexer settle`, [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-owner-rebuild.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-owner-rebuild.md) §3) streams a quarantined track's issued, unacknowledged promotions again to its SNode, which answers each from its journal, and the release is then tried again (§3.3 there); promoted parts still never clear.
 - A stuck rejected-part cleanup holds every consensus update. From a release that acknowledged rejected blocks on, each rejected partition of that indexer counts in the drain gate until its SNode acknowledges the cleanup, and every update meanwhile is refused with `consensus update requires all rejected-part cleanups to be acknowledged`. The acknowledgement never comes while the source SNode is down or evicted, when the SNode refuses the cleanup (for example a part whose row LtHash differs from the one it recorded at intake, a table it does not own, or a mixed command), or when the SNode misbehaves. Signal: after its release the indexer stays in the table registry's `quarantined_indexers`, so its host keeps answering `"quarantined":true` (`si_info`) and refusing its tables although `si_track` shows `quarantined: false`, and `arbiter_track_rejected_partitions{indexer_id}` stays above 0 (`si_track_metrics`; the arbiter README's alert `ArbiterRejectedCleanupStuck`, which this repository does not deploy). Remedy: quarantine the indexer again (§8.1). The drain gate skips a quarantined indexer's work, so consensus updates pass again, while its rejected partitions stay recorded and its host keeps refusing its tables; once the cause is fixed, a later release (acknowledging only blocks rejected since, usually none) re-dispatches the same cleanups, re-signed, and the indexer leaves `quarantined_indexers` with the last acknowledgement.
 - Before any authority rotation, every SNode's overlay must list the new authority in `storageIntegrity.snode.authorityAddresses`, synced and restarted: SNodes authorize promotions and cleanups against that static list, with no epoch, so work suspended by a quarantine and re-sent after the rotation, signed by the new authority, is refused otherwise (arbiter stage-2 plan C12).
 - The leader groups submissions by owner within its submission grouping window (`ingress.submission_grouping_window`, binary default 50 ms); the chart exposes no value for it, and `test_render.py` keeps it that way. Each statement waits on the leader up to the window before it is proposed, so INSERT latency rises by up to 50 ms and a client with one statement in flight at a time is capped near 20 statements per second (§6.4 measures it against the §4.1 baseline); the voters run Raft with group commit (`BatchApplyCh`) since `v0.12.0`, so one window's statements reach the log in a few batches. A shorter window, or `0`, needs a chart value of its own, in its own reviewed change.
```

```python
"""Writes the §0 helper chains of the two stage-3 P4 runbooks (Plan S3-D Task 54; local, never committed).

usage: python3 -I build_chain.py <out-dir>, from the root of the production checkout.

Each runbook's §0 says: define the helpers of §0 of the earlier runbooks, unchanged and in that order (the
first bash block of each §0), then its own. This writes exactly that, one file per P4 runbook:
<out-dir>/chain-hardening.bash and <out-dir>/chain-owner-rebuild.bash.
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

EARLIER = [
    "dynamic-table-set", "multi-source", "multi-source-tracks", "stage3-p0", "stage3-lockdown", "stage3-indexer-c",
    "stage3-p1-backups", "stage3-p2-members", "stage3-p3-replica-reads",
]


def helper_block(name):
    path = pathlib.Path(f"docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-{name}.md")
    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    start = lines.index("## 0. Session helpers")
    end = next((i for i in range(start + 1, len(lines)) if re.match(r"## \d+\. ", lines[i])), len(lines))
    for i in range(start, end):
        if lines[i] == "```bash":
            j = lines.index("```", i + 1)
            return f"# --- the first bash block of §0 of {path}\n" + "\n".join(lines[i + 1:j]) + "\n"
    sys.exit(f"{path}: §0 holds no bash block")


out = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
chain = [helper_block(n) for n in EARLIER]
hardening = helper_block("stage3-p4-hardening")
rebuild = helper_block("stage3-p4-owner-rebuild")
(out / "chain-hardening.bash").write_text("".join(chain) + hardening)
(out / "chain-owner-rebuild.bash").write_text("".join(chain) + hardening + rebuild)
print(f"chain-hardening.bash: {len(EARLIER) + 1} helper blocks; chain-owner-rebuild.bash: {len(EARLIER) + 2} helper blocks; in {out}")
```

    assert any(l.startswith("admitted ") and w in l for l in got), ("not admitted", w)
for w in uncovered:
    assert any(l.startswith("UNCOVERED ") and w in l for l in got), ("not refused", w)
assert got[-1] == f"census: {len(admitted)} admitted, {len(uncovered)} uncovered or unattributed", got[-1]
print(f"ok synthetic census: {len(admitted)} flows admitted, the DinD pod and a stray Keeper client uncovered")

# 8. The §8.3 watch's readers fail closed. kc_stub stands in for kubectl (si_kubectl and si_kadmin call it too):
# a Forbidden log read, a pod list that fails or is empty, and an unreadable SI pod list each make the reader
# fail with nothing on stdout, so the watch's `|| e="the client logs could not be read"` (or `|| d=...`) aborts;
# readable answers still report what they hold.
kc_stub() { # $1 mode, then kubectl's arguments
  local mode="$1"
  shift
  case " $* " in
    *" -n sentio-network-devnet2 get pods "*)
      case "$mode" in list-fails | si-list-fails) echo 'Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden' >&2; return 1 ;; no-pods) return 0 ;; esac
      case " $* " in *" -o name "*) printf 'pod/%s\n' storage-integrity-si-v2-source-0-0-0 storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source-0-0-0 ;; *) printf '%s\n' sea-g-1 sea-g-2 ;; esac ;;
    *" -n clickhouse get pods "*)
      case "$mode" in list-fails) echo 'Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden' >&2; return 1 ;; no-pods) return 0 ;; esac
      case " $* " in *" -o name "*) echo pod/chi-clickhouse-extra-usage-0-0-0 ;; *) echo sea-g-3 ;; esac ;;
    *" -n kube-system get pods "*) echo pod/cilium-x ;;
    *" -n kube-system exec "*) return 0 ;;
    *" logs "*)
      case "$mode" in
        forbidden) echo 'Error from server (Forbidden): pods "x" is forbidden: User cannot get resource "pods/log"' >&2; return 1 ;;
        errors) case " $* " in *indexer-b-source*) printf '%s\n' 'Coordination::Exception: Session expired (ZSESSIONEXPIRED)' 'Connection loss' 'ok' ;; *) echo ok ;; esac ;;
        *) echo ok ;;
      esac ;;
    *) echo "kc_stub: unexpected kubectl $*" >&2; return 1 ;;
  esac
}
kc_with() { # $1 mode, $2 helper, the rest its arguments: runs the helper in a subshell whose kubectl is kc_stub
  local mode="$1"
  shift
  # shellcheck disable=SC2329 # the helper the subshell runs calls this kubectl
  (kubectl() { kc_stub "$mode" "$@"; }; "$@")
}
for mode in forbidden list-fails no-pods; do
  if out="$(kc_with "$mode" si_keeper_client_errors 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z 2> "$t/kce-$mode.err")"; then echo "si_keeper_client_errors succeeded with $mode: [$out]"; exit 1; fi
  [ -z "$out" ]
  [ -s "$t/kce-$mode.err" ]
  e="$(kc_with "$mode" si_keeper_client_errors 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z 2> /dev/null)" || e="the client logs could not be read"
  [ "$e" = "the client logs could not be read" ]
done
[ -z "$(kc_with clean si_keeper_client_errors 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z)" ]
[ "$(kc_with errors si_keeper_client_errors 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z)" = "sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source-0-0-0 2" ]
for mode in si-list-fails no-pods; do
  if kc_with "$mode" si_cnp_drops 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z > /dev/null 2>&1; then echo "si_cnp_drops succeeded with $mode"; exit 1; fi
done
[ "$(kc_with clean si_cnp_drops 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z)" = "$(printf 'time\tsource\tdestination\tport\treason')" ]
ok "the Keeper watch's readers fail closed: a Forbidden log, a failed or empty pod list abort; clean and erring logs, and an empty Hubble answer, read as they are"

# 9. The owner-rebuild runbook's checks, when its helpers are in the chain.
if declare -F si_rebuild_py > /dev/null; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"level":"info","msg":"rebuilding hg_safe from the arbiter'"'"'s acknowledged inventory","phase":"fence"}' \
    '{"phase":"plan","table_id":"db.t","partition_id":"p_a","publish_seq":7,"parts":2,"from_own_unsafe":1,"from_object_store":1,"missing":[],"root":"0xr"}' \
    '{"phase":"done","dry_run":true,"already_rebuilt":false,"tables":1,"partitions":1,"parts":2,"from_own_unsafe":1,"from_object_store":1,"missing":0}' > "$t/dry.jsonl"
  [ "$(si_rebuild_py check-report "$t/dry.jsonl" dry)" = "dry run: 1 partitions planned, every part covered" ]
  printf '%s\n' '{"phase":"plan","table_id":"db.t","partition_id":"p_a","publish_seq":7,"parts":2,"from_own_unsafe":1,"from_object_store":0,"missing":["all_1_1_0"],"root":"0xr"}' \
    '{"phase":"done","dry_run":true,"already_rebuilt":false,"tables":1,"partitions":1,"parts":2,"from_own_unsafe":1,"from_object_store":0,"missing":1}' > "$t/dry-missing.jsonl"
  if si_rebuild_py check-report "$t/dry-missing.jsonl" dry 2> /dev/null; then echo "a dry run with a missing part passed"; exit 1; fi
  printf 'table\treplica\thost\tactive\ndb__t\tsnode-3\th\tno\ndb__t\tverifier-1\th\tyes\n' > "$t/keeper-before.txt"
  printf '%s\n' '{"phase":"fence","table_id":"db.t","path":"/sentio/0/unsafe/db__t","present":true,"dropped":true}' \
    '{"phase":"restore","table_id":"db.t","partition_id":"p_a","publish_seq":7,"parts":2,"from_own_unsafe":1,"from_object_store":1,"missing":[],"root":"0xr"}' \
    '{"phase":"done","dry_run":false,"already_rebuilt":false,"tables":1,"partitions":1,"parts":2,"from_own_unsafe":1,"from_object_store":1,"missing":0}' > "$t/run.jsonl"
  [ "$(si_rebuild_py check-report "$t/run.jsonl" run "$t/keeper-before.txt")" = "rebuild: 1 fence lines, 1 stale replicas dropped, 1 partitions restored, 1 parts from the own hg_unsafe replica, 1 from the object store" ]
  [ "$(si_rebuild_py report "$t/run.jsonl" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 3 ]
  printf 'db__t\tp_a\th1\t1\ndb__t\tp_a\th2\t2\n' > "$t/parts-a.tsv"; printf 'db__t\tp_a\th2\t2\ndb__t\tp_a\th1\t1\n' > "$t/parts-b.tsv"
  si_rebuild_py parts-diff "$t/parts-a.tsv" "$t/parts-b.tsv" > /dev/null
  printf 'db__t\tp_a\th3\t1\n' > "$t/parts-c.tsv"
  if si_rebuild_py parts-diff "$t/parts-a.tsv" "$t/parts-c.tsv" > /dev/null; then echo "different parts compared equal"; exit 1; fi
  printf '%s\n' '{"table_id":"db.t","partition_id":"p_a","publish_seq":7,"base_partition_root":"0xr","safe_parts":["x","y"],"last_acked_promotion_seq":7,"unacked_promotion_seq":0}' > "$t/ps-a.jsonl"
  [ "$(si_rebuild_py partstates-diff "$t/ps-a.jsonl" "$t/ps-a.jsonl")" = "partition states equal: 1 partitions, none unacknowledged" ]
  printf 'loss\t2026-10-20T00:00:00Z\t1792454400\nlost\t2026-10-20T00:05:00Z\t1792454700\naccepted\t2026-10-20T01:00:00Z\t1792458000\n' > "$t/rto.tsv"
  [ "$(si_rebuild_py rto "$t/rto.tsv" | tail -n 1)" = "P4_REBUILD_RTO=3600" ]
  si_rebuild_py next-run "17 4 * * *" > /dev/null
  printf '%s\n' 'log line' '{"format":"si-backup-index-v1","network_id":"devnet2","owner_indexer_id":2,"name":"20261020T041700Z-incr","kind":"incr","base":"20261019T041700Z-full","chain_length":2,"snapshot_id":"0xs","entry":{"safe_block_seq":10,"applied_promotion_seq":7},"tables":[{"physical_table":"db__t","table_id":"db.t","incarnation_seq":3,"parts":[{"name":"p_a_1_1_0","partition_id":"p_a","phys_hash":"h","rows":1}]}]}' > "$t/backup.log"
  si_rebuild_py backup "$t/backup.log" 2 "$t/backup-name.txt" 10 > /dev/null
  [ "$(cat "$t/backup-name.txt")" = 20261020T041700Z-incr ]
  if si_rebuild_py backup "$t/backup.log" 1 "$t/x.txt" 10 2> /dev/null; then echo "another owner's backup was accepted"; exit 1; fi
  ok "owner-rebuild checks: report filter, dry and run reports, parts, partition states, RTO, schedule, backup index"
fi
echo "selftest passed"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Local direct-Helm rendering only; deployment context/order options are not used."""
import argparse,hashlib,json,os,re,subprocess,tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
class UniqueLoader(yaml.SafeLoader):
    pass
def unique_mapping(loader,node,deep=False):
    result={}
    for key_node,value_node in node.value:
        key=loader.construct_object(key_node,deep=deep)
        if key in result:raise ValueError('duplicate YAML key')
        result[key]=loader.construct_object(value_node,deep=deep)
    return result
UniqueLoader.add_constructor(yaml.resolver.BaseResolver.DEFAULT_MAPPING_TAG,unique_mapping)
FORBIDDEN={'k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse.yaml','k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse-extra.yaml'}
def require(ok):
    if not ok: raise ValueError('unsupported or unsafe local render input; details withheld')
def plain(x):
    if isinstance(x,str):require('{{' not in x and '}}' not in x and '\x00' not in x)
    elif isinstance(x,dict):
        for k,v in x.items():plain(k);plain(v)
    elif isinstance(x,list):
        for v in x:plain(v)
    else:require(x is None or isinstance(x,(int,float,bool)))
def checked(root,parent,value,folder=False):
    require(isinstance(value,str) and not Path(value).is_absolute());plain(value)
    p=(parent/value).resolve(); require(p.is_relative_to(root));require(str(p.relative_to(root)) not in FORBIDDEN)
    require(p.is_dir() if folder else p.is_file());return p
def load(root,file,name):
    root=Path(root).resolve();path=checked(root,root,file)
    raw=path.read_text();plain(raw);doc=yaml.load(raw,Loader=UniqueLoader)
    require(isinstance(doc,dict) and not set(doc)-{'helmDefaults','releases'})
    defaults=doc.get('helmDefaults',{});require(isinstance(defaults,dict) and not set(defaults)-{'kubeContext','createNamespace'})
    require(defaults.get('kubeContext','sentio-sea')=='sentio-sea' and defaults.get('createNamespace',False) is False)
    require(isinstance(doc.get('releases'),list));rows=[r for r in doc['releases'] if isinstance(r,dict) and r.get('name')==name]
    if not rows:return None
    require(len(rows)==1);row=rows[0];require(not set(row)-{'name','namespace','chart','needs','set','values','wait','timeout'})
    require(re.fullmatch('[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*',name) is not None);require(isinstance(row.get('namespace'),str));plain(row)
    require(isinstance(row.get('needs',[]),list) and all(isinstance(s,str) for s in row.get('needs',[])))
    require(isinstance(row.get('wait',False),bool));require(type(row.get('timeout',1)) is int)
    chart=checked(root,path.parent,row['chart'],True)
    require(str(chart.relative_to(root)) in {'charts/storage-integrity','charts/sentio-node'})
    require(isinstance(row.get('values',[]),list) and isinstance(row.get('set',[]),list))
    vals=[]
    for v in row.get('values',[]):
        if isinstance(v,str):vals.append(('file',checked(root,path.parent,v)))
        else:
            require(isinstance(v,dict) and set(v)=={'nodeSelector'} and isinstance(v['nodeSelector'],dict))
            require(all(isinstance(k,str) and isinstance(s,str) for k,s in v['nodeSelector'].items())); vals.append(('inline',v))
    sets=[]
    for v in row.get('set',[]):
        require(isinstance(v,dict) and set(v)=={'name','file'} and v['name']=='service.chainsConfig')
        sets.append((v['name'],checked(root,path.parent,v['file'])))
    require(len(sets)<=1)
    return root,path,row,chart,vals,sets

def render(tree,file,release,output):
    data=load(tree,file,release)
    if data is None:raise LookupError('selected release absent')
    root,path,row,chart,vals,sets=data
    out=Path(output);out.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='direct-helm-inline-') as td:
        args=['helm','template',release,str(chart),'--namespace',row['namespace']]
        for i,(kind,value) in enumerate(vals):
            if kind=='inline':
                value_path=Path(td)/f'inline-{i}.yaml';value_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(value));value_path.chmod(0o600)
            else:value_path=value
            args+=['-f',str(value_path)]
        for name,p in sets:args+=['--set-file',name+'='+str(p)]
        run=subprocess.run(args,cwd=path.parent,capture_output=True,timeout=120)
        require(run.returncode==0 and bool(run.stdout.strip()))
        objects=list(yaml.safe_load_all(run.stdout));require(objects and all(isinstance(x,dict) and x.get('apiVersion') and x.get('kind') and isinstance(x.get('metadata'),dict) and x['metadata'].get('name') for x in objects))
        keys=[(x['apiVersion'],x['kind'],x['metadata'].get('namespace',''),x['metadata']['name']) for x in objects];require(len(keys)==len(set(keys)))
        out.write_bytes(run.stdout);out.chmod(0o600)
        meta={'release':release,'namespace':row['namespace'],'helmfile':file,'chart':str(chart.relative_to(root)),'ordered_values':[str(v.relative_to(root)) if k=='file' else {'inline_keys':sorted(v)} for k,v in vals], 'set_file_names':[k for k,v in sets], 'ignored_operational_fields':sorted(set(row)&{'needs','wait','timeout'}),'ignored_defaults':sorted(load_defaults(path)), 'sha256':hashlib.sha256(run.stdout).hexdigest(),'objects':len(keys),'object_keys_sha256':hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(sorted(keys)).encode()).hexdigest()}
        out.with_suffix(out.suffix+'.meta.json').write_text(json.dumps(meta,indent=2)+'\n')
        return meta

def load_defaults(path):return yaml.load(path.read_text(),Loader=UniqueLoader).get('helmDefaults',{})

def compare(base_tree,head_tree,entries,new_releases,output_dir):
    """Compare exact bytes and resource identities; permit only genuinely new named releases."""
    names=[n for f,n in entries];require(len(names)==len(set(names)))
    require(len(new_releases)==len(set(new_releases)) and set(new_releases)<=set(names))
    results=[]
    for file,name in entries:
        require(load(head_tree,file,name)is not None)
        head=render(head_tree,file,name,Path(output_dir)/('head-'+name+'.yaml'))
        absent=load(base_tree,file,name)is None
        if absent:
            require(name in new_releases);results.append({'release':name,'status':'new','head':head});continue
        require(name not in new_releases)
        base=render(base_tree,file,name,Path(output_dir)/('base-'+name+'.yaml'))
        require(base['sha256']==head['sha256'] and base['object_keys_sha256']==head['object_keys_sha256'])
        results.append({'release':name,'status':'identical','base':base,'head':head})
    return results

ENTRIES=[
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml","storage-integrity-si-v2"),
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml","sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a"),
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml","sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b"),
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/helmfile.yaml","sentio-node-devnet2-observer"),
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-testnet-v2/helmfile.yaml","sentio-node-testnet-v2-indexer-a"),
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-testnet-v2/helmfile.yaml","sentio-node-testnet-v2-indexer-b"),
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-testnet-v2/helmfile.yaml","sentio-node-observer"),
 ("k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml","sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c"),
]
def export_base(tree,ref,destination):
    import tarfile
    tree=Path(tree).resolve()
    # Ref and filename metadata are validated before archive reads any content.
    require(isinstance(ref,str) and bool(ref) and not ref.startswith("-") and "\x00" not in ref)
    sha=subprocess.check_output(["git","-C",str(tree),"rev-parse","--verify",ref+"^{commit}"],text=True).strip()
    require(re.fullmatch("[0-9a-f]{40}",sha)is not None)
    names=subprocess.check_output(["git","-C",str(tree),"ls-tree","-rz","--name-only",sha],text=True).split("\x00")
    # The two credential-bearing files are excluded at the archive argument layer.
    args=["git","-C",str(tree),"archive",sha,"--",".",*[(":(exclude)"+n) for n in sorted(FORBIDDEN)]]
    process=subprocess.Popen(args,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    try:
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=process.stdout,mode="r|") as archive:
            for member in archive:
                require(member.name not in FORBIDDEN)
                p=(Path(destination)/member.name).resolve();require(p.is_relative_to(Path(destination).resolve()))
                # Deployment inputs must be regular files; never follow source symlinks.
                if member.isdir() or member.isfile():archive.extract(member,destination)
                else:require(member.issym())
        require(process.wait(timeout=30)==0)
    except Exception:
        process.kill();process.wait();raise
    require(all(not(Path(destination)/n).exists() for n in FORBIDDEN))
    return sha

def main():
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser();parser.add_argument("action",choices=["compare","diff"])
    parser.add_argument("--tree",required=True);parser.add_argument("--base-ref",required=True);parser.add_argument("--release")
    args=parser.parse_args()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="si-p3-direct-render-") as td:
        base=Path(td)/"base";base.mkdir();export_base(args.tree,args.base_ref,base)
        out=Path(td)/"renders"
        if args.action=="compare":
            require(args.release is None)
            results=compare(base,args.tree,ENTRIES,[],out)
            for result in results:print(result["release"]+" identical")
        else:
            entries=[(file,name)for file,name in ENTRIES if name==args.release];require(len(entries)==1)
            file,name=entries[0];a=out/"base.yaml";b=out/"head.yaml"
            render(base,file,name,a);render(args.tree,file,name,b)
            def objects(p):
                return {(x["kind"],x["metadata"]["name"]):x for x in yaml.safe_load_all(p.read_text())}
            before,after=objects(a),objects(b)
            for key in sorted(set(before)|set(after)):
                if before.get(key)!=after.get(key):print("changed "+"/".join(key))
if __name__=="__main__":
    try:main()
    except Exception:raise SystemExit("direct-render: unsupported grammar, missing input or local render failure; details withheld; stop")

head=sys.argv[1]
if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}",head)is None:sys.exit("invalid checked PR head; stop")
pages=json.load(sys.stdin)
if not isinstance(pages,list)or not pages or any(not isinstance(p,list)or not p or len(p)>100 for p in pages):sys.exit("missing or malformed paginated PR commits; stop")
commits=[c for p in pages for c in p]
if len(commits)>=250:sys.exit("REST commit listing reached its limit; stop")
trailer="Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>";seen=set()
for c in commits:
 if not isinstance(c,dict)or not isinstance(c.get("sha"),str)or re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}",c["sha"])is None or c["sha"]in seen:sys.exit("malformed or duplicate PR commit; stop")
 seen.add(c["sha"]);a=c["commit"]["author"];message=c["commit"]["message"]
 if not isinstance(message,str)or(a["name"],a["email"])!=("poetry","chen@sentio.xyz"):sys.exit("unexpected primary author; stop")
 coauthors=re.findall(r"(?im)^[ \t]*co-authored-by[ \t]*:.*$",message)
 parsed=subprocess.run(["git","interpret-trailers","--parse"],input=message,text=True,check=True,capture_output=True).stdout.splitlines()
 if coauthors not in ([],[trailer])or parsed.count(trailer)!=len(coauthors):sys.exit("unexpected or duplicated coauthor trailer; stop")
if commits[-1]["sha"]!=head:sys.exit("REST listing head differs from the checked head; stop")
print("PR commit identities and pinned head verified")
```

## Task 55: devnet2 — P4 network hardening (live): census, staging proof, interserver steps 1 and 2 with node pins, SI policies, Keeper allowlist, failure domains, exit probe (S3-D)

Spec §14 "Network hardening (P4, before k is raised)", §16 row P4 ("hardening probed from every pod"), §9.3 "Failure independence" and §18, as clarified by K55 (failure domains; decision D39), K56 (interserver step 1's order) and K57 (ingress-only policies, census, probes) and bound by contract §36–§37: devnet2-si-v2's interserver HTTP gets credentials in two rolling steps, its six SI ClickHouses are pinned to the nodes their volumes hold (sources pairwise distinct, no verifier ClickHouse on a source's node), each SI installation gets an ingress-only Cilium policy and the shared `clickhouse-keeper-extra` ensemble an ingress allowlist, each enforced only after a 7-day census and probes from every pod, and the failure domains are recorded for Plans S3-E4 and S3-F. The task executes `docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p4-hardening.md` (Task 54, merged in `P4_PR`) section by section and block by block, in contract §37.4's order with one refinement (Notes): preparation → census (7 days) → interserver secret (the user's action, before the staging pair that names it) → staging proof → §5.0 verifier moves (only for a `MOVE` line of the census placement) → step 1 with the node pins (indexer-b, indexer-c, network) → step 2 in the same order → SI policies observe → probes → enforce (indexer-b, indexer-c, network) → Keeper allowlist observe → probes → the Keeper enforce PR, its merge and its apply with the abort watch → failure domains → exit probe → end. The runbook is the source of truth for every check, helper, evidence name and expected output (decision D19); this task adds the exact content of every single-service commit and of the Keeper PR (made by its own tools, Step 1), the gates, its own read-only checks, the user's terminal blocks, and the ledger: it records `INTERSERVER_STEP1_END`, `INTERSERVER_STEP2_END`, `DEVNET2_FAILURE_DOMAINS` and `HARDENING_END` with the run record `hardening run` in Appendix C (contract §37.3).

No step updates governance or consensus parameters or takes an issuance hold. The stated table-set transition and acceptance promotions still occur; this is not a claim that they create no Raft entries. Every change has its documented way back (runbook §12): an interserver step and its node pins revert through `si_p4_roll` with a revert commit (§12.1), a policy goes back to observe at once and its enforce commit is reverted (§12.3), the Keeper allowlist goes back to observe live and through a revert PR (§12.4). Irreversible, and named in each gate: the acceptance rows (values `4201`–`4204`, `429<n>` per move and `428<k>` per revert window, in `devnet101.swap_new2`; rows `4201`–`4207` and `429<n>` in indexer-b's `devuser1.s3_p4`, created in Step 4 and dropped by Task 56, and in indexer-c's acceptance table `<db>.s3e_e2e`, which the indexer-c runbook made) and their promotions, and the one table-set transition of `devuser1.s3_p4`'s `CREATE TABLE`; the staging pair's throwaway data (its volumes and Keeper root, deleted in runbook §3.4); only if a §5.0 move runs, the moved verifier ClickHouse's old volume (the protocol tables its verifier creates again and its `hg_unsafe` replicas, which clone again from the sources; the PV stays `Retain`ed and `Released` for the user); and the ephemeral probe containers, which stay terminated in each probed pod's spec, the production `clickhouse-extra` and `clickhouse-keeper-extra` pods included, until that pod is next recreated (Kubernetes cannot remove one).
